Its long development period meant it missed the timing needed to gain momentum for widespread adoption, but it was an ambitious attempt to push forward advanced language features.

name: Dart
problem: 大規模Webアプリ開発におけるJavaScriptの構造化・ツール支援の弱さを、クラスベースの型付き言語で解決したかった。
summary: 当初はWeb向けだったが、Flutterフレームワークで再び脚光を浴びた。
problem_en: In the early 2010s, Google believed that in its large-scale internal web application development, JavaScript's dynamic typing and weak structuring were undermining codebase maintainability. Lars Bak and others, who had experience developing virtual machines, set out to create a language with class-based object orientation and a type system, one that could also receive advanced tooling support from IDEs, aiming to offer an alternative to JavaScript with an eye, initially, toward embedding a dedicated VM in the browser.
summary_en: The direct adoption in browsers it originally aimed for never materialized, but the language is now "active," having returned to the spotlight as the core language of Google's Flutter framework for mobile and desktop app development. It is an example of a language that survived by changing its role, from a web-oriented origin to a cross-platform UI development language.

name: VBScript
problem: Internet Explorer上でVisual Basicの文法に慣れた開発者が手軽にWebページを動的にできるようにしたかった。
summary: Windowsの自動化スクリプトとしても使われたが、セキュリティ懸念で衰退。
problem_en: In the mid-1990s, as Netscape's JavaScript began bringing dynamic behavior to web pages, Microsoft was also pressed to equip its Internet Explorer with similar scripting capability. However, Microsoft already had a huge community of developers, both internal and external, working with Visual Basic. Rather than having them learn a new syntax from scratch, it was more rational to let them use the familiar BASIC-family syntax directly in the browser. VBScript was thus created by rebuilding Visual Basic's language assets as a lightweight interpreted language, intended for automating web pages and Windows administrative tasks.
summary_en: With the end of Internet Explorer and security concerns (its abuse as a vector for malware), Microsoft itself deprecated it, and it is no longer used in new development — a "legacy" language. It survives only as a legacy in some old Windows business systems and automation scripts.

name: Visual Basic(Classic)
problem: WindowsのGUIフォームをドラッグ&ドロップで組み立てながら、BASICの手軽さでアプリを開発したかった。1988年に作られたGUIデザイナー「Ruby」と、開発中止になったデータベース製品Omega向けの組み込みBASICエンジン「EB」を組み合わせる形で1991年に誕生した。
summary: RAD(高速アプリ開発)の代名詞として1990年代に爆発的に普及。
problem_en: In the late 1980s, developing Windows applications required programmers to work directly in C and the Windows API to hand-craft windows and buttons, which set an extremely high bar for programmers without specialized expertise. Alan Cooper had developed a tool called "Tripod" that let developers assemble GUIs simply by placing form components on the screen, and Microsoft sought to combine this with a BASIC language interpreter to realize an environment where anyone could build Windows applications by dragging and dropping. The resulting Visual Basic fused the ease of BASIC with the rapid application development (RAD) made possible by a form designer.
summary_en: Microsoft ended support in 2008 and encouraged migration to the .NET-based VB.NET. It is now a "legacy" language not used for new development, but its historical significance in supporting Windows application development in the 1990s is substantial, and it still remains as a target for maintaining older business systems.

name: ActionScript
problem: Flashアニメーション上にインタラクティブな挙動やゲームロジックをプログラム可能にしたかった。
summary: Flashコンテンツ全盛期を支えたが、Flash終息とともに使われなくなった。
problem_en: In the late 1990s, Macromedia's Flash had become popular as a vector animation tool, but it initially offered only simple timeline playback control and could not create games or interactive advertisements that responded to user actions. On the web, JavaScript was already achieving dynamic behavior, and Macromedia likewise needed to build a programmable mechanism into Flash. Building on the syntax and concepts of the then-spreading JavaScript, ActionScript was designed as a scripting language that could manipulate Flash movie clips and buttons.
summary_en: With the end of support for Flash Player itself in 2020 by Adobe (which had acquired Macromedia), ActionScript has become, in effect, a "historical" language that is no longer used. HTML5/CSS- and JavaScript-based technologies have taken over the roles that Flash content used to play.

name: SNOBOL
problem: 文字列の複雑なパターンマッチングと書き換えを、当時のFortranやアセンブリより自然に記述したかった。
summary: 文字列パターンマッチングの先駆的言語。Icon・AWK等に影響。
problem_en: In the early 1960s, text processing was mainly done in Fortran or assembly, but these languages lacked any facility for structurally pattern-matching and rewriting strings, making them ill-suited to purposes such as symbolic processing, natural language analysis, and compiler parsing. Ralph Griswold and others at Bell Labs aimed to build a language that could describe text processing more naturally than any language of its time, by embedding the operation of searching for a pattern within a string and replacing the matched portion as a core feature of the language itself. The resulting SNOBOL established a pioneering design that treated patterns as a first-class data type.
summary_en: It is a "historical" language that has vanished from among today's mainstream languages, but it is valued as a pioneer that passed on the concept of string pattern matching to many later text-processing languages.

name: Icon
problem: SNOBOL4のパターンマッチング能力を保ちながら、より一般的で読みやすい構文の汎用言語にしたかった。
summary: ゴールディレクテッド評価という独自の制御機構を持つ文字列処理言語。
problem_en: SNOBOL4 had excellent expressive power for pattern matching, but its distinctive syntax and limited data structures made it hard to read as a general-purpose programming language and unsuited to writing large-scale programs. Ralph Griswold, the creator of SNOBOL himself, reflected on these shortcomings and designed a successor language that adopted ALGOL-style readable block structure and control constructs while retaining the strength of pattern matching. The goal was a language that could handle both text processing and general application development.
summary_en: Icon remains a "niche" language, still used today by some enthusiasts and in text-processing and language-processing research, and the direct successor of Icon itself has been carried forward into Unicon (a Unicode and object-oriented extension of Icon).

name: sed
problem: エディタedのコマンド列を対話操作なしにファイル全体へ一括適用し、非対話的なテキスト変換を自動化したかった。
summary: ストリームエディタ。パイプライン処理でのテキスト置換に今も使われる。
problem_en: The line editor `ed` was a familiar tool for early Unix developers, but repeatedly typing the same interactive editing commands across multiple files or large numbers of lines was inefficient. Lee E. McMahon set out to create a "stream editor" that carried over `ed`'s command set but could be run as a script in a single batch, without any interaction with the user, aiming to automate mechanical text transformation across whole files as a batch process.
summary_en: Nearly half a century later, sed remains an "active" language, still built into pipeline processing as a standard tool on Unix-like operating systems, and it remains in active use as a staple of text transformation in shell scripts.

name: REBOL
problem: ネットワーク越しにデータと振る舞いを一体化した「メッセージ」として自然にやり取りできる軽量言語が欲しかった。
summary: データとコードを同一視するホモイコニックな軽量言語。
problem_en: As the Internet was rapidly spreading, Carl Sassenrath, who had experience designing the Amiga operating system kernel, felt the need for a lightweight mechanism that could exchange data and code (behavior) between different systems over a network without distinction. In existing languages, data formats and program syntax were separate, requiring redundant conversion for distributed processing across a network. He therefore combined Lisp's homoiconic nature (in which code and data share the same representation) with Forth's simple evaluation model to design REBOL, a language that could represent and transmit code and data together as a single "message."
summary_en: Its adoption remained limited due to the failure of commercialization and delayed open-sourcing, and it is now positioned as a "historical" language. Its design philosophy has been carried forward into its successor language, Red.

name: Red
problem: REBOLの簡潔さを受け継ぎつつ、REBOLにはなかったネイティブコンパイルとシステムプログラミング能力を持たせたかった。
summary: REBOLの後継として、スクリプトからシステム記述までを一つの言語で狙う。
problem_en: REBOL drew attention for its concise design that unified code and data, but its execution speed was slow and it was unsuited to systems programming or native compilation, so developers were ultimately forced to fall back on C or C++ for lower-level tasks. Nenad Rakocevic, a member of the REBOL community, designed Red to preserve REBOL's expressiveness and ease of use while aiming for a "full stack" language capable of handling everything from scripting to OS-level systems description within a single language.
summary_en: Red is a "niche" language whose development continues today within a small community of developers, positioned as an attempt to extend REBOL's philosophy into the field of systems programming.

name: Factor
problem: Forthのスタックベース計算モデルに、モダンな高階関数とオブジェクト指向を組み合わせて実用言語にしたかった。
summary: Forth系の連結(concatenative)プログラミングを現代化した言語。
problem_en: Forth's stack-based computational model runs extremely fast and with a small memory footprint, but it lacks abstraction mechanisms, modern data structures, and object-oriented facilities, leaving it with insufficient expressive power for developing large, complex software. Slava Pestov sought to revive stack-based languages as modern practical languages by preserving the concatenative programming style inherited from Forth while combining it with higher-order functions, closures, and a dynamically typed object system.
summary_en: Factor remains a "niche" language used mainly by research and enthusiast communities, positioned as an experimental demonstration of the concatenative programming paradigm in a modern form.

name: AppleScript
problem: プログラマでない一般ユーザーが、英語の文章に近い記述でMac上の複数アプリを自動操作・連携させたかった。
summary: 自然言語に近い構文でMacアプリ間の操作を自動化する言語。
problem_en: In the early 1990s, Macintosh was gaining a mechanism for "inter-application communication" that let multiple applications work together, but making use of it required specialized programming knowledge. Apple wanted to let ordinary users and power users who were not programmers build automation workflows spanning multiple applications — tasks commonly done in daily work, such as "open this file with this app, do that operation, then save it" — using a description close to natural English sentences. This led to the development of AppleScript, a scripting language with a natural-language-like syntax that makes heavy use of verbs and prepositions.
summary_en: It is still bundled with macOS today and continues to be used for automating apps on the Mac, making it a "niche" language. In recent years it has increasingly been used alongside the more general-purpose JavaScript for Automation (JXA), but it retains its position as the representative language of macOS automation.

name: Java
problem: 家電組込み機器向けに設計していた「どのCPU上でも同じバイナリが動く」言語を、台頭するWebの世界で安全に配布できるようにしたかった。
summary: 「Write Once, Run Anywhere」を掲げ企業システムの標準となった言語。
problem_en: Java originated in an in-house effort called the "Green Project," conceived as a language for controlling home appliances and embedded devices, where the same binary would run on any CPU architecture (its original name was Oak). However, the interactive television market it targeted never took off, and the development team redirected the technology toward the rapidly growing World Wide Web instead. Distributing native applications written in C or C++ to an unspecified number of browser environments carried risks of crashes and security vulnerabilities and was not realistic, so a safe, portable language that ran on a virtual machine was needed.
summary_en: Java remains one of the de facto standard languages for enterprise system development today, and it is widely in active use for Android app development and enterprise backend systems. The JVM execution platform continues to serve as the foundation for numerous later languages (Kotlin, Scala, Clojure, and others), and the language itself continues to expand its features through regular version updates.

name: Kotlin
problem: Javaとの完全な相互運用性を保ちながら、null安全や簡潔な構文でJavaの冗長さと実行時エラーを減らしたかった。
summary: Googleが公式Android開発言語に採用しJavaを置き換えつつある言語。
problem_en: The IDE company JetBrains had long developed its own product (IntelliJ IDEA) in Java, and was routinely troubled by Java's verbose syntax and the null pointer exceptions (NullPointerException) that frequently occurred at runtime. Scala, an existing JVM language, offered high expressiveness but suffered from slow compilation and a steep learning curve, so there was a need for a practical language that could fully interoperate with existing Java codebases while offering simpler and safer syntax. Adoption grew rapidly after Google designated it an official language for Android development in 2017.
summary_en: Kotlin has now established itself as Google's official Android development language and is an actively used language that is displacing Java. It has also broadened its scope into server-side development (with frameworks such as Ktor) and multiplatform development (Kotlin Multiplatform), becoming one of the central languages of the JVM ecosystem. JetBrains itself continues to use it as the development language for its own IDE products, and adoption within enterprises has been increasing year by year.

name: Scala
problem: オブジェクト指向と関数型プログラミングを対立させず、JVM上で一つの統一された言語として融合したかった。
summary: OOPとFPを融合したJVM言語。ビッグデータ基盤Sparkの実装言語。
problem_en: Martin Odersky was a researcher who had also been involved in developing javac (the official Java compiler), and he believed there was no fundamental contradiction between object-oriented programming and functional programming, two paradigms that were at the time treated as almost entirely separate camps. Since the existing Java language leaned heavily toward object orientation, and purely functional languages like Haskell had not seen much adoption in practice, Scala was designed as an attempt to fuse the two into a single unified language on the JVM, achieving both academic rigor and practical usability in industry.
summary_en: Scala remains an actively developed, current language, and it is firmly used in the field of data engineering, particularly owing to its position as the implementation language of the big-data processing platform Apache Spark. As the pioneer that brought functional programming in earnest into the JVM world, it continues to exert an ideological influence on the design of subsequent JVM languages. In recent years, migration to Scala 3, which has simplified the language specification, has been underway.

name: Ceylon
problem: Javaのジェネリクスの型消去やnull安全性の欠如といった設計上の弱点を、大規模モジュールシステムとともに刷新したかった。
summary: Javaの弱点克服を狙ったが普及に至らず開発終了した言語。
problem_en: Ceylon's designer Gavin King was also known as the author of Hibernate, a prominent Java EE framework, and through his day-to-day development work he keenly felt Java's design weaknesses. In particular, "type erasure" — where generics exist only at compile time and their type information is erased at runtime — and the lack of null safety, which led to frequent runtime exceptions, made maintaining large codebases difficult. Ceylon was developed to fundamentally overhaul these weaknesses while also aiming to be a next-generation Java alternative equipped with a large-scale module system.
summary_en: Ceylon had a technically ambitious design, but it did not achieve widespread adoption, partly due to the rise of competing JVM languages such as Kotlin, and development by Red Hat ended around 2020, leaving it treated as a historical language. It is sometimes referenced in the history of language design as an example that pioneered pointing out and attempting to solve Java's weaknesses. Although the project itself has ended, parts of its design philosophy have left an influence on discussions within other JVM language communities.

name: VB.NET
problem: Visual Basic Classicのユーザー資産を保ちながら、.NET基盤の共通言語ランタイム上で完全なオブジェクト指向言語として作り直したかった。
summary: .NET上のVisual Basic後継。C#と共通ランタイムを共有する。
problem_en: Throughout the 1990s, Visual Basic (Classic) became synonymous with RAD (rapid application development) and spread explosively, but its internal design depended on COM technology, which was fundamentally incompatible with the .NET vision (a foundation for running multiple languages uniformly on a common language runtime) that Microsoft put forward in the early 2000s. VB.NET was rebuilt from scratch as a fully object-oriented language that could preserve the vast existing base of Visual Basic assets and programmer knowledge while still gaining the benefits of the .NET foundation (garbage collection, interoperability with languages such as C#, and so on).
summary_en: VB.NET remains actively used today as part of the .NET ecosystem, retaining solid support particularly for maintaining existing business applications and among developers who prefer its concise syntax. While it lacks the momentum of new feature additions that C# has, it continues to be supported by Microsoft and its operation is guaranteed on the latest versions of .NET.

name: PowerShell
problem: Windows管理業務で、文字列だけをパイプで受け渡すUnixシェルの限界を超え、.NETオブジェクトそのものをパイプで扱いたかった。
summary: オブジェクトをパイプでやり取りするWindows標準の管理シェル。
problem_en: Windows administrators had long been forced to perform large-scale system administration using a command prompt and batch files that were far weaker than the shells of Unix-like OSes (such as bash). Unix shell pipelines pass only strings (text) between commands, requiring fragile text processing to parse the output. Designer Jeffrey Snover sought to eliminate this cumbersome string parsing at its root by creating a management shell built on the .NET foundation, one that could pass actual objects through pipes.
summary_en: PowerShell is now widely used as the standard Windows management shell and automation tool, and later became open source and cross-platform as PowerShell Core, running on macOS and Linux as well. It has also become an indispensable tool for automating the management of cloud infrastructure (Azure), and occupies an important position in the DevOps field.

name: Processing
problem: デザイナーやアーティストがビジュアル表現をJavaの煩雑さなしに素早く試作したかった。
summary: クリエイティブコーディング教育・アート制作の定番言語/環境。
problem_en: Casey Reas and Ben Fry, both from the MIT Media Lab, noticed that when designers and visual artists tried to prototype expressions using computer graphics, the boilerplate code needed for full-fledged Java class definitions and GUI setup was a major barrier. Even for creators without formal programming training, there was a need for an environment where they could immediately draw shapes and animations on screen and iterate through trial and error by writing just a few lines of code. Rather than using Java as-is, Processing addressed this by layering a simplified grammar and a sketch-oriented development environment on top of it.
summary_en: Processing remains in active use today as a staple language and development environment in creative coding education and art production. It has been adopted at art and design education institutions around the world as an entry point through which programming beginners and designers engage with code through visual expression, and community-driven development continues.

name: Erlang
problem: 電話交換機のソフトウェアに求められる、無停止で自己修復し大量の同時通信を捌ける超高可用性システムを作りたかった。
summary: アクターモデルによる耐障害・高並行性を実証した通信業界発の言語。
problem_en: In the 1980s, Ericsson was developing software for telephone switches that had to handle millions of simultaneous calls while ensuring that a crash in one process would not affect any other, keeping the entire system running for years without stopping—an extremely demanding requirement. The procedural languages of the time made it difficult to design systems that combined massive concurrency with self-healing from failures, so Joe Armstrong and others built a new language on top of the logic language Prolog, adopting an "actor model" in which lightweight processes communicate only through message passing. The result made it possible to build highly available systems based on the philosophy of "let it crash"—giving up on a failed part and simply restarting it.
summary_en: Erlang continues to run behind the scenes of communications infrastructure and messaging systems (such as WhatsApp), and is highly regarded as a language that has proven fault tolerance and high concurrency. Direct adoption remains niche, but its design philosophy has been carried on by the family of BEAM languages led by Elixir, and it continues to develop actively today.

name: Elixir
problem: Erlang VM(BEAM)の堅牢な並行処理性能を保ちながら、モダンなツールとRuby的に書きやすい構文で開発したかった。
summary: Erlang VM上で動く、書きやすさを重視したモダンな関数型言語。
problem_en: José Valim, who worked on the Ruby on Rails core team, was frustrated by the limits of Ruby's concurrency performance (the difficulty of using multiple cores due to things like the global interpreter lock). Meanwhile, the Erlang VM (BEAM) offered high concurrency and fault tolerance proven in telephone switching systems, but its syntax was unfamiliar to programmers used to dynamic languages like Ruby, and it lacked macro-based metaprogramming and modern development tooling. So Valim designed Elixir as a new language that combined BEAM's robust concurrency foundation with Ruby-like, readable syntax and a powerful macro system.
summary_en: Elixir is increasingly adopted for web services and real-time communication systems that demand fault tolerance and high concurrency, and it continues to be actively developed as a language that carries Erlang's reliability forward in a more approachable, modern form.

name: Pony
problem: アクターモデルの並行性を保ちながら、コンパイル時にデータ競合を型システムで完全に排除したかった。
summary: 型システムでデータ競合を静的に防ぐことを目指すアクターモデル言語。
problem_en: The actor model, as represented by Erlang, achieves high concurrency through message passing, but the risk of data races still remains if actors share mutable data. Rust, meanwhile, achieved memory safety and prevention of data races through compile-time ownership checking, but its design philosophy differed from the flexible concurrency model of the actor approach. Sylvan Clebsch designed Pony to combine both the concurrency of the actor model and Rust-like static verification, aiming for a language that could eliminate data races and exceptions entirely through its compile-time type system alone, without relying on runtime locks or exceptions.
summary_en: Pony has an advanced type system that draws academic attention, but its user base remains limited and niche. As an experimental language demonstrating the ambitious goal of statically eliminating data races, it has offered one option in the design of concurrent-processing languages.

name: occam
problem: トランスピュータという並列処理チップの能力を最大限引き出すため、通信逐次プロセス(CSP)理論をそのまま言語化したかった。
summary: CSP理論を直接実装した並行処理専用言語。Go等に理論的影響。
problem_en: In the early 1980s, the British semiconductor company INMOS was developing a microprocessor called the "transputer," designed to be connected in multiples to perform parallel computation. However, the mainstream languages of the time generally assumed sequential execution and were inadequate for drawing out the transputer's inherent parallel processing power. David May took the theory of Communicating Sequential Processes (CSP), proposed by Tony Hoare, and translated it almost directly into a language specification, designing "occam," in which independent processes communicate synchronously via channels, enabling parallel programming directly tied to the transputer's hardware structure.
summary_en: occam itself became a historical language as the transputer declined commercially, but as an early example of implementing CSP theory as an actual language, it occupies an important place in the history of concurrent programming languages.

name: Swift
problem: Objective-Cの古いC由来の構文やポインタの危険性を捨て、安全性と実行速度を両立するiOS/macOS向け言語が欲しかった。
summary: Appleプラットフォームの標準言語としてObjective-Cを置き換えた。
problem_en: Objective-C, which had long supported Apple's iOS/macOS development, carried old C-derived syntax and bugs stemming from manual pointer manipulation and nil references. In addition, its distinctive grammar, which mixed C with Smalltalk-style messaging syntax, was costly for beginners to learn. Chris Lattner, also a developer of the LLVM compiler infrastructure, designed a new language, Swift, that maintained interoperability with Objective-C while combining modern type safety, safe nil handling via optional types, and fast execution speed, making it Apple's next-generation standard language across its platforms.
summary_en: Swift has now completely replaced Objective-C as the standard development language across all Apple platforms, including iOS, macOS, and watchOS, and open-sourcing has advanced its expansion into other fields such as server-side development.

name: Crystal
problem: Rubyのような書き心地の良い構文のまま、コンパイルによってCネイティブ並みの実行速度を得たかった。
summary: Ruby風の構文を持つコンパイル型・静的型言語。
problem_en: Ruby was beloved by programmers for its readable, easy-to-write syntax, but being a dynamically typed interpreted language, its execution speed lagged far behind compiled languages like C. Ary Borenszweig and others developed Crystal to preserve Ruby-like natural, concise syntax as much as possible, while using static typing and type inference to catch many errors at compile time, and ultimately compiling to native code to achieve execution speed comparable to C.
summary_en: Crystal is a niche language with a clear concept—"write like Ruby, run like C"—and is supported by a community of developers who prioritize performance, though it has not achieved mainstream adoption.

name: Gleam
problem: Erlang VM上でRustのような静的型付けとわかりやすいエラーメッセージを得たかった。
summary: BEAM VM上で動く、型安全性を重視した新興関数型言語。
problem_en: The Erlang VM (BEAM) had long offered high concurrency and fault tolerance through the actor model, but both Erlang itself and Elixir were dynamically typed, meaning that in large codebases, type-related bugs could not be caught before execution. Louis Pilfold wanted to bring Rust-like static typing and clear compiler error messages to BEAM, and developed Gleam, a functional language with robust type inference, so that developers could ensure type safety while still benefiting from BEAM's concurrency infrastructure.
summary_en: Gleam is an emerging language that has drawn attention in recent years for bringing static typing to the BEAM ecosystem, and it is gradually gaining adoption among developer communities that want type safety while still leveraging the assets of Erlang and Elixir.

name: MATLAB
problem: 学生が線形代数の数値計算ライブラリ(LINPACK等)をFortranでコンパイルせず対話的に使えるようにしたかった。
summary: 行列演算を核とした技術計算・シミュレーション向け商用環境。
problem_en: In the 1970s, in university numerical analysis courses, students had to compile and link Fortran code just to use matrix computation libraries such as LINPACK and EISPACK, which got in the way before they could even get to the essence of learning matrix operations. Cleve Moler, then a faculty member at the University of New Mexico, wanted to create an environment where students could try out matrix operations interactively, simply by typing commands, without having to think about compiling. Thus was born MATLAB, short for "Matrix Laboratory," designed as an interactive environment for handling linear algebra with the ease of a calculator. It was later commercialized and grew into a standard environment for technical computing in general, including control engineering and signal processing.
summary_en: It remains an active language today (status: active), and continues to be widely used in university education and in engineering and finance practice as a commercial environment for technical computing and simulation centered on matrix operations. Even as open-source alternatives (such as Julia and Python+NumPy) rise, it retains solid demand thanks to its accumulated technical assets and rich toolboxes.

name: R
problem: 商用の統計言語Sに代わる、統計解析とグラフ作成のための無料でオープンな環境が欲しかった。
summary: 統計解析・データ可視化分野で研究者に広く使われるオープンソース言語。
problem_en: In the 1990s, the commercial language S from Bell Labs was the de facto standard in the field of statistical analysis, but its high licensing costs were a barrier for students and researchers. Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman of the University of Auckland in New Zealand wanted to create an open-source statistical analysis environment that anyone could use for free while following S's syntax and functionality. Building on a lightweight implementation inspired by the design of Scheme interpreters, they developed a language specialized for statistical analysis and graphics. The name "R" both reflects the initials of the two designers' first names and pays homage to S.
summary_en: R remains an actively used language today (status: active), firmly established as an open-source language widely used by researchers and data scientists in statistical analysis and data visualization. It enjoys particularly strong support in fields such as reproducible analysis for academic papers and bioinformatics.

name: Julia
problem: Pythonのような書きやすさとCのような実行速度を、動的言語のまま両立させたかった(いわゆる「2言語問題」の解消)。
summary: 科学技術計算向けに速度と書きやすさの両立を狙った新興言語。
problem_en: In the field of scientific and technical computing, the so-called "two-language problem" had long been a persistent headache: it had become standard practice to prototype in an easy-to-write language like Python and then rewrite only the performance-critical parts in C or Fortran. Researchers at MIT wanted to eliminate this compromise and create a language that kept the ease of writing dynamically typed code while approaching C-level execution speed through JIT (just-in-time) compilation. It was designed with the goal of combining the usability of existing scientific computing languages (such as MATLAB) with performance comparable to statically typed languages.
summary_en: Julia remains an actively used language (status: active), gaining adoption in numerical simulation and machine learning as an emerging language that aims to combine speed with ease of writing. Positioned as a solution to the "two-language problem," it has been steadily growing its user base, particularly within the research community.

name: J
problem: APLの特殊記号入力の問題を解消し、標準ASCIIキーボードだけで配列プログラミングを書けるようにしたかった。
summary: APLをASCII文字だけで表現し直した後継配列言語。
problem_en: APL's notation was mathematically powerful, but it had the practical drawback of requiring special keyboards and fonts to input its dedicated symbols (such as ∇ and ⍴), making it difficult to use on ordinary terminals or in ASCII environments. Kenneth Iverson, APL's own creator, together with Roger Hui, wanted to create a successor language that could be written using only a standard ASCII keyboard without sacrificing the expressive power of array programming. By replacing special symbols with combinations of characters (compound operators such as `/.`, for example), it was designed as a language that would be easy to print, distribute, and share as text files.
summary_en: J is positioned as a niche language (status: niche), and as a successor array language that re-expressed APL using only ASCII characters, it continues to be used firmly by some specialists in fields such as numerical computing and finance.

name: K
problem: 金融の大量時系列データを、極限まで簡潔な記法でメモリ効率よく高速処理したかった。
summary: 金融業界の高速時系列データ処理で使われるAPL系言語。
problem_en: In the financial industry, there was a need to aggregate and analyze massive volumes of time-series data, such as stock prices and exchange rates, at speeds where even millisecond-level delays were unacceptable. Arthur Whitney, who had also been involved in the development of APL, wanted to push the conciseness of array programming even further and create a language that maximized memory efficiency and execution speed through a notation pared down to the absolute minimum amount of code. By making heavy use of single-character operators and implicit array operations, he aimed to make it possible to process queries against enormous time-series databases with astonishingly short code, and to do so at high speed.
summary_en: K is positioned as a niche language (status: niche), and it remains in active use today as an APL-family language for high-speed time-series data processing in the financial industry, through commercial products such as kdb+.

name: Wolfram Language
problem: 数式処理・数値計算・グラフ描画を単一の記号的な統一言語で扱いたかった。
summary: Mathematicaの基盤言語。あらゆるものを記号式として統一的に扱う。
problem_en: In the 1980s, symbolic computation (symbolic manipulation, differentiation, and integration of formulas), numerical computation, and graph plotting were often each handled by separate, dedicated pieces of software, forcing researchers to switch between different tools depending on their purpose. Stephen Wolfram, a theoretical physicist, wanted to create a language in which formulas, data, graphics, and even the program's own code could all be handled through a single, unified representation called a "symbolic expression." The Wolfram Language was developed under this philosophy of unified symbolic processing, and it was released to the world as the foundational language of the product Mathematica.
summary_en: It remains an active language today (status: active), continuing to be used in academic research and engineering computation as the foundational language of Mathematica, under a design philosophy that treats everything uniformly as symbolic expressions.

name: SQL
problem: E.F.Coddのリレーショナルモデルを、専門知識のない業務担当者でも英語に近い文で問い合わせできるようにしたかった。
summary: リレーショナルデータベース問い合わせの事実上唯一の標準言語。
problem_en: In 1970, IBM researcher E. F. Codd published a groundbreaking theory called the "relational model," which treated data as a collection of tables, but the language for actually manipulating it was pure mathematical relational algebra and relational logic, which was difficult for business staff without specialized knowledge to use. Donald Chamberlin and Raymond Boyce, also of IBM, wanted to let anyone query this relational model using syntax close to English sentences, such as "SELECT," "FROM," and "WHERE." This language, initially called SEQUEL (Structured English QUEry Language), was later renamed SQL and became established as the standard query language for relational database management systems (RDBMS).
summary_en: It remains an active language today (status: active), continuing to be used behind almost every business system and web service as the de facto sole standard language for querying relational databases.

name: Prolog
problem: 自然言語処理の研究のために、「どう計算するか」でなく「何が真か」という論理規則の記述だけでプログラムを動かしたかった。
summary: 論理プログラミングの代表格。AI・自然言語処理研究で使われた。
problem_en: In the early 1970s, natural language processing researchers faced a problem: when grammar rules and semantic interpretation rules were written in a procedural language, the description of "how to process things" buried the clarity of the language rules themselves. Alain Colmerauer of France and Robert Kowalski of the United Kingdom wanted to create a language that would directly execute the ideas of formal logic (predicate logic) as a program, so that one only had to write facts and rules about "what is true," and the system would automatically perform the inference. Born from this idea, Prolog became the flagship of a new paradigm, logic programming, operating based on a resolution principle involving backtracking search.
summary_en: Prolog is positioned as a niche language (status: niche), and as the flagship of logic programming it continues to be used in AI and natural language processing research and in some reasoning systems.

name: Datalog
problem: Prologの表現力の一部に限定する代わりに、必ず停止しデータベースクエリ最適化と相性の良い論理言語が欲しかった。
summary: 必ず停止することを保証した、DB向けに限定されたProlog系言語。
problem_en: Prolog was a highly expressive logic programming language, but because it allowed free use of recursion and side effects, it suffered from problems such as queries that might never terminate, or results that varied depending on execution order—making it awkward to use as a database query language. Database researchers wanted to keep Prolog's logic-programming framework while deliberately restricting its expressiveness, so that every query would always halt in finite time and would mesh well with relational database query-optimization techniques. Datalog was organized by the academic community by drawing on both the relational model of SQL and the ideas of logic programming.
summary_en: Datalog is positioned as a niche language (status: niche), adopted as the query foundation for program analysis tools and some graph database products, as a limited Prolog-derived language for databases that guarantees termination.

name: Mercury
problem: Prologの動的型付けゆえのバグを、静的な型・モード・決定性宣言で実行前に検出したかった。
summary: 静的型・モード解析を備えた高性能な論理型言語。
problem_en:
Prolog pioneered the expressive power of logic programming, but because it is dynamically typed, it had the weakness that errors in the types of arguments passed to predicates, or in their instantiation state (whether an argument is input or output), could not be discovered until runtime. The larger the software written in a logic-programming language, the more serious this kind of bug became, and it stood as a barrier to industrial adoption.

Researchers at the University of Melbourne in Australia sought to solve this problem by creating a language that retained Prolog's declarative expressive power while statically checking type, mode (whether an argument is bound or unbound), and determinism (how many solutions can be produced) at compile time. Begun as a research project, this effort also set a goal of exceeding existing logic-language implementations in execution speed.
summary_en: Mercury remains a niche language today, but its design as a statically typed logic language continues to be held in high academic regard. Practical adoption is limited, but the approach of overcoming Prolog's weaknesses through a type system represents a milestone in logic programming research where reliability is required. Development continues today, with the open-source community maintaining the implementation.

name: SPARQL
problem: RDF形式で表現されたセマンティックWeb上のグラフデータを横断的に問い合わせたかった。
summary: RDFグラフデータベース向けの標準クエリ言語。
problem_en:
In the 2000s, the W3C advocated the Semantic Web, an effort to make information on the web interpretable by machines as data with "meaning," and established RDF (triples consisting of subject, predicate, and object) as a general-purpose data model to serve as its foundation. However, without a standard means of actually searching and joining the distributed data expressed as RDF graphs, this model would not have been practical.

So the W3C established SPARQL as a standard query language based on graph pattern matching, playing a role analogous to SQL in relational databases. An important goal was also to allow multiple RDF data sources published by different organizations to be handled crosswise in a single query.
summary_en: SPARQL is still actively used today, retaining its status as the standard query language in the fields of knowledge graphs such as DBpedia and Wikidata, and in the Semantic Web and linked data. In recent years, alongside growing interest in graph databases in general, similar querying approaches have also drawn attention in graph stores other than RDF.

name: XQuery
problem: 増え続けるXML文書を、リレーショナルDBのように構造化して検索・変換したかった。
summary: XML文書に対する問い合わせ・変換を行う標準クエリ言語。
problem_en:
From the late 1990s into the 2000s, XML rapidly became the standard format for document exchange and data representation, but there was no unified way to search, extract, and transform tree-structured XML documents, forcing developers to rely on individual implementations using XSLT or general-purpose programming languages.

The W3C set out to define XQuery as a standard language that could declaratively query and transform sets of XML documents, much as SQL does for relational databases, unifying the search and reconstruction of hierarchically structured data. A further goal was to allow queries spanning multiple XML documents or databases to be expressed within a single language.
summary_en: XQuery now occupies a niche position; it never became mainstream, partly because the spread of the JSON format relatively shrank XML usage itself, but it is still used in some native XML databases and document processing systems. It remains a technology in active use in fields where XML retains a strong foothold, such as processing financial transaction messages.

name: PL/SQL
problem: SQLだけでは書けない条件分岐やループを伴う手続き型ロジックを、データベースサーバ内で直接実行したかった。
summary: Oracle DB向けのSQL手続き型拡張言語。
problem_en:
SQL was designed as a declarative query language based on set operations, and it was not well suited to expressing complex business logic involving conditional branching, loops, and variables. As a result, assembling processing that spanned multiple SQL statements on the application side increased network round-trip overhead, which was inefficient both in terms of performance and manageability.

Oracle developed PL/SQL, an extension language that built procedural control structures into SQL, allowing complex business logic to be executed directly inside the database server as stored procedures. This eliminated the need to exchange SQL statements repeatedly between client and server, allowing entire processes to be completed on the server side.
summary_en: PL/SQL continues to be actively used today as the core extension language of the Oracle database, and it remains in active operation in the core systems of many enterprises, including those in finance and manufacturing.

name: Transact-SQL(T-SQL)
problem: SQL Serverのストアドプロシージャとして、手続き的な制御構造を持つ処理をサーバ側で実行したかった。
summary: SQL Server向けのSQL手続き型拡張言語。
problem_en:
Standard SQL is a declarative query language based on set operations, and lacked mechanisms for expressing procedural processing such as variable declarations, conditional branches, and loops.

Sybase developed Transact-SQL by adding procedural control structures to SQL, in order to meet the need, in its own database products, to execute business logic combining multiple SQL statements together on the server side without communication between client and server. It was later carried over to Microsoft, which built SQL Server based on Sybase's technology, and became the core language of Microsoft's flagship database product.
summary_en: Transact-SQL remains actively used today as the core language of Microsoft SQL Server (and Azure SQL), and continues to see widespread active use in developing stored procedures for enterprise systems. Even amid the shift toward the cloud, it continues to play an important role as a target for migrating existing assets.

name: PostScript
problem: プリンタの機種ごとに異なる制御コードを気にせず、ページのレイアウトを機種非依存に正確に記述したかった。
summary: ページ記述言語の元祖。PDFの前身となった。
problem_en:
In the early 1980s, laser printers and typesetting machines each had their own proprietary control codes depending on the manufacturer and model, making it difficult to print the same document accurately on a different output device. John Warnock and others, who had been researching page description at Xerox PARC, conceived of a language to solve this problem by describing the placement of text, graphics, and images on a page in a device-independent way.

Because Xerox was reluctant to commercialize the technology, Warnock and colleagues left to found Adobe and turned it into a product called PostScript. A defining characteristic was its Forth-derived, stack-based execution model, which allowed the processor built into a printer to directly interpret and execute the program.
summary_en: PostScript is now a legacy technology, with new practical use almost entirely replaced by PDF, but its historical significance as a foundational technology of the printing industry, with immense influence over many years, remains great. Some print workflows and RIPs (raster image processors) still continue to use PostScript implementations.

name: TeX
problem: 自著の数学書の組版品質が活版印刷から劣化していくことに耐えられず、美しい数式組版を自分で厳密に制御したかった。
summary: 学術論文組版の事実上の標準。LaTeXの基盤言語。
problem_en:
Donald Knuth was deeply dissatisfied that the revised edition of his own book, "The Art of Computer Programming," was published with degraded typesetting quality as a result of the shift from letterpress printing to phototypesetting. In particular, typesetting academic books containing mathematical formulas required a high level of specialized skill, and the general document processing systems of the time could not reproduce that quality.

Knuth therefore set out to design and implement his own typesetting system, one that could rigorously control line spacing, letter spacing, and even mathematical formula layout as algorithms, in order to achieve high-quality typesetting by computer. Development took far longer than originally anticipated, and Knuth himself ended up researching typography theory as a result.
summary_en: TeX is still widely used today in the typesetting of academic papers and mathematics books, and especially in the form of LaTeX it remains the de facto standard for writing papers in fields such as mathematics, physics, and computer science. Despite being designed more than 40 years ago, the fact that it is still actively used today is an unusual case of longevity in the history of programming languages.

name: Verilog
problem: デジタル回路の設計を、実際に試作する前にシミュレーションで動作検証できる記述言語が欲しかった。
summary: デジタル回路設計・検証で広く使われるハードウェア記述言語。
problem_en:
As integrated circuits grew more complex, designers found it increasingly difficult to fully verify the behavior of large-scale digital circuits using only circuit diagrams or breadboard prototypes. If defects were discovered only after a chip was actually manufactured, it resulted in enormous losses of cost and time.

Phil Moorby therefore developed Verilog as a language that could describe a circuit's structure and behavior like software, allowing logical behavior to be verified on a simulator before manufacturing. By adopting a syntax similar to C, it was designed to be easy for existing software engineers to pick up.
summary_en: Verilog remains widely used today in semiconductor design and verification, and alongside VHDL it holds its position as one of the two major hardware description languages for digital circuit design. In commercial ASIC design and verification flows in particular, its extended version, SystemVerilog, has become the de facto standard.

name: VHDL
designers: 米国防総省(VHSICプログラム)
problem: 米軍が発注する集積回路の仕様を、発注元と製造元の間で曖昧さなく共有できる標準記述形式にしたかった。
summary: Adaの構文を受け継ぐ、防衛・航空宇宙分野発のハードウェア記述言語。
problem_en:
In the early 1980s, the U.S. Department of Defense was commissioning integrated circuits from numerous private companies as part of the VHSIC (Very High Speed Integrated Circuit) program, but because each company used its own proprietary design documents and notation, discrepancies in specification interpretation arose, and it was difficult to maintain and reuse design assets over the long term.

The Department of Defense therefore established VHDL (VHSIC Hardware Description Language) as a standard description language that could unambiguously share circuit specifications between clients and manufacturers, and that could be verified and reused into the future. In designing it, the syntax of Ada — already adopted as the standard language for military and defense systems — was used as a base, and a rigorous specification premised on long-term maintainability was required.
summary_en: VHDL remains an actively used language, widely employed today in semiconductor design and verification. Alongside Verilog, it is one of the two major hardware description languages for digital circuit design, and it enjoys particularly high trust in the defense and aerospace fields. It also continues to be adopted as a standard in university education and public institution projects, especially in Europe.

name: dBase
problem: パーソナルコンピュータ上で、専門家でなくても簡易なデータベース(住所録等)を作成・検索できるようにしたかった。
summary: パソコン向けデータベース管理ソフトの草分け。
problem_en:
In the late 1970s, when personal computers were just beginning to appear, database management was a technology for specialists working on mainframes or minicomputers, and it was difficult for ordinary users to build and search simple databases such as address books or inventory lists on their own.

Wayne Ratliff, an engineer at JPL (the Jet Propulsion Laboratory), developed a data-management program called Vulcan as a hobby project and expanded it into dBase, which allowed users to register, search, and aggregate data simply by entering commands, without requiring specialized knowledge. It was then commercialized by Ashton-Tate.
summary_en: dBase is now a historical language with almost no new practical use, but as a pioneer of database management software for personal computers, it left a great influence on subsequent compatible products and the culture of business application development. The ".dbf" file format continued to be used for a long time as a data exchange format with other software, even after dBase itself declined.

name: FoxPro
problem: dBaseと互換性を保ちながら、実行速度の遅さを解消し、より高度なアプリケーション開発環境を提供したかった。
summary: dBase互換で高速化された、業務アプリ開発向けDB言語。
problem_en:
dBase, as a pioneer of PC-based database management software, achieved widespread adoption, but its slow execution speed as an interpreted language and its lack of features for building large-scale business applications were pointed out as shortcomings.

Fox Software developed FoxPro as a product that maintained compatibility with dBase's .dbf format and command set while offering speed gains through compilation and a more advanced development environment (including a screen designer and report-building features). Maintaining compatibility so that existing dBase users could migrate easily was also an important goal for capturing the market.
summary_en: FoxPro is now a legacy language, and after Microsoft ended support for it, it has seen almost no adoption in new development, but it has a track record of having supported many small and medium-sized business systems from the 1990s through the 2000s. There remains some ongoing demand for maintaining old Visual FoxPro applications that are still running today.

name: sh(Bourne Shell)
problem: Unixの旧シェルの機能不足(制御構造やスクリプトの読みやすさ)を解消し、堅牢なシステム管理用スクリプト言語にしたかった。
summary: Unixシェルスクリプトの標準的な祖形。POSIX shの基礎。
problem_en:
The old shell (the Thompson shell) bundled with 1970s Unix Version 7 had very poor control structures, such as variables, loops, and conditionals, and lacked the features needed to write substantial scripts.

Stephen Bourne of Bell Labs designed the Bourne Shell as a more robust language, drawing on the block structure and expression concepts of ALGOL 68, able to withstand both interactive command entry and script writing for system administration. This design was adopted as the standard shell across Unix-family operating systems and became the common foundation for the shell languages that followed.
summary_en:
sh (Bourne Shell) remains active today as the basic specification for POSIX-compliant shell scripting, continuing to exist as `/bin/sh` on many Unix-family systems.

It is the syntactic prototype of successor shells such as Bash and Zsh, and it is positioned as the starting point of the shell-scripting field itself. Its role as a highly portable, minimal common language continues to be valued in writing automation scripts today.

name: Bash
problem: GNUプロジェクトとして、プロプライエタリなBourne Shellの自由な代替実装を提供したかった。
summary: GNU/Linuxの標準シェル。今も大半のLinuxディストリビューションで既定。
problem_en:
In the 1980s, the standard Unix shell, the Bourne Shell, was proprietary software owned by AT&T and could not be freely modified or redistributed. The GNU Project aimed to build a "completely free Unix-compatible OS," and as part of that effort a free, Bourne-Shell-compatible shell was needed.

Brian Fox developed Bash as an extended shell that preserved sh-compatible syntax while incorporating features such as the C shell's history mechanism and the Korn shell's completion functionality. The name "Bourne-Again SHell" signals that it is the spiritual successor to the Bourne Shell.
summary_en:
Bash is still adopted as the default shell in most Linux distributions today, and remains widely used as a scripting language for system administration and CI/CD.

Beyond the GNU Project's original goal of a free Bourne-Shell-compatible environment, it has become, in effect, one of the industry-standard shells — an indispensable presence in server operations and automation.

name: Zsh
problem: 既存シェルの補完機能や対話性の弱さを見直し、より高機能でカスタマイズ性の高い形にしたかった。
summary: 高度な補完機能で人気、macOSの標準シェルにも採用された。
problem_en:
By 1990, the Bourne Shell (sh) and Bash were already widely used, but there remained room for improvement in areas such as completion features, spelling-mistake correction, and interactive customizability.

Paul Falstad, then a student at Princeton University, developed Zsh to create an interactive shell that incorporated the good parts of existing shells such as sh, Bash, and the C shell, while being more capable and flexibly customizable. It began as a personal project, but features were gradually added and it developed into an independent shell.
summary_en:
Zsh retains a devoted following thanks to its advanced completion features and customizability, and its adoption as the default shell on macOS further widened its user base.

Community configuration frameworks such as Oh My Zsh have also become popular, and it remains in active use today as an interactive shell for developers.

name: csh(C Shell)
problem: プログラマがC言語の構文感覚のままシェルスクリプトや対話操作(ヒストリ機能等)を扱えるようにしたかった。
summary: C風構文とヒストリ機能を導入した対話向けシェル。
problem_en:
In the late 1970s, Bill Joy, who led the development of BSD Unix at the University of California, Berkeley, found the interactive usability of the shells of the time lacking—for instance, there was no way to reuse command history.

Additionally, for programmers accustomed to C, the syntax of the Bourne Shell demanded a different style of writing than C did, imposing a learning cost. Joy therefore designed csh as an interaction-oriented shell whose expressions and control syntax were closer to those of C, and which also came equipped with history and alias functionality.
summary_en:
Design flaws pointed out in csh as a scripting language led to it being gradually replaced by Bourne-family shells for system administration purposes.

Its lineage as an interactive shell was carried on by tcsh, but csh itself is now a legacy presence that sees hardly any use in new script development.

name: fish
problem: シェルの構文の一貫性のなさや設定の煩雑さを見直し、デフォルトのままで賢い補完と読みやすさを提供したかった。
summary: 設定なしで使えるユーザーフレンドリーな対話型シェル。
problem_en:
Years of maintaining backward compatibility had left Bash and Zsh with syntax that was in places inconsistent, and that was hard to use comfortably without initial configuration.

Axel Liljencrantz wanted to design from scratch, without being bound by backward compatibility with the sh family, so as to create a user-friendly interactive shell that offers smart autocompletion and readable syntax by default, with no configuration file required. This is how fish came about; the name derives from "friendly interactive shell."
summary_en:
Because of its lack of POSIX compatibility, fish is unlikely to become a corporate systems-administration standard, but it retains a strong following centered on individual interactive use, making it a niche presence.

Its approach of providing a comfortable experience with no configuration required is often cited when discussing the modern shell and terminal experience.

name: Logo
problem: 子供が「タートルグラフィックス」を動かす体験を通して、抽象的な数学的思考をプログラミングで学べるようにしたかった。
summary: タートルグラフィックスで知られる教育用言語の元祖。
problem_en:
The psychologist and mathematician Seymour Papert wondered whether children could intuitively grasp abstract mathematical concepts through a "bodily sense of movement." Programming education at the time was aimed mainly at university students and professionals, and there was almost no language accessible to children.

Building on Lisp's approach to symbolic processing, Papert introduced "turtle graphics," in which a character called a "turtle" on screen is moved by commands to draw shapes, and designed Logo as a language for learning procedural thinking, recursion, and geometric concepts while playing. This idea grew out of educational experiments at MIT's Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.
summary_en:
Logo, as the originator of turtle graphics, left a large mark on the history of educational languages, and it continues to be used in some educational settings today.

It is positioned as a language that laid the foundation for the field of programming education itself, with its ideas carried forward into more intuitive visual programming environments such as Scratch that followed it.

name: Scratch
problem: 子供がテキストの文法エラーに悩まされず、ブロックを組み合わせるだけでプログラムの概念を学べるようにしたかった。
summary: ブロックを組み合わせる視覚的プログラミング教育の世界的標準。
problem_en:
In traditional text-based programming education, syntax errors (typos, forgetting a semicolon, and so on) posed a major barrier for children, making it hard for them to focus on the programming concepts they were actually supposed to learn.

Mitchel Resnick and others at the MIT Media Lab, carrying forward the educational spirit of Logo's turtle graphics, aimed to create an environment where programs could be built simply by dragging and dropping blocks instead of typing code, and developed Scratch with this in mind. The goal was for children around the world to learn programming through creating and sharing their own creative works.
summary_en:
Scratch has established itself as the worldwide standard for visual, block-based programming education, and it remains widely used today as teaching material for programming in primary and secondary education.

Its design philosophy of letting learners grasp programming concepts without being troubled by syntax errors has had a major influence on the way programming education itself is approached.

name: Alice
problem: 3Dアニメーションのキャラクターを操作する楽しさを通じて、初学者にオブジェクト指向の概念を教えたかった。
summary: 3Dアニメーション制作を通じてOOPの概念を学ぶ教育用環境。
problem_en:
Object-oriented programming deals with abstract concepts such as classes, methods, and instances, which made it difficult to approach, especially for programming beginners and for women and others less familiar with traditional CS education.

Randy Pausch and others at Carnegie Mellon University extended the Logo-like idea of learning by moving a character around, and developed Alice as an environment where learners could naturally absorb the concepts of objects and method calls while having fun, through the experience of moving 3D animated characters with drag-and-drop commands.
summary_en:
Alice continues to be used today in introductory university lectures and elsewhere as an educational environment for learning object-oriented concepts through 3D animation creation.

It maintains a unique position in programming education as teaching material for the stage before transitioning to text-based languages.

name: LabVIEW
problem: 電気・機械系のエンジニアがテキストコードを書かずに、計測器制御プログラムを配線図のように視覚的に組みたかった。
summary: 計測・制御分野で使われるデータフロー型のビジュアルプログラミング環境。
problem_en:
Electrical and mechanical engineers working with measurement and control instrumentation were not necessarily skilled in text-based programming languages, and developing instrument-control programs in a language like C posed a significant barrier to entry.

National Instruments reasoned that if measurement programs could be built with a feel similar to wiring up a schematic or circuit diagram, then even people who were not specialist programmers could develop data-acquisition and instrument-control software. This led to LabVIEW, a "dataflow" visual programming environment in which icons are connected by wires to represent the flow of data.
summary_en:
LabVIEW continues to be used actively today in the measurement and control field, with a broad track record of adoption in industrial applications combined with National Instruments' measurement hardware.

Its distinctive ability to build specialized measurement programs without writing text code sets it apart from visual programming environments in other fields.

name: Brainfuck
problem: 最小限の8命令だけでチューリング完全性を実現できるか、また可能な限り小さな処理系(240バイト)を作れるかという極限の挑戦だった。
summary: 最小構成のチューリング完全言語として最も有名な難解言語。
problem_en: Urban Müller created this language as an extreme thought experiment into how few instructions could be pared down while still achieving Turing completeness. The goal was to show that programs could be written with as few as eight instructions, and also to make the compiler itself as small as possible (the first implementation is said to have been 240 bytes), with practicality disregarded from the outset. It also carried a self-deprecating aim of being "a language for writing programs that are hard to read and hard to write," and precisely because of this extremity it became the symbolic representative of the esoteric language (esolang) genre.
summary_en: Positioned as esoteric (an esolang), it is not used for practical purposes. As the archetype of a minimal Turing-complete language, it is the best known within the esoteric-language community and continues to be used as a reference point and model when creating new esoteric languages.

name: Whitespace
problem: 空白・タブ・改行という「目に見えない」文字だけでプログラムを構成できるかというジョーク的な発想を実現したかった。
summary: 空白文字だけで書く、他言語コードに埋め込み可能な難解言語。
problem_en: Whitespace was created out of a purely joking idea: "wouldn't it be fun if a program's meaningful code could be made up entirely of invisible characters — spaces, tabs, and newlines?" It was released, fittingly, on April Fools' Day, and its purpose was less about solving any practical problem than about inverting the common assumption of existing programming languages that only visible characters count as code. Part of the idea also envisioned a mischievous use case: embedding a separate program, invisible to the eye, within the source code of another language, appearing as nothing but blank space.
summary_en: It is positioned as an esoteric language and is not used for practical purposes. Because of the strong impact of "invisible code," it is still frequently cited today in articles introducing esoteric languages, or simply as a joke.

name: INTERCAL
problem: 既存のあらゆる言語設計上の「常識」(単純な代入や明快な制御構造)をあえて全て裏返し、パロディとして極めて書きにくい言語を作りたかった。
summary: 最古の難解言語とされる、既存言語設計へのパロディ作品。
problem_en: INTERCAL is considered the oldest esoteric language, created in a spirit of parody that deliberately inverted every design "common sense" of existing languages of the time such as Fortran and COBOL. It intentionally ignored textbook principles of good language design, such as simple assignment and clear control structures — the joke was the very act of creating "a language as far from practicality as possible, hard to write and hard to understand." Elements such as the obligation to insert the polite word `PLEASE` before commands, and a specification in which commands are ignored with a certain probability, are scattered throughout as satire of serious language design.
summary_en: INTERCAL is classified as esoteric and is not used for practical purposes. It is regarded as the starting point of the esoteric language genre itself, and is passed down as the classic origin that many later joke languages reference.

name: Befunge
problem: プログラムを1次元の行としてではなく2次元の格子として実行し、コンパイラの最適化(命令の並べ替え)を根本的に不可能にする挑戦だった。
summary: 命令が2次元格子上を動き回って実行される難解言語。
problem_en: Befunge grew out of the challenge of executing a program as a two-dimensional grid rather than as a traditional one-dimensional sequence of lines. Because the instruction pointer moves freely around the grid, turning up, down, left, or right, this fundamentally defeats the usual technique of a compiler reordering instructions for optimization — it was, in a sense, a challenge in "unoptimizability." The fact that the source code itself can take the form of a picture-like two-dimensional figure also makes this language unique.
summary_en: Befunge is positioned as an esoteric language and is not used for practical purposes. Owing to its unique two-dimensional execution model, it is especially known among esoteric languages for its distinctive visual appearance, and it has served as a starting point for derivative languages and later visually oriented esoteric languages.

name: Malbolge
problem: 「意図的に人間にもコンパイラにも理解不能な、実用上最も書くのが困難な言語」を作るという極端な思考実験だった。
summary: 設計者自身も最初のプログラムを書けなかったとされる最難関の難解言語。
problem_en: Malbolge was designed as an extreme thought experiment aimed at "creating a language that is intentionally incomprehensible to both humans and compilers, and that is practically the most difficult to write." The name is taken from the eighth circle of Hell in Dante's Divine Comedy (the realm of malicious fraud), and true to its name, it aims to push the "difficulty of writing" found in existing esoteric languages to an even more extreme limit. It has a mechanism whereby the meaning of instructions changes according to execution position and cryptographic transformations, and its design is so counterintuitive that even its own designer is said to have initially been unable to hand-write a working program.
summary_en: Malbolge is positioned as esoteric and is not used for practical purposes. With a reputation as "theoretically Turing-complete but practically almost impossible to write," it is treated as being in a class of its own even within the esoteric-language community.

name: Piet
problem: プログラムのソースコード自体を抽象絵画(色の付いたピクセル格子)として成立させたかった。
summary: ソースコードが画家ピート・モンドリアン風の抽象画になる難解言語。
problem_en: Piet was born from a purely artistic motivation: to make source code itself function as an abstract painting. Its name comes from the painter Piet Mondrian, and by executing a grid of colored pixels as "source code," it embodies a thought experiment that makes program and painting coincide. Practical programming convenience is entirely disregarded; instead, the challenge lies in how much complex processing can be achieved within the constraint of "can you write a program that is also a beautiful, or meaningful, picture."
summary_en: Piet is positioned as an esoteric language and is not used for practical purposes. It is often introduced, particularly within the more art-oriented corners of the esoteric-language world, as a representative example of fusing programming with visual art.

name: LOLCODE
problem: インターネットミーム「lolcat」の話し言葉(壊れた英語)そのものをプログラミング言語の構文にするジョークだった。
summary: lolcatミームの言い回しをそのまま構文にしたジョーク言語。
problem_en: LOLCODE arose from a joke: taking the "lolcat" meme that was popular on the internet at the time (the deliberately broken English phrasing attached to cat pictures) and turning it directly into the syntax of a programming language. A program that begins with "HAI" and ends with "KTHXBYE," with variable declaration written as "I HAS A," faithfully renders the internet meme's phrasing into code as an end in itself, and it also serves as a parody of existing languages with their earnest grammatical rules.
summary_en: It is positioned as esoteric and is not used for practical purposes. As a leading example of an internet meme turned directly into a programming language, it is often introduced as an approachable gateway into esoteric languages.

name: Chef
problem: 動作するプログラムのソースコードを、そのまま実際に調理できる料理レシピとして読めるようにしたかった。
summary: プログラムが料理レシピとして読める難解言語。
problem_en: Chef was created from a humorous thought experiment: making the source code of a working program readable as an actual cooking recipe that could literally be cooked. Programs include an ingredient list and cooking steps, with variables mapped to "ingredients" and stack operations mapped to cooking actions such as "mixing" and "pouring." The core idea of the language is introducing an evaluation axis entirely different from practicality — aiming for both correct operation as a program and (in theory) the ability for a human to actually cook it as a recipe.
summary_en: It is positioned as an esoteric language and is not used for practical purposes. Because its source code can genuinely be read as an actual recipe, it is introduced as a particularly humorous work even among esoteric languages.

name: Shakespeare Programming Language
problem: プログラムのソースコードを、シェイクスピア劇の台本のように登場人物の対話として書けるようにしたかった。
summary: 戯曲の台本のような構文を持つ難解言語。
problem_en: The Shakespeare Programming Language (SPL) aims to let source code be written as dialogue between characters, in the manner of a Shakespearean play script. Variables are declared as "characters," and assignment and arithmetic are expressed as theatrical compliments or insults exchanged between characters. The goal was a literary parody, far removed from practicality: a program that both runs correctly and can (with some strain) be read aloud as a play.
summary_en: It is positioned as an esoteric language and is not used for practical purposes. Thanks to the literary device that makes a program readable aloud as a play, it is remembered as a particularly unique work even among esoteric languages.

name: Unlambda
problem: 変数を一切使わず、純粋な関数合成(SKIコンビネータ計算)だけでプログラムが書けることを示したかった。
summary: 変数を持たず関数合成のみで書く、コンビネータ論理ベースの難解言語。
problem_en: Unlambda was created as a thought experiment to show that a program could be written using nothing but pure function composition—that is, SKI combinator calculus—without using any variables at all. True to its name, "un-lambda" strips the "lambda" (variable binding) itself out of the lambda calculus, and the language's aim is to deliberately eliminate the notion, central to functional programming, of naming and handling values, in order to push to the limit just how much computation can be expressed through combinator application alone.
summary_en: Unlambda is positioned as an esoteric language and is not used for practical purposes. Its theoretical purity as a "variable-free functional language" makes it especially favored, among esoteric languages, by those with an interest in the theory of computation.

name: Ook!
problem: Brainfuckの8命令を、オランウータンの鳴き声(Ook.など)の組み合わせだけに置き換えるジョークだった。
summary: Brainfuckをオランウータンの鳴き声だけで表現し直したジョーク言語。
problem_en: Ook! was created as a straightforward joke that replaces Brainfuck's eight instructions with nothing but orangutan calls (combinations of "Ook.", "Ook?", and "Ook!"). Its name and concept are an homage to Terry Pratchett's Discworld series, in which the Librarian of the Unseen University has been transformed into an orangutan and can say only "Ook" — no practical problem-solving was ever intended. It simply assigns, faithfully and one-to-one, a three-word combination to each of Brainfuck's instructions, and the very idea of "reimplementing a minimal language in the most nonsensical syntax possible" is itself the joke.
summary_en: It is classified as esoteric and is not used for practical purposes. As a parody of Brainfuck, it is often cited within the esolang community as a representative "one-off joke."

name: ArnoldC
problem: 映画俳優アーノルド・シュワルツェネッガーの名台詞だけでプログラムの制御構造(if文やループ)を表現したかった。
summary: 映画の名台詞がそのまま構文になっているジョーク言語。
problem_en: ArnoldC was created as a joke that combined fandom with programming, expressing a program's control structures (if statements, loops, function definitions) entirely through famous lines from actor Arnold Schwarzenegger's movies. "I'll be back" represents the end of a loop, and "GET TO THE CHOPPER" represents the start of a function, and so on: the goal itself was to dutifully map famous movie lines onto syntactic elements, with no intention from the outset of solving any practical programming problem.
summary_en: Positioned as an esoteric language, it is not used for practical purposes. As a joke language that even movie fans can appreciate, it is still frequently cited today as an introduction to esoteric languages or as a joke in presentation titles.

name: FALSE
problem: たった1024バイトの極小コンパイラで、Forth的なスタックベース言語をどこまで機能的に作れるか試したかった。
summary: 極小コンパイラを追求した言語。Brainfuck誕生の直接のきっかけとなった。
problem_en: FALSE was created as a challenge to see how functional a Forth-like stack-based language could be made with a compiler of only 1024 bytes. Rather than practicality itself, it was a minimalist experiment in how much language functionality could be preserved under the constraint of shrinking the compiler's implementation size to the utmost limit, and the resulting terse, symbol-heavy syntax later became one of the starting points of the "esoteric language" genre. The name "FALSE" itself is a wry joke, hinting at a denial of practicality.
summary_en: FALSE is positioned as an esoteric language and is not used for practical purposes. Owing to its aspect as an experiment in minimal compilers, it continues to be referenced by later designers of esoteric languages as one of the representative works of the genre's early days.

name: ひまわり
problem: 日本語話者、特にプログラミング初心者が、英語圏の構文に慣れる負担なく日本語の文法のままプログラムを記述できるようにしたかった。日本語処理系だけで実用的なプログラムが書けることを示す先駆的な試みとして開発された。
summary: なでしこの前身となった日本語プログラミング言語。2008年公開のVer.1.94を最後に開発終了。
wikipedia_ja: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ひまわり_%28プログラミング言語%29
problem_en: Around 2000, English-based syntax was a major barrier to learning for Japanese speakers, especially programming beginners. Kujira Hikoutsukue thought that this barrier could be removed if programs could be written using the grammar of the Japanese language as-is. Himawari was developed as a pioneering attempt to demonstrate that practical programs could be written using a Japanese-language processing system alone, and it was implemented in Delphi (Object Pascal).
summary_en: Development stopped after the release of Ver. 1.94 in 2008, and it is now positioned as a historical language. Its design philosophy has been carried forward into its successor language, Nadeshiko.

name: なでしこ
problem: 日本語話者がプログラミング学習の障壁である英語ベースの構文を超え、母語である日本語の文法でそのままプログラムを記述できるようにしたかった。前身のひまわりが抱えていた実行速度の遅さや不自然な日本語命令といった問題を、文法とシステム構成から根本的に再設計することで解決したかった。
summary: 日本国内で最もよく知られる日本語プログラミング言語の一つ。教育・趣味用途で使われる。
wikipedia_ja: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/なでしこ_%28プログラミング言語%29
problem_en: Its predecessor language, Himawari (ひまわり), was praised for its philosophy of letting programs be written in Japanese, but it had practical shortcomings such as slow execution speed, the need for word-segmented (spaced) text, and many unnatural Japanese commands. To resolve these problems, Kujira Hikouki chose not merely to improve the existing codebase but to rethink the grammar and system architecture from the design stage, building a more natural and faster Japanese programming language from scratch. The official release was published on February 17, 2005.
summary_en: Nadeshiko is one of the best-known Japanese programming languages in Japan, and continues to be used today for educational purposes and hobbyist programming. Development is ongoing, and version 3 moved to a JavaScript-based implementation.

name: HSP(Hot Soup Processor)
problem: プログラミング初心者や趣味のゲーム制作者が、BASICのような手軽さでWindows上のゲームやツールを日本語環境ですぐに作れるようにしたかった。
summary: ゲーム開発・同人ソフト界隈で長年使われてきた国産のホビー向け言語。
problem_en: In the mid-1990s, following its predecessor Light SOUP Processor (LSP), which had been developed for the PC-9800 series, Onitama wanted to let programming beginners and hobbyists who wished to make games or tools write programs with the ease of BASIC, but suited to the Windows environment of the time. Development began in 1995, and it was released as freeware in 1996.
summary_en: It is a domestically developed (Japanese) hobby-oriented language that has long enjoyed high recognition in the game development and doujin software community, and it continues to be developed today as HSP3.

name: Mind
problem: 日本語話者がForthの強力なスタックベース計算モデルの恩恵を受けながら、英語のワード列ではなく日本語の語順に近い記述でPOSシステムなど大規模な業務システムを開発できるようにしたかった。
summary: Forthから派生した日本語プログラミング言語。業務システム開発で使われてきた。
problem_en: Forth allows fast, resource-efficient programs to be written thanks to its stack-based computational model, but its notation built from English word sequences was not intuitive for Japanese speakers. Katagiri Akira wanted to preserve Forth's powerful computational model and extensibility while making it possible to write programs in a natural notation closer to Japanese word order, creating a Japanese programming language robust enough to withstand the development of large-scale business systems such as POS systems.
summary_en: Among Japanese programming languages it has a long history, and it remains a niche language still used today in the field of business system development.

name: ドリトル
problem: 日本の小中学校の情報教育で、英語ベースの構文につまずくことなく、日本語の語順のままオブジェクト指向プログラミングとタートルグラフィックスの概念を学べる教材言語が必要だった。
summary: 日本語による教育用オブジェクト指向言語。初等・中等教育のプログラミング教材として使われる。
wikipedia_ja: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ドリトル_%28プログラミング言語%29
problem_en: Around the year 2000, computing education in Japanese elementary and junior high schools called for teaching materials that would let students learn the fundamentals of programming without stumbling over English-based syntax. Susumu Kanemune (currently a professor at Osaka Electro-Communication University) and Yasushi Kuno believed that a language allowing objects to be manipulated in Japanese word order (subject-object-predicate) would let children naturally encounter the ideas of object orientation and turtle graphics, and they designed Dolittle with this in mind. Its name derives both from "do little" (a play on doing a bit of programming) and from Hugh Lofting's novel character Doctor Dolittle.
summary_en: As a Japanese-language educational object-oriented language, it continues to be used today as programming teaching material in primary and secondary education.

name: プロデル
problem: Visual Basic 6.0ベースの日本語言語TTSneoが.NET時代に取り残されていく中、.NET Framework基盤で日本語の語順のままオブジェクト指向のWindowsアプリケーションを開発できる後継環境が必要だった。
summary: .NET Framework上で動く日本語プログラミング言語。TTSneoの後継として開発された。
problem_en: The Japanese-language programming language TTSneo had been a beloved scripting language built on Visual Basic 6.0, but as the era of .NET arrived, its underlying technology was becoming outdated. The developer known as "Yuto" wanted to rebuild, on the .NET Framework, an environment that let users develop object-oriented Windows applications while writing code in natural Japanese word order, in order to offer TTSneo users a successor language they could migrate to. A concept version was released in August 2007.
summary_en: Prodel is often introduced as one of the "three major Japanese programming languages," alongside Nadeshiko and Dolittle, and remains a niche language on the .NET platform that continues to be actively developed today.

name: Mojo
problem: PythonがAI/ML分野で広く使われる一方、実行速度の遅さとGPU/TPUなどハードウェア向け最適化の欠如が、研究からプロダクションへの移行を妨げていた。Pythonとの高い構文互換性を保ちながら、Rust並みの安全性とC言語並みの実行速度を単一言語で実現したかった。
summary: Python互換の構文を持つAI/システムプログラミング向け新言語。MLIR基盤のコンパイラを持つ。
problem_en: In the early 2020s, Python had become the de facto standard language for AI and machine learning, but its slow execution speed as an interpreted language, and its lack of optimization for accelerators such as GPUs and TPUs, were hindering the transition from research-stage prototypes to production environments. Chris Lattner, who had also designed LLVM, Clang, and Swift, founded Modular and developed Mojo as a language that maintains a high degree of syntactic compatibility with Python while achieving, through compilation, memory safety on par with Rust and execution speed on par with C.
summary_en: Mojo is an emerging language under active development that addresses Python's execution-speed problems in the AI and machine learning field, and its adoption is expected to spread following its open-sourcing in 2026.

name: V
