problem: Go言語のシンプルさや高速なコンパイルを保ちながら、Goが持たない直和型(sum type)などの機能を追加し、外部依存のないシングルバイナリを高速に生成できる言語が欲しかった。
summary: シンプルさと高速コンパイルを掲げる新興のシステムプログラミング言語。
problem_en: Go had gained support for its simple syntax and fast compilation, but it lacked some features that developers wanted, such as sum types, option types, and compile-time safety checks. Alexander Medvednikov designed V as a modern systems programming language that preserved Go's simplicity and good developer experience while adding these features, and that could quickly generate single binaries with no external dependencies.
summary_en: V is a niche, up-and-coming systems programming language that touts simplicity and fast compilation, and it has an active community.

name: Odin
problem: ゲーム開発のようなデータ指向設計(DOD)が求められる分野で、C言語のシンプルさを保ちながら、モダンな配列・スライス機能と高速なコンパイル時間を提供するシステムプログラミング言語が欲しかった。
summary: ゲーム開発者に人気のデータ指向設計向けシステムプログラミング言語。
problem_en: In fields such as game development, where large amounts of data need to be processed efficiently, the idea of Data-Oriented Design (DOD) had come to be emphasized. Bill Hall believed there was a need for a systems programming language that preserved the simplicity and transparency of C while offering modern array and slice features, fast compile times, and language features that made DOD easy to practice, and he began developing Odin in 2016.
summary_en: It is a systems programming language for data-oriented design that has been gaining popularity mainly among game developers, and it continues to be actively developed as an option alongside C, C++, and Rust.

name: Windows Batch(コマンドプロンプト)
problem: MS-DOSの利用者が、COMMAND.COM(後のcmd.exe)に一連のコマンドを手入力する手間を省き、定型的な操作をファイルにまとめて自動実行できるようにしたかった。CP/Mから続くコマンド行操作の延長として、最小限の制御構文(IF、GOTO、FORなど)だけを備えた素朴なスクリプト機能が用意された。
summary: MS-DOS/Windowsのコマンドプロンプトで使われる最も基本的なスクリプト言語。
problem_en: In MS-DOS, which appeared in 1981, users had to manually type a series of commands into the command interpreter COMMAND.COM each time. Performing routine operations (such as copying files or making backups) manually every time was inefficient, and, as an extension of the command-line operations carried over from CP/M, a mechanism was needed that could bundle a series of commands into a file and run them automatically. The resulting batch file (.bat) had minimal control constructs such as IF, GOTO, and FOR, and on Windows NT-based systems, cmd.exe — the successor to COMMAND.COM — carried this on.
summary_en: Now that the more capable [PowerShell](powershell.md) has appeared, adoption in new development has decreased, but it remains widely used in legacy automation scripts and the maintenance of older systems — the most fundamental scripting language in the Windows environment.

name: GW-BASIC
problem: IBM PC互換機の普及に伴い、ROMに焼き込まれたIBM Cassette BASIC/BASICAに依存しない、ディスクベースで動作する独立したBASIC処理系が必要だった。既存のBASICプログラム資産との高い互換性を保ちながら、PC-DOS/MS-DOS環境全般で動く実装を提供することが目指された。
summary: MS-DOS PC全盛期に広く使われたBASIC処理系。QuickBASIC・QBasicの直接の前身。
problem_en: Early IBM PCs came with Cassette BASIC burned into ROM or the disk-based BASICA (made by IBM), but these depended on ROM built into IBM hardware and could not run as-is on third-party PC/AT compatible machines. Microsoft developed GW-BASIC as an independent BASIC implementation that did not depend on ROM and worked entirely from disk, maintaining high compatibility with existing BASICA programs while making it possible to distribute it widely across the PC-DOS/MS-DOS environment as a whole.
summary_en: GW-BASIC is now positioned as a historical language (status: historical) with almost no practical use today. However, the role it played during the PC boom of the 1980s was significant, and it occupies an important place in the history of programming education as the starting point of a lineage leading to QuickBASIC, QBasic, and Visual Basic.

name: QuickBASIC
problem: GW-BASICは行番号とGOTO文に依存した非構造的なプログラミングスタイルを強いており、大きなプログラムほど可読性・保守性が悪化した。MicrosoftはSUB/FUNCTIONによる構造化プログラミングを可能にし、さらにインタプリタだけでなくコンパイラも提供することで、実行速度と開発効率の両方を高めたいと考えた。
summary: 構造化プログラミングとコンパイラを提供したMicrosoft製BASIC。Visual Basicの直接の前身。
problem_en: GW-BASIC depended heavily on line numbers and GOTO statements, which meant that as programs grew larger, it became increasingly hard to follow the flow of execution—the "spaghetti code" problem. It was also an interpreter only, limiting execution speed. Microsoft developed QuickBASIC to enable structured programming via SUB/FUNCTION, to allow programs to be written without line numbers, and to raise both ease of development and execution speed by providing a compiler in addition to the interpreter.
summary_en: QuickBASIC is now positioned as a historical language (status: historical). It is remembered as an important branch point in the BASIC lineage, having given rise to two distinct directions—a lightweight educational version (QBasic) and a commercial visual development environment (Visual Basic).

name: QBasic
problem: MicrosoftはGW-BASICを置き換える、MS-DOSに無償で標準同梱できる学習・実行環境を必要としていた。QuickBASIC 4.5からコンパイラとリンカを取り除き、インタプリタ機能だけに絞ることで、誰でもすぐ使える軽量なBASIC環境を実現した。
summary: MS-DOSに標準搭載された教育用BASIC処理系。多くのユーザーの入門言語となった。
problem_en: Microsoft needed to replace GW-BASIC, which had been bundled standard with MS-DOS, but could not simply distribute the commercial QuickBASIC for free. So it stripped the compiler and linker functionality out of QuickBASIC 4.5, developing QBasic as a lightweight implementation limited to interpreter functionality, and bundled it free of charge as a standard part of MS-DOS 5.0 and later, providing an environment where anyone could immediately start learning to program.
summary_en: It is now positioned as a legacy language (status: legacy) with essentially no practical use, but it is still remembered fondly by the generation who learned programming on MS-DOS PCs in the 1990s as the first programming language they ever touched.

name: ABC
problem: BASICやPascal、AWKなど当時の教育用・実務用言語の煩雑さを解消し、初心者でも直感的に扱える高水準言語を作りたかった。変数宣言を省略し、インデントによるブロック構造や無制限精度演算を導入することで、Pascalの4分の1程度の行数で同等のプログラムが書けることを目指した。CWIでの長年の研究を経て、後にPythonの設計に大きな影響を与えることになる。
summary: 教育とプロトタイピングを目的に設計され、後のPythonに大きな影響を与えたインタラクティブな高水準言語。
problem_en: In the 1980s, educational and practical languages such as BASIC, Pascal, and AWK had many cumbersome syntactic constraints that made it hard for beginners to focus on the essence of programming. After years of research at CWI (the Dutch national research institute for mathematics and computer science), ABC's developers aimed to let programmers write equivalent programs in roughly a quarter of the lines Pascal would need, by adopting mechanisms such as omitting variable declarations, using indentation for block structure, and unlimited-precision numeric arithmetic. Their biggest goal was to create a high-level language that could be used intuitively even by people who were not professional programmers. Notably, it was designed not merely as an educational toy but as a prototyping language robust enough for practical work. This design philosophy would later have a major influence on the birth of Python.
summary_en: Positioned as historical (a language that has finished its historical role). ABC itself is no longer widely used, but its design philosophy lives on today in the form of Python.

name: CLU
problem: 大規模なソフトウェアシステムの複雑さを管理するため、データ抽象化の理論を実用的な言語機能として実現したかった。「クラスタ」という仕組みでデータ表現と操作を一体化し、抽象データ型・イテレータ・例外処理・パラメトリックな型を一つの言語に統合することを目指した。継承こそ持たなかったものの、その設計はのちのオブジェクト指向言語やジェネリクスの基礎を築いた。
summary: 抽象データ型とクラスタの概念を確立し、後のオブジェクト指向・ジェネリクス設計に大きな影響を与えた先駆的言語。
problem_en: In the mid-1970s, as large-scale software systems grew more complex, none of the languages of the day offered "data abstraction" theory as a practical feature. The CLU development team at MIT devised a mechanism called the "cluster," which unified a data's internal representation with the procedures that operate on it, aiming to integrate abstract data types, iterators, exception handling, and parametric types (generics) into a single language system. Although it lacked an inheritance mechanism, it sought to improve the maintainability and reliability of large programs through thorough modularity and encapsulation. This design would go on to lay the theoretical groundwork for later object-oriented languages and generics.
summary_en: CLU is regarded as historical (a language that has finished its historical role). CLU itself is no longer used in practice, but the concepts of abstract data types, iterators, and exception handling are deeply rooted in today's major languages.

name: Mesa
problem: Xerox PARCのAltoワークステーション向けに、強い型付けと分割コンパイルが可能なシステム記述言語を作りたかった。Pascal譲りの構文にインタフェースと実装を分離するモジュール機構、モニタによる並行処理、例外処理機構を組み込み、大規模なシステムソフトウェアを堅牢に開発できることを目指した。その設計思想は後継のCedarやModula-2、さらにはJavaにまで受け継がれた。
summary: Xerox PARCで生まれた、モジュールと例外処理・並行制御を備える先駆的なシステム記述言語。
problem_en: In the 1970s, Xerox PARC needed a strongly typed language supporting separate compilation in order to develop advanced system software for the Alto workstation. The Mesa development team built on Pascal's clear syntax as a foundation while incorporating a module mechanism that separated interface from implementation, concurrency control via monitors, and an exception-handling mechanism, aiming for a language that could robustly build large-scale system software. A distinctive feature was that it was an "engineering language" for multiple developers collaborating to build a massive system, rather than for a single programmer. This design philosophy was carried forward into its successor Cedar and into Modula-2, and even, more distantly, into Java.
summary_en: It is positioned as historical (a language whose historical role has ended). It was used only internally at Xerox PARC and never achieved widespread adoption, but its design around modules, exception handling, and concurrency control left a strong influence on later languages such as Modula-2 and Java.

name: Newsqueak
problem: マウスやキーボードなど複数の入力デバイスと同時にやり取りするグラフィカルユーザインタフェースを、自然に記述できる言語を作りたかった。HoareのCSP理論をもとに、チャネルを第一級オブジェクトとして扱うことで、変数への格納や関数間の受け渡しを可能にし、並行処理をより柔軟に表現できるようにした。この設計は後にAlef、Limbo、そしてGoの並行処理モデルへと受け継がれていく。
summary: チャネルを第一級オブジェクトとして扱う並行処理モデルを確立し、Go言語の設計にまで連なる源流となった言語。
problem_en: In the late 1980s, there was a need for a language that could naturally express a graphical user interface interacting simultaneously with multiple input devices such as a mouse and keyboard. Building on Hoare's CSP (Communicating Sequential Processes) theory, Newsqueak's developers treated channels as first-class objects, making them possible to store in variables and pass between functions, allowing concurrency to be expressed more flexibly. Rather than remaining a purely theoretical experiment, the project sought a practical concurrency model for writing actual GUI programs. This design later carried forward into Alef, Limbo, and eventually the Go language's concurrency model.
summary_en: Newsqueak is positioned as historical (a language that has finished its historical role). Newsqueak itself was never used in practice, but its channel-based concurrency model has been carried forward into the present day via Alef and Limbo, ultimately arriving in the widely used Go language.

name: Limbo
problem: 組み込み機器上で動作する分散OS「Inferno」のために、ネットワーク越しの分散システムを安全かつ簡潔に記述できる言語を作りたかった。Alefのチャネルベース並行モデルを引き継ぎつつ、ガベージコレクションを備えた仮想マシン(Dis)上で動作させることで、移植性とメモリ安全性を両立させることを目指した。
summary: Inferno OS向けに設計された、チャネルベースの並行処理とガベージコレクションを備える分散システム記述言語。
problem_en: In the mid-1990s, a language was needed that could describe distributed systems over a network safely and concisely for "Inferno," a distributed operating system intended to run on embedded devices. Limbo carried forward Alef's channel-based concurrency model while running on a garbage-collected virtual machine (Dis), aiming to achieve both portability and memory safety. It also aimed to resolve the cumbersome memory management and the difficulty of porting to multiple architectures that had plagued Alef. The overarching goal was to be able to write system software that runs safely across heterogeneous networked environments.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). It continues to be used alongside Inferno OS in some embedded and research applications, but has not achieved widespread adoption.

name: Alef
problem: Plan 9オペレーティングシステム向けに、Newsqueakが持つチャネルベースの並行処理モデルを、C言語のようなコンパイル型言語で実現したかった。procとtaskという二種類の並行実行単位を用意し、実用的なシステムプログラミングに耐える性能を確保しようとした。しかしガベージコレクションを持たず複数アーキテクチャでの保守が困難だったため、最終的にPlan 9第3版までに放棄された。
summary: Plan 9のために作られた、チャネルベース並行処理をコンパイル型言語で実現しようとしたが後に放棄された言語。
problem_en: In the early 1990s, during the development of the Plan 9 operating system, there was a need to realize the channel-based concurrency model of Newsqueak in a compiled language like C. Alef provided two kinds of concurrent execution units, proc (process) and task (a lightweight unit of execution), and sought to secure execution performance robust enough for practical systems programming. Whereas Newsqueak had an interpreter-like execution environment, Alef aimed for speed usable even as an internal OS component by compiling to native code. However, the lack of garbage collection made memory management cumbersome, and maintaining it across multiple architectures also became difficult.
summary_en: It is positioned as historical (a language whose historical role has ended). Due to the lack of garbage collection and portability issues, the language itself was abandoned by Plan 9's third edition, handing its role over to its successor, Limbo.

name: Sather
problem: 1990年当時、オブジェクト指向言語Eiffelの設計思想には共感しつつも、その実装系の実行性能の低さに不満を持っていた。効率的なコンパイルによりC言語並みの実行速度を実現しながら、契約による設計や反復子、パラメータ化された型を備えたオブジェクト指向言語を作りたかった。あわせてガベージコレクションによる安全なメモリ管理も両立させたかった。
summary: Eiffelの思想を受け継ぎつつ実行性能を追求した、ICSIバークレー発のオブジェクト指向言語。
problem_en: In 1990, many researchers strongly sympathized with the ideas behind the object-oriented language Eiffel, such as design by contract and iterators, yet were dissatisfied with the low execution performance of its implementations. At ICSI Berkeley, Sather aimed to create an object-oriented language that, through efficient compilation, achieved execution speed comparable to C while still offering design by contract, iterators, and parameterized types (generics). It is notable for also pursuing safe memory management via garbage collection alongside this, aiming for a language that satisfied both performance and safety simultaneously. The name "Sather" comes from Sather Tower at the University of California, Berkeley.
summary_en: Sather is classified as historical, a language whose historical role has ended. It earned a certain amount of recognition as an academic experimental language but never achieved widespread practical use, and today it is mainly referenced in the context of language design research.

name: Hope
problem: 1980年当時、代入文のような副作用を排除し、数学的に明快で操作しやすいプログラムを書ける、シンプルな関数型言語を作りたかった。パターンマッチによる関数定義と代数的データ型という新しい概念を導入し、多相型やオーバーロードを扱える強い型システムを備えた実験的な言語を目指した。後のMirandaやHaskellにも通じる考え方を先取りしたいという狙いもあった。
summary: パターンマッチと代数的データ型を初めて導入した、エディンバラ大学発の実験的関数型言語。
problem_en: In 1980, there was a demand for a simple functional language that could eliminate side effects such as assignment statements and allow programs to be written and manipulated in a mathematically clear way. The Hope development team at the University of Edinburgh aimed to create an experimental language that introduced the new concepts of function definition through pattern matching and algebraic data types, equipped with a strong type system capable of handling polymorphism and overloading. Unlike existing dynamically typed functional languages such as Lisp, it was distinctive in trying to combine static typing with mathematical clarity. There was also an ambition to anticipate ideas that would later be seen in Miranda and Haskell.
summary_en: Hope is positioned as historical (a language whose historical role has ended). Hope itself is no longer used in practice, but the concepts of pattern matching and algebraic data types have become standard features of modern functional languages.

name: Interlisp
problem: 1960年代後半、AI研究者が試行錯誤しながら効率よくプログラムを書けるよう、Lisp処理系にデバッガやエラー自動修正機能(DWIM)、操作履歴管理などを統合した対話的な開発環境を作りたかった。単なる言語仕様にとどまらず、研究者の生産性を高める統合プログラミング環境そのものを提供したかった。BBN LISPを土台に、Xerox PARCでさらに洗練させることを目指した。
summary: DWIMなど先進的な開発支援機能を備えた、AI研究向けLispの統合プログラミング環境。
problem_en: In the late 1960s, in order to let AI researchers write programs efficiently through trial and error, there was a need for an interactive development environment that integrated a debugger, automatic error correction, and operation-history management into a Lisp processing system. Building on BBN LISP and refining it further at Xerox PARC, Interlisp aimed to provide not merely a language specification but an integrated programming environment that would itself raise researchers' productivity. In particular, the automatic error-correction feature known as DWIM (Do What I Mean) was an advanced idea in which the processing system automatically guessed and corrected typos and minor mistakes. Its greatest aim was to speed up the cycle of trial and error in AI research.
summary_en: Interlisp is positioned as historical (a language that has finished its historical role). Interlisp itself has fallen out of use, but the ideas of an interactive debugging environment and automatic error correction are valued as forerunners of the modern integrated development environment (IDE).

name: Maclisp
problem: 1966年当時、MITのProject MACにおいて、Lisp 1.5の連想リスト探索に頼る遅い変数アクセスを改善し、より高速に動作するLisp処理系を作りたかった。可変長引数を取る関数やマクロ、配列、非局所脱出、高速な数値演算など実用的な機能を備え、大規模なAIプログラムの開発に耐える実行速度を実現したかった。
summary: MITで開発された、実行速度と実用機能を重視した初期の代表的Lisp処理系。
problem_en: In 1966, within MIT's Project MAC, there was a need for a faster Lisp implementation that would resolve the problem of slow variable access caused by Lisp 1.5's reliance on association-list lookup. By providing practical features such as functions and macros that take variable-length arguments, arrays, non-local exits, and fast numeric operations, Maclisp aimed to achieve execution speeds that could withstand the demands of developing large-scale AI programs. What is notable is that rather than being merely a theoretical implementation, it was polished into a practical tool actually used at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. It was ported to multiple machine architectures over many years and was an especially influential presence among early Lisp implementations.
summary_en: Maclisp is positioned as historical (a language that has finished its historical role). Maclisp itself is no longer used, but as an early Lisp implementation it carries historical significance for having influenced many later Lisp dialects.

name: SIMSCRIPT
problem: 1962年当時、RAND Corporationにおいて、大規模な離散事象シミュレーションを、英語に近い自由形式の記述で誰でも構築・保守できるようにしたかった。Fortran上に構築したプリプロセッサとして実装することで、構造化されモジュール化されたシミュレーションモデルを効率よく記述できる専用言語を作りたかった。
summary: 英語的な記述で離散事象シミュレーションを記述できる、RAND研究所発のシミュレーション言語。
problem_en: In 1962 at the RAND Corporation, there was a demand for a way to let anyone build and maintain large-scale discrete-event simulations using free-form descriptions close to English. SIMSCRIPT was implemented as a preprocessor built on top of Fortran, aiming to be a dedicated language that could efficiently describe structured, modularized simulation models. It represented system state using the concepts of entities, attributes, and sets, and built programs around the occurrence of events over time, a design that became a precursor of event-driven simulation. It is also known for having Harry Markowitz, the Nobel laureate economist famous for his work in financial engineering, involved in its design.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). While in modern times it has ceded its role to its successor, SIMSCRIPT II, and to other simulation-specific languages and tools, it is still referenced in some simulation fields today.

name: IPL
problem: 1956年当時、コンピュータに記号処理やリスト操作を行わせ、定理証明などの人工知能的な問題解決を実現したかった。数値計算中心だった既存の手法では扱えなかった、動的なメモリ割り当てやリスト構造、再帰、関数を引数として渡す機能などを、アセンブリ言語に近い低レベルの記述で実現したかった。
summary: 記号処理とリスト操作を可能にした、人工知能研究の出発点となった最初期の言語。
problem_en: In 1956, there was an ambitious goal of having computers perform symbolic processing and list manipulation to achieve artificial-intelligence-like problem solving, such as theorem proving. The designers of IPL (Information Processing Language) sought to realize, at a level of description close to assembly language, capabilities that existing numerically-focused methods could not handle — dynamic memory allocation, list structures, recursion, and passing functions as arguments. "Logic Theorist," actually developed using IPL, is known as a pioneer of automated theorem proving by computer and became one of the starting points of artificial intelligence research. Its greatest significance lies in having pioneered, at a remarkably advanced level for its time, the concepts of symbolic processing and list structures.
summary_en: It is positioned as historical (a language whose historical role has ended). IPL itself is no longer used, but as the earliest language that served as the starting point of artificial intelligence research, it holds an important place in the history of computer science.

name: EuLisp
problem: Common Lispのように過去の設計に縛られすぎず、かといってSchemeほど最小主義的でもないLispをヨーロッパの産学コミュニティで標準化したかった。オブジェクト指向をLispに深く統合し、組み込み機器や教育用途にも段階的に展開できる階層構造の言語を作りたかった。
summary: オブジェクト指向を統合しつつ組み込み用途にも対応できるよう欧州で標準化されたLisp方言。
problem_en: As of 1990, there was a desire within the European academic and industrial community to standardize a Lisp that was neither too heavily bound by Common Lisp's past design decisions nor as minimalist as Scheme. EuLisp aimed to deeply integrate object orientation into Lisp and to create a hierarchically structured language that could scale down to embedded devices and up to educational use. What stands out is its adoption of a hierarchical module structure that builds up features from level 0 to level 1, rather than a single monolithic specification, allowing flexible implementation depending on the use case. It was an international collaborative project in which multiple European research institutions worked together on the standardization.
summary_en: EuLisp is positioned as a niche language used in specific fields. It never achieved widespread adoption, but it continues to be referenced in the context of European language design research.

name: SCM
problem: R4RSやR5RSなどのScheme標準に準拠しつつ、C言語で実装することで幅広い環境に移植できる実用的なScheme処理系を作りたかった。Scheme-to-Cコンパイラやリンク可能なモジュールなど、実務での使いやすさも両立させたかった。
summary: 移植性と標準準拠を重視したC言語実装のScheme処理系。
problem_en: In 1990, there was a demand for a practical Scheme implementation that conformed to Scheme standards such as R4RS and R5RS while also being portable to a wide range of environments by being implemented in C. SCM adopted a design that emphasized practical usability, including a Scheme-to-C compiler and linkable modules, aiming for a robust implementation that would run on diverse platforms. What was distinctive was its attempt to simultaneously satisfy two often-conflicting requirements: standard conformance and portability. Its designer, Aubrey Jaffer, was also deeply involved in Scheme standardization efforts, and SCM was long referenced as a faithful implementation of the standard.
summary_en: SCM is positioned as an active language, in wide and current use. While SCM itself is not particularly well known as a major implementation, it continues to be used in some environments as a standard-conformant Scheme implementation.

name: JOSS
problem: RAND研究所において、専門のプログラマーを介さずに数学者やアナリストが自ら計算機と対話しながら問題を解けるようにしたかった。タイムシェアリング環境で複数のユーザーが同時に会話形式で計算機を使える、訓練なしでも自然に使える仕組みを作りたかった。
summary: 対話的な会話形式での問題解決を目指した初期のタイムシェアリング型言語。
problem_en: At RAND Corporation in 1963, there was a demand for mathematicians and analysts to be able to solve problems by conversing directly with a computer, without going through a dedicated programmer. JOSS (JOHNNIAC Open Shop System) aimed for a mechanism, in a time-sharing environment, that would let multiple users use the computer conversationally at the same time, in a way that felt natural even without training. At a time when batch processing was the norm, an interactive response model in which computation results came back immediately after user input was groundbreaking, and it became a forerunner of later time-sharing systems and interactive languages. It is also known for having been created by Cliff Shaw, who also designed IPL.
summary_en: It is positioned as historical (a language whose historical role has ended). JOSS itself is no longer used, but it holds a place in the history of computer science as an important early language that pioneered the idea of interactive computer use.

name: FLOW-MATIC
problem: 数学記号に不慣れなビジネス分野の経営者や事務担当者でも扱える、英語に近い単語でデータ処理を記述できる言語を作りたかった。データの定義と処理手順を明確に分離することで、事務処理プログラムをより分かりやすく書けるようにしたかった。
summary: 英語に近いキーワードで事務処理を記述した初期の言語で、後のCOBOLの原型となった。
problem_en: In 1955, there was a demand for a language that could describe data processing in words close to English, so that business executives and clerical staff unfamiliar with mathematical notation could use it. FLOW-MATIC aimed to make business-processing programs easier to understand by clearly separating the definition of data from the processing procedure. Its designer, Grace Hopper, held a strong conviction that programs should not belong only to mathematicians, but should be close to a natural language that executives and clerical workers could also understand, and that philosophy runs through the entire design of this language. This attempt would go on to directly influence the design of COBOL.
summary_en: Positioned as historical (a language that has finished its historical role). FLOW-MATIC itself is no longer used, but it occupies an important place in the history of computer science as the prototype from which COBOL was derived.

name: ALGOL 58
problem: 1950年代後半、各国・各メーカーごとにばらばらだった科学技術計算用言語を統一し、機種に依存せずアルゴリズムを記述・発表できる「万国共通の言語」を作りたかった。当初IAL(International Algebraic Language)と呼ばれ、ヨーロッパのGAMMとアメリカのACMが共同で設計した最初の国際標準化言語である。
summary: ヨーロッパと米国の合同委員会が設計した最初の国際標準アルゴリズム記述言語で、ALGOL 60の直接の前身となった。
problem_en: In the late 1950s, as computer use spread across different countries and manufacturers, the languages for describing algorithms had also splintered, each machine having its own. This meant that not only was it difficult to port a program written for one computer to another, there was also no common notation for presenting algorithms in academic papers. Europe's GAMM (Society for Applied Mathematics and Mechanics) and America's ACM formed a joint committee to create a "universal language" that could describe and publish scientific and technical computing algorithms independently of any particular machine. Initially called IAL (International Algebraic Language), it built on the practical success of Fortran while aiming for a more mathematical and rigorous notation. This effort was groundbreaking as the first programming language designed through international agreement.
summary_en: ALGOL 58 is historical (a language that has finished its historical role) and was never widely used in practice. However, as the source, via ALGOL 60, of many procedural languages, it is regarded as an important milestone in the history of programming languages.

name: ALGOL W
problem: ALGOL 60の実用上の不足点を補い、文字列型・レコード参照・while文などを加えたより簡潔で実用的な改良版を作りたかった。より野心的なALGOL 68案が採択される中、堅実な改良路線として独自に発展させたかった。
summary: ALGOL 60を実用面で拡張した言語で、Pascalの直接の前身となった。
problem_en: ALGOL 60 was an excellent language specification, but it still left much to be desired in practice, including the lack of a string type, awkward handling of record references, and insufficient looping control. In the international standardization process, the trend was moving toward adopting the more ambitious and complex ALGOL 68 proposal, but Wirth and Hoare independently sought to create a solid, easy-to-implement improved version instead. ALGOL W built on ALGOL 60 while adding practical features such as a string type, records (references), and while statements, aiming for an algorithm-description language that suppressed complexity while still standing up to practical use.
summary_en: It is historical (a language whose historical role has ended) and is not used in practice today. It is remembered as a language representing the transitional stage from ALGOL 60 to Pascal in efforts to make ALGOL-family languages more practical.

name: Modula
problem: Wirthは、Pascalに大規模プログラムを整理して管理する仕組みが欠けていると考え、関連する宣言をひとまとめにできるモジュール機構を導入したいと考えた。あわせて、複数のプロセスを安全に並行実行できる「マルチプログラミング」を言語レベルで記述できるようにすることも目指した。この成果は後継のModula-2に引き継がれていった。
summary: Pascalにモジュールと並行処理機能を加えたWirthの言語で、Modula-2の前身となった。
problem_en: Wirth, the designer of Pascal, realized while actually building large-scale programs that Pascal itself lacked mechanisms for organizing and managing large programs. There was no way to bundle related types, variables, and procedures together and hide them from the outside, so programs became harder to keep track of as they grew larger. Wirth wanted to introduce a "module" mechanism into Pascal that could bundle related declarations together as a single unit. He also wanted the language itself to support the concept of "multiprogramming," safely executing multiple processes concurrently, in order to meet the growing needs of concurrency and real-time control that were emerging at the time.
summary_en: Modula is historical (a language that has finished its historical role), and is not used on its own today. However, its ideas of a module mechanism and concurrency were carried directly into its successor, Modula-2, leaving a major mark on the design of subsequent structured programming languages.

name: Euclid
problem: DARPAとカナダ国防省の支援のもと、プログラムの正しさを形式的に検証できる「検証可能なプログラム」を書くための言語を作りたいという動機で開発された。Pascalをベースにしつつ、検証を妨げるあいまいな機能を取り除き、安全性の高いシステムプログラミングを実現することを目指した。
summary: 形式的検証を前提に設計された、Pascal系の安全性重視システムプログラミング言語。
problem_en: In the 1970s, DARPA (the U.S. Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency) and Canada's Department of National Defence needed a language for writing "verifiable programs," ones for which it could be mathematically proven that the written program truly behaved according to its specification. Languages like Pascal at the time were expressive, but carried many ambiguous features—such as pointer aliasing and mixed side effects—that made formal verification difficult. Lampson and colleagues therefore sought to design a systems programming language, built on top of Pascal, that deliberately removed features that hindered verification, prioritizing safety and verifiability above all else. Use in settings requiring high reliability, such as military and defense systems, was kept in mind.
summary_en: It is historical (a language whose historical role has ended) and is not used in practice today. It stands as an early attempt at programming language design premised on formal verification, and is referenced within the history of programming language research.

name: Cedar
problem: Xerox PARCの研究者たちは、Mesaの静的な型システムや手動でのメモリ管理の煩雑さを解消し、対話的なプログラミング環境で快適に開発できる言語を作りたいと考えた。ガベージコレクションや動的型、文字列処理の強化などをMesaに加えることで、実験的なワークステーション向けソフトウェアをより生産的に開発できるようにすることを目指した。
summary: MesaにGCや動的型を加えた、Xerox PARCの実験的な統合プログラミング環境向け言語。
problem_en: Researchers at Xerox PARC who continued to use Mesa came to feel that its static type system and manual memory management were too cumbersome for an experimental, interactive programming environment. In a workstation environment where people wanted to quickly try out new ideas, having to strictly fix types and worry about freeing memory each time got in the way of productivity. Morris and Teitelman therefore set out to build a language on top of Mesa that incorporated garbage collection, dynamic typing, and enhanced string handling, so that it could be used comfortably within an interactive development environment. The name Cedar comes from the image of a new branch growing on the existing tree that is Mesa.
summary_en: It is historical (a language whose historical role has ended) and is not used today. It is referenced in the history of research on GUI and garbage collection practicality, as an experiment in interactive programming environments at Xerox PARC.

name: TMG
problem: 1960年代初頭、コンパイラを一から手作業で書く作業は煩雑で誤りが生じやすかったため、McClureは構文規則を宣言的に記述するだけでコンパイラを自動生成できるツールを作りたいと考えた。再帰下降とバックトラックによる構文解析の仕組みは、後にUnix上でBやPL/Iの初期版(EPL)を開発する際にも用いられた。
summary: 構文規則の記述からコンパイラを自動生成する、初期のコンパイラコンパイラ言語。
problem_en: In the early 1960s, writing a compiler entirely by hand was a very laborious task; even the parsing portion alone took a great deal of time and effort and was prone to errors. McClure wanted to create a tool that could automatically generate a parser (and by extension a compiler) that worked correctly simply from a declarative description of the grammar rules. TMG (short for "Transmogrifier," meaning something that transforms) built the mechanism of recursive-descent parsing with backtracking directly into the language processor itself, becoming an early pioneer of what is now called a "compiler-compiler," generating a program from a description of grammar rules.
summary_en: TMG is historical, a language whose historical role has ended, and it is no longer used today. It is referenced in the history of compiler technology as an early implementation of the concept of a compiler-compiler.

name: CPL
problem: ALGOL 60が科学技術計算に特化しすぎていたため、Stracheyらは産業プロセス制御や事務処理から低水準のシステム記述まで幅広い用途に対応できる、より汎用的な言語を作りたいと考えた。しかし仕様が野心的で肥大化しすぎ、完全なコンパイラの実装には至らないまま終わった。
summary: ALGOL 60を汎用化しようとした大規模言語仕様で、後のBCPLやCの源流となった。
problem_en: ALGOL 60 had beautiful syntax and a rigorous specification, but its design was too specialized for scientific and technical computing to adequately cover industrial process control, business data processing, or even low-level system description. Strachey and Barron tried to build on top of ALGOL 60 to create a general-purpose language (the Combined Programming Language, or CPL for short) capable of handling every use case. However, in trying to cram far too many features into a single language — from high-level abstraction down to low-level bit manipulation — the specification became too vast and complex, and the project ended up as an unrealized concept without ever reaching a complete compiler implementation.
summary_en: CPL is historical (a language whose historical role has ended), and since no complete compiler was ever implemented, it was never actually used in practice. However, it occupies an important place in the history of programming languages as the starting point of the lineage running through BCPL, B, and C — the modern system programming languages.

name: Boo
problem: de Oliveiraは、.NETのCommon Language Infrastructureが持つUnicode対応や国際化、Webアプリケーション機能を活かしつつ、Pythonのような読みやすい構文で書ける静的型付け言語を作りたいと考えた。コンパイラやマクロによる拡張性を重視し、クロージャやジェネレータといった関数型的な機能も取り込んだ。
summary: .NET向けにPython風の構文と静的型付けを組み合わせた言語で、Unityのスクリプト言語としても使われた。
problem_en: The .NET Common Language Infrastructure (CLI) had strong Unicode support, internationalization, and a rich set of libraries for web applications, but the main languages used on it, such as C# and VB.NET, could hardly be described as having syntax as concise and readable as Python's. De Oliveira wanted to create a statically typed language that could make full use of the capabilities of the .NET platform while being written in a readable, Python-like indentation-based syntax. He also made the language itself flexibly extensible through compiler extension mechanisms (compiler steps and macros), and actively incorporated functional features such as closures and generators.
summary_en: Boo is positioned as niche (a language used in specific fields), and although it was once used as one of the scripting language options for the Unity engine, its use is now confined to a limited community.

name: Brook
problem: GPUが持つ高い並列演算性能をグラフィックス描画以外の汎用計算(GPGPU)に活用したかった。C言語をストリームプログラミングの考え方で拡張し、カーネル関数とデータストリームという抽象化によって、OpenGLやDirectXなどのグラフィックスAPIを意識せずにGPU向けの並列コードを書けるようにしたかった。
summary: StanfordのGPGPU研究から生まれた、C言語を拡張したストリーム指向のGPUプログラミング言語。
problem_en: In the early 2000s, GPUs were rapidly increasing their computational performance, but their parallel computing power could be used almost exclusively for graphics rendering. Buck and Hanrahan wanted to harness this high parallel computing performance for general-purpose computation (GPGPU) beyond graphics. At the time, performing computation on a GPU required forcibly repurposing the mechanisms of graphics APIs such as OpenGL or DirectX, which was a high barrier for programmers without specialized knowledge. They therefore extended the C language with the concept of stream programming, introducing the abstractions of "kernel functions" and "data streams" so that parallel code for the GPU could be written directly without having to be conscious of the graphics APIs.
summary_en: Brook is historical (a language that has finished its historical role) and is not used in current development. It was superseded by later GPGPU technologies such as CUDA and OpenCL, but it is remembered as pioneering research that opened up the idea of general-purpose computation using the GPU.

name: GLSL
problem: OpenGLにおけるシェーダ記述を、当時主流だった低レベルなアセンブリ形式のシェーダ言語から解放し、C言語に似た高水準の構文で直感的に書けるようにしたかった。オープン標準であるOpenGLの利点を保ちながら、頂点・フラグメント処理をプログラマブルに記述できる仕組みを提供したかった。
summary: OpenGL向けに標準化された、C言語ライクな高水準GPUシェーディング言語。
problem_en: In early-2000s OpenGL, working with shaders (the mechanism for programming per-vertex and per-pixel rendering processes) required writing low-level assembly-style instruction sequences directly, and code aiming to achieve complex visual effects became extremely cumbersome and hard to maintain. Kessenich and others, working under the OpenGL ARB (the standards body), wanted to create a language that could describe shaders using a readable, high-level syntax similar to C. While preserving the advantages of OpenGL as an open standard, they aimed to open up shader programming to a much wider range of developers by providing a mechanism for describing vertex and pixel (fragment) processing intuitively and programmably.
summary_en: It is active (a language in current, wide use), and it continues to be widely used today as the standard shading language in real-time 3D graphics development using OpenGL, OpenGL ES, and WebGL.

name: Gosu
problem: 保険業務システムを開発するGuidewire社が、顧客企業がビジネスルールを安全かつ柔軟に記述できるスクリプト言語(GScript)を必要としたことから生まれたかった。JVM上で動作しJavaと高い相互運用性を持ちながら、静的型付けによる充実したコード補完・リファクタリング支援を実現したかった。
summary: Guidewireの保険業務システム向けに開発された、JVM上で動く静的型付け言語。
problem_en: Guidewire, a company developing systems for insurance operations, needed a scripting language that would let its insurance-company customers safely and flexibly customize their own business rules (such as premium calculation methods and underwriting conditions). This effort, which began as an in-house language called GScript, evolved into a language that ran on the JVM with high interoperability with Java assets, while also offering rich code completion and refactoring support through static typing. McKinney and colleagues focused on practicality and developer experience so that developers of business systems could confidently write and maintain large-scale business logic.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific domain), continuing to be used mainly for customizing Guidewire's insurance-operations systems.

name: Oz
problem: 論理型・関数型・オブジェクト指向・並行制約プログラミングといった複数のパラダイムを一つの言語の中で統一的に扱いたかった。プログラミング言語教育において、様々な計算モデルの本質的な違いと共通点を単一の処理系の上で学べるようにしたかった。
summary: 論理・関数・オブジェクト指向・並行処理を統合した教育志向のマルチパラダイム言語。
problem_en: Around 1990, the world of programming languages had a variety of paradigms — logic, functional, object-oriented, and concurrent — each existing as its own independent family of languages, without an adequate framework for understanding them in a unified way. Smolka wanted to integrate these multiple paradigms into a single language without contradiction, positioning them atop a single computational model (a concurrent computation model based on constraint programming). Furthermore, Oz was strongly conscious of educational purposes as well as research, aiming to let learners systematically understand the essential differences and commonalities among various computational models through a single implementation.
summary_en: Oz is a historical language (having completed its historical role) and is not widely used in practice today. However, its design philosophy of handling diverse paradigms atop a unified computational model continues to be referenced in programming language education and research.

name: Pizza
problem: 当時のJavaに欠けていたジェネリクス、関数(クロージャ)、代数的データ型、パターンマッチングといった関数型言語由来の機能を、Java仮想マシン上でJavaと完全互換の形で実現したかった。関数型プログラミングの理論的成果を実用的なオブジェクト指向言語に統合する実験をしたかった。
summary: Javaにジェネリクスや代数的データ型を持ち込んだ実験的な拡張言語で、後のScalaの原型となった。
problem_en: Java, in 1996, had only just appeared and was attracting attention, but it lacked features that had long been taken for granted in functional languages, such as generics (parameterized types), first-class functions (closures), algebraic data types, and pattern matching. Odersky and Wadler wondered whether these features derived from functional languages could be realized on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) while remaining fully compatible with Java. Pizza was designed as an experiment in integrating the results of type-theory research into a practical object-oriented language, while still being able to make direct use of existing Java bytecode and class libraries.
summary_en: Pizza is historical—a language whose historical role has ended—and it is not used today. It is remembered as the starting point of a lineage, as an experiment in integrating generics and functional features into Java, that led to Java's later introduction of generics and to the birth of Scala.

name: Whiley
problem: Tony Hoareが2003年に提唱した「検証コンパイラ」という課題に応え、形式検証を日常的かつ実用的に使えるプログラミング言語を一から設計したかった。既存言語の持つ検証のしづらさという弱点を避け、契約(事前条件・事後条件・不変条件)をコンパイラが自動的に検証できるようにしたかった。
summary: 形式検証を前提に設計された、契約による検証をコンパイラが行う実験的言語。
problem_en: In 2003, computer scientist Tony Hoare proposed the "verifying compiler" as a long-term challenge for programming language research: the goal of building a language implementation whose compiler could automatically verify that a program behaves correctly according to its specification. Pearce set out to meet this challenge head-on, designing a programming language from scratch that built in formal verification from the start as something to be used routinely and practically, rather than as a special add-on feature. He aimed to avoid the "hard to verify" weakness found in many existing languages, and to let the compiler automatically check contracts (preconditions, postconditions, and invariants).
summary_en: It is positioned as a niche language, used in fields such as formal verification and programming language research. It has not achieved adoption as a mainstream commercial language.

name: XPath
problem: XMLドキュメントの木構造から任意の要素や属性を条件指定で選び出す共通の記法が必要とされていた。XSLTやXPointerといった複数の関連仕様がそれぞれ独自の参照方法を持つのを避け、共通の構文とデータモデルを提供したかった。
summary: XML文書内のノードをpath式で選択するためのクエリ言語。
problem_en: As XML became widespread, a common notation was needed for selecting arbitrary nodes, under specified conditions, from the tree structure of an XML document (the hierarchy of elements, attributes, and text nodes). At the time, several related specifications, such as XSLT and XPointer, were each trying to define their own way of referencing nodes, and there was a risk that this would lead to a proliferation of similar-but-different notations across specifications. The W3C tried to unify this basic operation of node selection within XML documents by establishing a single path-expression language that these specifications could all share.
summary_en: Active (a language currently in wide use); it is still widely used today as the standard means for selecting nodes within XML documents, inside XSLT, XQuery, and the XML-processing libraries of various programming languages.

name: XSLT
problem: XML文書を別のXML、HTML、プレーンテキストなど任意の形式へ宣言的に変換したかった。SGML向けの変換言語DSSSLの考え方をXMLの世界に持ち込み、テンプレートとパターンマッチングでスタイル変換を記述できるようにしたかった。
summary: XML文書をテンプレートとパターンマッチングで別形式へ変換する宣言型言語。
problem_en: As XML documents began to spread, the need to transform an XML document into another XML format, into HTML, or into plain text, rapidly grew. The W3C and its lead designer, James Clark, brought the ideas of DSSSL (Document Style Semantics and Specification Language), which had handled style transformation for SGML documents, into the world of XML, and sought to build a declarative transformation mechanism based on templates and pattern matching. The aim was to let document transformations be described simply by mapping structural patterns on the input side to templates on the output side, without writing a program procedurally.
summary_en: XSLT is active (a language in wide, current use) and remains the standard for transforming XML documents. Its presence as a mainstream web technology has faded somewhat alongside the decline of XML usage itself, but it is still active in fields such as enterprise systems and document processing.

name: MUMPS
problem: マサチューセッツ総合病院での患者記録・検査情報管理を、極めて限られたハードウェア資源のタイムシェアリングシステム上で効率的に行いたかった。アセンブリ言語での開発に対する不満から、組み込みのデータベース機能を持つ簡潔な言語を作りたかった。
summary: 医療情報システム向けに階層データベースを内蔵した実用指向の言語。
problem_en: MUMPS (Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System) was created to manage patient records and test information at Massachusetts General Hospital. The time-sharing systems of the day had extremely limited memory and processing power, and within those constraints a mechanism was needed that would let multiple users access data simultaneously. Development in assembly language was unproductive, and the developers were dissatisfied with it. They therefore aimed to create a dedicated, concisely written language with hierarchical database functionality built in from the start. In responding to the special demands of the medical field, a unique design emerged in which the language itself and the data store were fused together.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). It is rarely used in general software development, but it remains actively in operation today as the foundation of medical information systems such as electronic health records, remaining indispensable in that field.

name: Fortress
problem: DARPAの高生産性コンピューティングシステム計画のもと、Fortranに代わる高性能科学技術計算言語を作りたかった。数式に近い記法や暗黙の並列実行を取り入れつつ、型安全性など現代的な言語機能も両立させたかった。
summary: 数式記法と暗黙の並列性を特徴とした科学技術計算向け言語(開発中止)。
problem_en: Fortress was developed as part of DARPA's High Productivity Computing Systems (HPCS) program, aiming to be a next-generation scientific computing language to succeed Fortran. It sought to let programs be written in notation close to mathematical formulas, directly reflecting the notation that mathematicians and scientists were already accustomed to. Anticipating an era in which parallel computing was becoming the hardware norm, the language's basic policy was for code to be executed in parallel implicitly, without explicit parallelization directives. It also incorporated modern language features such as type safety and generics, aiming to achieve both high performance and safety at once.
summary_en: Fortress is positioned as historical (a language that has finished its historical role). Development was discontinued by Sun (by then Oracle) in 2012, and the implementation was never completed. However, its ideas of implicit parallelism and mathematical notation remain a reference point in discussions on the design of later scientific computing languages.

name: A+
problem: APLを置き換え、金融分野の数値処理に特化した対話型の配列言語を作りたかった。グラフィカルユーザーインタフェース機能を組み込み、モルガン・スタンレー社内の高速な金融アプリケーション開発に対応したかった。
summary: 金融アプリケーション向けにAPLを拡張した対話型配列プログラミング言語。
problem_en: A+ was developed to replace APL, which had been used internally at the investment bank Morgan Stanley. APL was powerful for array-oriented numerical processing, but it was not well suited to interactive application development or building graphical user interfaces. A+ therefore aimed to retain the concise array operations inherited from APL while incorporating GUI components as a language feature, providing an environment for quickly developing and running financial applications. A defining characteristic is that it was designed with the expectation of actual use in the development of the company's high-speed trading systems and analysis tools.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). An open-source version has also been released, but use remains limited to a small group of enthusiasts and parts of the financial sector.

name: Clean
problem: 純粋関数型言語でありながら効率的なコード生成と副作用・入出力の扱いを両立させたかった。Haskellのようなモナドではなく一意型システムを導入することで、値の破壊的更新を安全に許可し実行効率を高めたかった。
summary: 一意型システムでI/Oと状態を扱う純粋関数型プログラミング言語。
problem_en: Clean was developed with the aim of preserving the mathematical beauty of pure functional programming while also achieving efficient code generation and practical handling of I/O and state. Handling side effects is a difficult problem in pure functional languages, and as an approach different from the monads adopted by Haskell, Clean introduced a uniqueness typing system. This mechanism guarantees at the type level that a value is referenced only once, aiming to allow safe destructive updates while improving execution efficiency. It began as a research language developed at Radboud University Nijmegen in the Netherlands.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). It continues to be used mainly for research and educational purposes, and retains its role as a reference point in theoretical research on functional languages.

name: Gofer
problem: 1990年代初頭、パソコン上でも動く軽量な処理系で関数型プログラミングを教育・研究したいという要望があった。フルスペックのHaskell処理系は当時のマシンには重すぎたため、Haskell 1.2相当のサブセットに型クラスなどの独自拡張を加えた小型インタプリタとして作られた。後継のHugsに開発が引き継がれ役目を終えた。
summary: 教育・研究向けに作られた軽量なHaskellサブセットのインタプリタ言語。
problem_en: Gofer was developed as a lightweight implementation that could run on personal computers of the early 1990s, in order to make functional programming teachable and researchable. Full-fledged Haskell implementations of the time were too heavy to be practical on ordinary personal computers. Mark P. Jones therefore designed a subset based on language specifications roughly equivalent to Haskell 1.2, adding his own extensions such as type classes, and implemented it as a small interpreter. It is notable for aiming to provide an environment where the advanced feature of type classes could be tried out even with limited computing resources.
summary_en: Gofer is classified as a historical language whose role has ended. Development was handed off to its successor implementation, Hugs, and development and use of Gofer itself have since ended.

name: Ballerina
problem: 従来のEAIやESBのような設定ファイル中心の統合ツールに代わり、サービス連携やAPI呼び出し、並行処理をコードとして自然に書きたいという動機から生まれた。ネットワーク通信やデータ交換をファーストクラスの言語機能として組み込み、クラウドネイティブな分散システム開発を容易にすることを目指した。
summary: クラウドネイティブな統合・分散システム開発のために設計された並行処理言語。
problem_en: Ballerina was developed out of a desire to naturally express service integration, API calls, and concurrency as code, replacing configuration-file-centric integration tools like traditional EAI (Enterprise Application Integration) and ESB (Enterprise Service Bus). Traditional tools favored visual integration through GUIs and XML configuration, but this approach suffered from declining maintainability as systems grew more complex and larger in scale. Ballerina therefore aimed to build elements of integration processing, such as network communication and data exchange, into the language as first-class features, supporting the development of cloud-native distributed systems at the level of the programming language itself.
summary_en: Ballerina is positioned as an active language, widely used today. Open-source development continues, led by WSO2, and adoption is growing in the fields of cloud-native API integration and microservice development.

name: Chapel
problem: HPC分野ではFortranやC/C++、MPIを組み合わせた並列プログラミングが複雑で生産性が低いという課題があった。アルゴリズムの記述と実装(データ分散・並列化)の詳細を分離し、Fortran/C系のHPC技術者とJavaやPythonに慣れた新世代の開発者双方にとって書きやすい言語を目指して開発された。
summary: HPC向けに生産性と並列表現力を両立させることを目指した次世代並列言語。
problem_en: Chapel was developed to address the problem that, in the field of HPC (high-performance computing), parallel programming combining Fortran or C/C++ with MPI was complex and offered low productivity. In conventional approaches, the description of the algorithm itself and the implementation details of data distribution and parallelization tended to become closely intertwined, making the code hard to follow. Chapel aimed to separate these two concerns, adopting a design that allows an algorithm to be expressed concisely while still permitting control over the details of parallel execution when needed. Another notable aim was to make the language easy to write for both HPC engineers accustomed to Fortran/C and a newer generation of developers accustomed to Java or Python.
summary_en: Chapel is positioned as active (a language that is currently in wide use). Development continues as open source, centered on Cray (now HPE), and it is used in the fields of scientific and technical computing and data-parallel processing on supercomputers.

name: X10
problem: DARPAのHigh Productivity Computing Systems構想のもと、ペタスケール級の超並列計算機を高い生産性で扱えるプログラミングモデルが求められていた。IBMはPGAS(分割グローバルアドレス空間)モデルとJava風のオブジェクト指向構文を組み合わせ、非同期タスクや分散データを自然に記述できる言語として設計した。
summary: IBMが開発したPGASモデルによる大規模並列計算向けオブジェクト指向言語。
problem_en: X10 was developed by IBM under DARPA's High Productivity Computing Systems (HPCS) initiative to realize a programming model that could handle petascale massively parallel computers with high productivity. Traditional parallel programming required dealing with low-level details in order to extract performance, which was a major barrier to productivity. X10 therefore adopted the PGAS (Partitioned Global Address Space) model and combined it with a Java-like object-oriented syntax, aiming to be a language that could naturally express asynchronous tasks and distributed data. Its goal was to make programming on large-scale parallel computers feel close to programming in an ordinary object-oriented language.
summary_en: X10 is positioned as a legacy language, maintained conservatively. Active development by IBM has already ended, and it is currently used only for limited research and maintenance purposes.

name: UPC
problem: 共有メモリ型並列計算の書きやすさと、メッセージパッシング型の分散メモリ計算が持つ性能・データ配置制御の両立が課題だった。既存のC拡張の長所を統合し、Cをベースに大規模並列マシン上でPGASモデルによるプログラミングを可能にすることを目指した。
summary: 共有メモリ的な視点で分散並列計算を記述できるCのPGAS拡張言語。
problem_en: UPC (Unified Parallel C) was developed to tackle the challenge of reconciling the ease of writing shared-memory parallel computation with the performance and data-placement control offered by message-passing distributed-memory computation. At the time, several different C language extensions had been proposed for parallel memory programming, but they were incompatible with one another and unstandardized. The UPC Consortium sought to integrate the strengths of these approaches, keeping the language based on C, to enable programming on large-scale parallel machines using the PGAS (Partitioned Global Address Space) model. Another goal was to let existing C programmers transition to parallel programming without a large learning cost.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). It continues to be used at some HPC research institutions and in legacy supercomputer environments, but its adoption in new development is limited.

name: ABAP
problem: 大企業の会計・資材管理などの基幹業務を扱うSAP R/2システム向けに、レポート作成や業務ロジックを効率よく記述できる専用言語が必要だった。データベース操作(SQL)と業務処理を統合的に書けるようにし、後にオブジェクト指向を取り込んで大規模ERPシステムの開発・保守性を高めることを目指した。
summary: SAPの基幹業務システム開発に特化したエンタープライズ向け言語。
problem_en: ABAP (Advanced Business Application Programming) was developed as a dedicated language for efficiently writing reports and business logic for the SAP R/2 system, which handled core operations such as accounting and materials management for large enterprises. In enterprise core systems, processing that generates reports from large volumes of database records plays a central role, but with general-purpose programming languages alone, integrating database operations with business processing tended to become cumbersome. ABAP was therefore designed as a language that could describe database operations (in syntax resembling SQL) and business processing logic in an integrated way. Object-oriented features were incorporated later, aiming to improve the development and maintainability of large-scale ERP systems.
summary_en: It is positioned as an active language, widely used today. Large enterprises around the world use SAP products as their core systems, and ABAP remains widely and indispensably used for their maintenance and customization.

name: SystemVerilog
problem: Verilogは大規模化するチップ設計や機能検証には表現力が不足しており、C++やJavaのようなオブジェクト指向機能を備えた高度な検証言語が求められていた。Co-Design AutomationのSuperlogを土台に、設計記述と機能検証を単一言語でカバーできるようにすることを目指した。
summary: Verilogにオブジェクト指向の検証機能を統合し、設計から検証まで扱えるようにしたハードウェア記述言語。
problem_en: SystemVerilog was developed to address the problem that conventional Verilog lacked sufficient expressive power for increasingly large and complex chip design and functional verification. In particular, the verification process demanded an advanced verification language with object-oriented features comparable to C++ or Java. Building on Co-Design Automation's Superlog language, SystemVerilog was extended under the leadership of Accellera (an industry standardization body), aiming to let a single language cover both hardware design description and functional verification. This sought to create an environment in which designers and verification engineers could collaborate on the same language foundation.
summary_en: SystemVerilog is positioned as an actively and widely used language (status: active). It has been standardized as an IEEE standard and continues to be widely used today as the standard language for design and functional verification in the semiconductor industry.

name: SystemC
problem: VHDLやVerilogによるRTL記述だけではハードウェアとソフトウェアの協調設計や上位レベルでのアーキテクチャ検討がしづらく、C++ベースでシステムレベルモデリングやトランザクションレベルモデリング(TLM)を行いたいという要求があった。複数のEDAベンダーが共同でC++クラスライブラリとして開発した。
summary: C++のクラスライブラリとしてハードウェアのシステムレベル設計・検証を可能にした言語。
problem_en: SystemC was developed to address the difficulty of hardware/software co-design and high-level architectural exploration using only RTL (register-transfer level) description in VHDL or Verilog. Conventional hardware description languages were strong at detailed structural description of circuits, but ill-suited to examining an entire system's architecture at a high level of abstraction or to flexibly handling the boundary between hardware and software. Multiple EDA vendors therefore jointly developed SystemC as a standard C++ class library, aiming to enable high-level system design, including transaction-level modeling (TLM).
summary_en: SystemC is positioned as an active language, in wide and current use. Standardized as an IEEE standard, it continues to be used today in the fields of high-level modeling for semiconductor design and hardware/software co-verification.

name: Chisel
problem: Verilog/VHDLでは再利用可能なハードウェアジェネレータを書く際の抽象化能力が乏しく、RISC-VベースのRocketチップのような複雑なプロセッサ設計を効率的に生成したいというニーズがあった。Scalaのオブジェクト指向・関数型機能を活用し、パラメータ化されたハードウェア記述を実現することを目指した。
summary: Scalaを土台にオブジェクト指向・関数型でハードウェアを生成的に記述できる言語。
problem_en: Chisel was developed at the University of California, Berkeley, to address the poor abstraction capabilities of Verilog and VHDL for writing reusable hardware generators. The background need was, in particular, to efficiently generate complex designs such as the RISC-V-based processor "Rocket Chip." Traditional hardware description languages made it difficult to generate parameterized modules or abstract higher-order designs, and large-scale processor designs tended to accumulate redundant code. Chisel was built on top of Scala's language features, aiming to achieve parameterized hardware description by leveraging the flexibility of Scala's object-oriented and functional programming.
summary_en: It is positioned as a niche language used in a specific field. It continues to be actively used in RISC-V processor research and development and in open-source hardware design.

name: LFE
problem: Erlang/BEAM上で堅牢な並行処理とフォールトトレラント性を保ちながら、Lisp流の強力なマクロシステムとホモイコニックな構文でメタプログラミングを行いたいという動機があった。Common LispやSchemeの伝統をErlang仮想マシン上に持ち込むことを目指した。
summary: Erlang仮想マシン上でLisp構文とマクロを使えるようにした関数型言語。
problem_en: LFE (Lisp Flavoured Erlang) was developed out of a desire to do metaprogramming with Lisp's powerful macro system and homoiconic syntax, while retaining robust concurrency and fault tolerance on the Erlang/BEAM virtual machine. Erlang excelled at concurrency and fault tolerance, but its syntax lacked the flexibility of Lisp-family languages, which treat code and data as one and the same. Robert Virding, himself a co-developer of Erlang, tried to combine the strengths of both by bringing the tradition of Lisps such as Common Lisp and Scheme onto the Erlang virtual machine.
summary_en: Positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). It continues to be used by a segment of the developer community interested in the Erlang ecosystem.

name: Terra
problem: 高性能計算向けのコードをLuaのような柔軟なスクリプト言語からメタプログラミングしつつ、C言語並みの実行性能を持つ低レベルコードを生成したいという課題があった。LLVMをバックエンドにJITコンパイルすることで、実行時コード生成と高速な数値計算を両立させることを目指した。
summary: Luaに埋め込んでメタプログラミングできる、C同等の性能を持つ低レベル言語。
problem_en: Terra was developed by researchers at Stanford University to address the challenge of metaprogramming high-performance computing code from a flexible scripting language like Lua while still generating low-level code with C-like execution performance. Traditionally, combining dynamic code generation with high execution efficiency was difficult, and there was a tradeoff between the flexibility of a scripting language and the performance of a statically compiled one. Terra was designed to be embedded within Lua, and by using JIT compilation with LLVM as its backend, it sought to achieve both runtime code generation and high-speed numerical computation at the same time.
summary_en: Terra is positioned as a niche language used in specific fields. It continues to be used mainly in research and parts of the graphics and numerical computing communities.

name: MoonScript
problem: Luaは軽量で高速な一方、クラス定義やリスト内包表記などの記述が冗長になりがちで、より快適に書ける構文が求められていた。CoffeeScriptのような簡潔な構文をLuaにコンパイルすることで、ゲーム開発などでの生産性を高めることを目指した。
summary: CoffeeScriptに着想を得た、Luaへコンパイルされる簡潔な構文のスクリプト言語。
problem_en: MoonScript was developed to address the fact that, while Lua is lightweight and fast, writing things like class definitions and list comprehensions in it tends to become somewhat verbose. Lua was widely used in fields such as game development and embedded scripting, but its basic syntax was somewhat inconvenient for writing modern language features concisely. MoonScript therefore adopted concise, readable syntax similar to CoffeeScript and compiled it into Lua code, aiming to improve development-time productivity while preserving Lua's execution efficiency. It was designed with particular attention to use in game development settings.
summary_en: It is positioned as niche (a language used in a specific field). It continues to be used steadily within part of the game-development community, but its range of use is limited.

name: Fennel
problem: Luaは高速で組み込みやすい一方、マクロなどメタプログラミング機能に乏しく、S式による柔軟な構文拡張ができないという課題があった。LuaのランタイムやFFIをそのまま活かしつつ、Lispの構文とマクロシステムを持つ軽量な代替言語を作りたかった。ゲーム開発や組み込み用途での実用性も重視された。
summary: LuaにコンパイルされるLisp方言で、Luaの速度とマクロの柔軟性を両立した言語。
problem_en: Lua is a fast and easily embeddable language, but it had the shortcoming of lacking metaprogramming features such as macros, and could not offer flexible syntactic extension via S-expressions. Fennel was designed as a lightweight alternative with Lisp's syntax and macro system, while still directly leveraging Lua's runtime and its rich FFI (foreign function interface). Practicality in domains where Lua is widely used, such as game development and embedded applications, is also emphasized. Because it compiles to Lua code, it can integrate seamlessly with the existing Lua ecosystem.
summary_en: Fennel is an actively used language, gaining particular support within the Lua-based game development community. It is chosen by developers who want to leverage the Lua ecosystem while also wanting the expressive power of Lisp-style macros.

name: GNU Prolog
problem: 商用処理系に頼らずネイティブコードを生成できる、フリーで高性能なProlog処理系が求められていた。ISO標準への準拠と、有限領域制約(FD)充足を統合することで、実用的な制約論理プログラミング環境を無償で提供したかった。
summary: 有限領域制約解消機能を備えたフリーのネイティブコードPrologコンパイラ。
problem_en: There was a demand for a high-performance Prolog implementation that could generate native code directly, without relying on commercial implementations. Many free Prolog implementations of the time remained bytecode interpreters, making it difficult to achieve execution speeds comparable to commercial products. GNU Prolog aimed to provide a practical constraint logic programming environment, free and open, by maintaining high conformance to the ISO Prolog standard while integrating finite-domain (FD) constraint satisfaction features. A defining characteristic is that, through native compilation, it sought to achieve performance viable not just for education but also for practical, real-world use.
summary_en: It is positioned as a niche language used in a specific field, and continues to be used as a Prolog implementation for constraint satisfaction problems and educational purposes. As a free alternative to commercial Prolog implementations, it retains a loyal user base.

name: Visual Prolog
problem: 従来のProlog(Turbo Prolog)は動的型付けでエラーが実行時まで発見しにくく、大規模な実用アプリケーション開発に不向きだった。強い静的型付けとオブジェクト指向をPrologに組み込み、Windows向けの本格的なGUIアプリケーションを開発できる商用環境を提供したかった。
summary: 強い静的型付けとオブジェクト指向を備えた商用Prolog開発環境。
problem_en: Conventional Prolog implementations, particularly Turbo Prolog, were dynamically typed, which meant errors were hard to catch until runtime, making them ill-suited for developing large-scale, practical applications. Visual Prolog sought to overcome this weakness by incorporating strong static typing and object-oriented concepts into Prolog. It further aimed to refine logic programming into a form applicable to practical software development by providing a commercial integrated development environment capable of building full-fledged GUI applications for Windows.
summary_en: It is positioned as a niche language used in a specific field. It continues to see steady use in areas such as enterprise business application development, and is still maintained and offered today as a commercial product by PDC.

name: Pharo
problem: Squeakは教育用途に特化しすぎており、商用・研究用の本格的なソフトウェア開発基盤としては機能過多かつ不安定な部分があった。Squeakからクリーンに分岐し、モジュール性が高くモダンな開発が可能な、オープンソースの次世代Smalltalk環境を作りたかった。
summary: Squeakから派生した、研究・産業用途向けのモダンなオープンソースSmalltalk。
problem_en: Squeak was overly specialized for educational use, and as a foundation for full-scale commercial or research software development it was either overloaded with unnecessary features or had issues with stability. Pharo aimed, by cleanly forking from Squeak, to create a highly modular, open-source next-generation Smalltalk environment able to withstand modern software development practices. It is notable for stripping away the educational elements and aiming to reconstruct a pure Smalltalk environment usable by researchers and professional developers on real projects.
summary_en: Pharo is an actively used language, with development and use continuing energetically in the research community and in some industrial applications. It has gained support as a venue for practicing pure object orientation and live programming.

name: Squeak
problem: Smalltalk-80は商用ベンダーの処理系に閉じており、自由に改変・移植できるオープンな実装が存在しなかった。Appleの研究者たちは、あらゆるプラットフォームに移植可能で、システム自身をSmalltalkで書き換えられる完全に自己記述的な処理系を、教育・研究向けに無償で提供したかった。
summary: Smalltalk-80をオープンソース化し移植性を高めた自己記述的なSmalltalk処理系。
problem_en: Smalltalk-80 was locked into commercial vendors' implementations, and no open implementation existed that anyone could freely modify or port. The researchers at Apple who had once created Smalltalk wanted to provide, free of charge for education and research, a fully self-describing system that could be ported to any platform and whose own implementation could be rewritten in Smalltalk code itself. Underlying this was also Alan Kay's consistent educational vision of creating a learning environment in which children could freely express their own ideas on a computer.
summary_en: Squeak is positioned as a niche language used in specific fields, and it continues to be used today in education and in research on self-describing systems. While many users have migrated to its successor Pharo, Squeak itself also maintains its own community.

name: Chicken Scheme
problem: Schemeは実装間の移植性が低く、既存のC言語資産と連携しづらいという課題があった。SchemeプログラムをポータブルなC言語コードへコンパイルすることで、幅広いプラットフォームで動作し、Cライブラリとも容易に連携できる実用的なScheme処理系を提供したかった。
summary: SchemeプログラムをC言語にコンパイルする移植性重視の実用的なScheme処理系。
problem_en: Scheme suffered from large implementation differences between processing systems, giving it poor portability, and it was also difficult to integrate with existing C-language assets. Chicken Scheme tried to solve this problem through an approach of compiling Scheme programs into portable C source code. This was intended to provide a highly practical Scheme implementation that would run anywhere a C compiler was available, and that could easily link with existing C libraries.
summary_en: It remains a currently used language, continuously used and developed by a community of developers who value its high portability and practicality. It is sometimes chosen for embedded scripting languages and tool development.

name: Chez Scheme
problem: 研究用途にも実用にも耐えうる、高品質なネイティブコードを生成する高速なScheme処理系が求められていた。既存のLisp/Scheme実装よりも効率的なコンパイラとインクリメンタルな開発環境を両立させたいという動機があった。
summary: 高速なネイティブコード生成を特徴とする高品質なScheme処理系。
problem_en: There was a need for a fast Scheme implementation that generated high-quality native code and could withstand both research and practical use. Many Lisp/Scheme implementations of the time were interpreter-centered and had limits on execution speed and the quality of the code they generated. Chez Scheme aimed to be a Scheme implementation that met the needs of both research and practical use, by having a more efficient optimizing compiler than existing implementations while also providing an interactive, incremental development environment.
summary_en: Chez Scheme is an actively used language, and thanks to its execution speed and the quality of its compiler, it continues to be used in both research and practical settings. Its adoption as the internal engine of other Scheme implementations also demonstrates the high technical regard it commands.

name: FreeBASIC
problem: DOSの終焉によりMicrosoft QuickBASICで書かれた資産や慣れ親しんだ構文が使えなくなっていく中で、無料でオープンソースの後継処理系を作りたかった。使い慣れたBASIC構文のままモダンなOS上でC言語並みのネイティブコードを生成したいという動機もあった。
summary: QuickBASIC互換を目指したオープンソースのネイティブコンパイル型BASIC。
problem_en: With the end of DOS, the enormous body of assets written in Microsoft QuickBASIC and the familiar BASIC syntax were becoming unusable as-is. FreeBASIC arose from the motivation to keep this legacy and knowledge usable by providing a free, open-source successor implementation. It also aimed to let developers keep using familiar BASIC syntax largely unchanged while generating native code on modern operating systems comparable to that produced by C.
summary_en: It is positioned as a niche language used in a specific field. It maintains a devoted user community, both for the hobbyist preservation of retro BASIC programming and for practical uses such as game development.

name: PureBasic
problem: Amiga向けのBlitz Basicが開発中止となったことを受け、その精神を受け継ぎながらWindowsなど新しいプラットフォームでも使える、シンプルで高速なネイティブコード生成型BASICを作りたかった。オブジェクト指向を排してあくまで構造化プログラミングに徹した軽量言語を志向した。
summary: Blitz Basicの後継として生まれた高速コンパイル型のBASIC言語。
problem_en: When Blitz Basic, which had been popular on the Amiga, was discontinued, there was a motivation to carry on its spirit while creating a simple, fast, native-code-generating BASIC that could also be used on new platforms such as Windows. PureBasic deliberately excluded complex concepts such as object orientation, committing purely to structured programming, aiming to be a lightweight language that was both accessible to beginners and excellent in execution speed.
summary_en: It is positioned as a niche language used in a specific domain. It continues to be used steadily by those in game development and utility development who want to easily create native applications.

name: Xojo
problem: Macintosh上にはWindowsのVisual Basicのような手軽なRAD開発環境が存在しなかったため、オブジェクト指向のBASIC系言語で同様の生産性をMac上で実現したかった。後にクロスプラットフォームでデスクトップ・モバイル・Webまで単一言語で開発できる環境を目指した。
summary: Visual Basicの精神を受け継ぐクロスプラットフォーム対応のオブジェクト指向RAD開発環境。
problem_en: At the time, the Macintosh had no easy RAD (rapid application development) environment comparable to Visual Basic on Windows. Xojo (originally named REALbasic) was born out of the motivation to achieve the same kind of productivity as Visual Basic on the Mac, through an object-oriented BASIC-family language. It later developed into an environment for building applications for multiple platforms — desktop, mobile, and web — from a single language and codebase.
summary_en: Xojo is positioned as a niche language used in a specific field. It continues to be offered and maintained today as a commercial product for individual developers and small to medium-sized businesses working on cross-platform business application development.

name: Small Basic
problem: Scratchのようなビジュアルプログラミングからテキストベースのプログラミングへとステップアップする子供や初学者に、無理なく学べる入り口を用意したかった。キーワード数を極限まで絞り込み、シンプルなIDEと組み合わせることで挫折を減らしたいという動機があった。
summary: 初心者向けにキーワードを14個に絞ったMicrosoft製の教育用BASIC言語。
problem_en: There was a need to provide children and beginners moving up from visual programming environments like Scratch to text-based programming with an entry point they could learn without strain. Small Basic was designed to pare its set of keywords down to an absolute minimum (about 14 by default) and, combined with a simple IDE, let beginners learn the fundamental concepts of programming without being defeated by syntactic complexity. It was developed by Microsoft as an educational project.
summary_en: Small Basic is positioned as an educational-purpose language, used as introductory teaching material for programming beginners, especially children. It plays the role of a bridge from visual languages to full-fledged text-based languages.

name: Liberty BASIC
problem: プログラミング初心者やホビイストが、Windows上で動くGUIアプリケーションを難しいAPI呼び出しを意識せずに、シンプルなBASIC構文だけで手軽に作れるようにしたかった。
summary: 初心者向けにWindows GUI開発を手軽にしたBASIC言語。
problem_en: There was a need for programming beginners and hobbyists to be able to easily create GUI applications that ran on Windows, without having to worry about complex API calls. Liberty BASIC aimed to provide an environment for building practical Windows applications with a low learning cost, by making it possible to handle GUI elements such as windows and buttons using nothing but familiar, simple BASIC syntax.
summary_en: It is positioned as a niche language used in a specific field. It maintains a loyal user base as an accessible tool for Windows GUI development aimed at programming beginners and hobbyists.

name: Curry
problem: 関数型プログラミングと論理型プログラミングは長らく別々の言語系統として発展してきたが、両者の利点を一つの言語で統合したいという学術的な動機から生まれた。高階関数などの関数型の表現力と、非決定的探索や制約解決といった論理型の強みを同時に使えるようにしたかった。
summary: 関数型と論理型を融合させた学術研究向けの関数論理プログラミング言語。
problem_en: Functional programming and logic programming had long developed as separate language lineages, and Curry arose from the academic motivation to unify the advantages of both into a single language. By creating a language that could simultaneously make use of the expressive power of functional features such as higher-order functions and lazy evaluation, together with the strengths of logic programming such as nondeterministic search, logic variables, and constraint solving, it aimed to practically explore a new paradigm called functional logic programming.
summary_en: Positioned as a niche language used in a specific field. It continues to be used today in the research and teaching of programming language theory and functional logic programming.

name: Max/MSP
problem: 作曲家やパフォーマーがプログラミングの専門知識なしに、インタラクティブな音楽・マルチメディア作品をリアルタイムで制作できる環境を作りたかった。専用DSPハードウェアに頼らず、一般的なコンピュータ上で音声信号処理やライブパフォーマンスを実現したかった。
summary: 音楽・マルチメディア制作向けのビジュアルデータフロー型プログラミング環境。
problem_en: There was a need to create an environment in which composers and performers, without any programming expertise, could produce interactive music and multimedia works in real time. Max/MSP aimed to realize audio signal processing and live performance on an ordinary computer without relying on dedicated DSP hardware. Its major distinguishing feature is a visual dataflow approach in which objects are connected by lines, letting musicians assemble complex processing without writing text code.
summary_en: Max/MSP is a language in active use, still widely employed in the production of electronic music, sound art, and interactive media works. It has become one of the standard tools for composers and sound artists.

name: Pure Data
problem: 商用のMaxをオープンソースかつ無償で、より自由に拡張できる形で再設計したかった。ネットワークを介して離れた場所にいる複数の演奏者がリアルタイムに音楽を共同制作できるようにしたかった。
summary: オープンソースのリアルタイム音楽・マルチメディア向けビジュアルプログラミング言語。
problem_en: There was a challenge in redesigning Max, a piece of commercial software, in an open-source, free form that could be extended more freely. Pure Data was created by Miller Puckette himself, who was also the developer of Max/MSP, by reorganizing that architecture. It also had a more ambitious goal: enabling multiple performers in different locations to collaboratively create music together in real time over a network.
summary_en: It is an actively used language today, widely employed in electronic music production, media art, and education. Being open source, it is also valued as a foundation for custom extensions by researchers and artists.

name: MyHDL
problem: Verilog/VHDLの冗長な文法や学習コストの高さを解消し、Pythonの簡潔さと豊富なエコシステムをハードウェア記述に持ち込みたかった。アルゴリズム設計とハードウェア実装を同じ言語・環境内で行き来できるようにしたかった。
summary: PythonでハードウェアをモデリングしVerilog/VHDLへ変換できるHDLパッケージ。
problem_en: The verbose grammar and high learning cost of Verilog/VHDL formed a barrier to entry for hardware design. MyHDL tried to solve this problem by bringing Python's conciseness and rich ecosystem to hardware description. By allowing algorithm design and hardware implementation to move back and forth within the same language and the same environment, it aimed to make the development cycle from simulation to implementation more efficient.
summary_en: MyHDL is positioned as a niche language used in a specific field. It continues to be used persistently in FPGA development, digital circuit design education, and prototyping.

name: Snap!
problem: Scratchの分かりやすいブロック操作を土台にしつつ、高階関数やラムダ式、第一級手続きといったより本格的な計算概念も教えられるようにしたかった。プログラミング未経験の大学生に対して、コンピュータサイエンスの本質的な考え方を専門用語やテキスト構文の壁なしに伝えたかった。
summary: Scratchを拡張し高階関数もサポートするブロック型教育用プログラミング言語。
problem_en: Snap! was created out of a desire to build on Scratch's accessible block-based interaction while bringing in more substantial computational concepts. It wanted to teach not just sequential processing and event handling, but the core ideas of functional programming — higher-order functions, lambda expressions, first-class procedures — in the form of blocks, without the barrier of technical terminology or text-based syntax. It was designed with a strong emphasis on serving as an introductory teaching tool that lets university students with no prior programming experience experience the essence of computer science early on.
