problem: 2003年に公開された仮想世界サービスSecond Lifeでは、ユーザー自身が3Dオブジェクトを作成できるだけでなく、それらに独自の振る舞いを持たせたいという要望があった。運営会社Linden Labは、C言語に近い親しみやすい文法を持ちながら、オブジェクトの状態遷移とイベント処理を自然に表現できるスクリプト言語を、Second Life内のオブジェクトに組み込む形で提供する必要があった。
summary: LSLは現在「niche」な言語であり、Second Lifeという特定のプラットフォーム内でのみ使われ続けている。
problem_en: In the virtual-world service Second Life, launched in 2003, users could create their own 3D objects but also wanted to give those objects custom behavior. Linden Lab needed a scripting language embedded directly into in-world objects with approachable, C-like syntax.
summary_en: LSL is currently positioned as a niche language (status: niche), used almost exclusively within the single platform of Second Life.

name: Euphoria
problem: ロバート・クレイグはトロント大学での計算機科学の修士研究でジョン・バッカスの関数型言語FPの考え方に触れ、そこから独自にプログラミング言語を一から作ってみるという個人的な取り組みを始めた。当時のインタプリタ言語の多くは、シンプルさと実行速度、初心者への扱いやすさのいずれかを犠牲にしていたとクレイグは考えた。
summary: Euphoriaは現在「niche」な言語であり、商用としてのRapid Deployment Softwareによる独占開発は終了している。2006年10月のバージョン3.0.0で完全にオープンソース化され、以後はopenEuphoria Groupによって保守が続けられている。
problem_en: While pursuing a master's degree in computer science at the University of Toronto, Robert Craig encountered John Backus's ideas on the functional language FP, and this sparked a personal project to design a programming language entirely from scratch.
summary_en: Euphoria is currently positioned as a niche language (status: niche); exclusive commercial development by Rapid Deployment Software has ended. The language was fully open-sourced with version 3.0.0 in October 2006.

name: Nemerle
problem: 2000年代初頭、.NET/Monoプラットフォーム上ではC#のようなオブジェクト指向言語が主流だったが、ML系やLisp系の関数型言語が持つ強力な型推論やパターンマッチング、メタプログラミング(マクロ)の表現力は取り込まれていなかった。
summary: Nemerleは現在「historical」な言語であり、目立った新規開発はほとんど行われていない。2012年に主要開発者がJetBrainsに雇用されて言語実装フレームワークNitraの開発に移ったこともあり、Nemerle自体の開発速度は大きく低下した。
problem_en: In the early 2000s, object-oriented languages like C# were dominant on the .NET/Mono platform, but the strong type inference, pattern matching, and metaprogramming expressiveness found in ML-family and Lisp-family functional languages had not been incorporated.
summary_en: Nemerle is currently a historical language (status: historical), with essentially no notable new development activity. Development momentum slowed considerably after its core developers were hired by JetBrains in 2012.

name: PBASIC
problem: 1990年代初頭、マイクロコントローラや組み込みプロセッサの世界はアセンブリ言語での開発が主流で、ホビイストや教育目的の利用者には敷居が高かった。Parallax, Inc.は、BASIC言語の平易な構文をそのまま組み込み開発に持ち込み、HIGH/LOW/PULSOUT/DEBUGといったハードウェア制御用の専用コマンドを追加することで、マイコンプログラミングを手軽にする言語PBASICを開発した。
summary: PBASICは現在「legacy」な言語であり、Parallax社自身もPropeller向けのSpinなど新しい言語・プラットフォームに軸を移している。しかし既存のBASIC Stamp製品を使った教育現場やホビー用途、産業機器の保守目的では、現在も一定の利用が続いている。
problem_en: In the early 1990s, microcontroller and embedded-processor development was dominated by assembly language, which was a high barrier for hobbyists and educational users. Parallax, Inc. brought the plain syntax of BASIC directly into embedded development.
summary_en: PBASIC is currently a legacy language (status: legacy); Parallax itself has shifted its focus to newer languages and platforms such as Spin for the Propeller chip.

name: A-0 System
problem: 1950年代初頭、UNIVAC I上でプログラムを組む際、プログラマはサブルーチンを呼び出すたびに、その格納アドレスや引数の受け渡しを手作業で機械語に翻訳する必要があり、既存のサブルーチン群を再利用する作業は煩雑で誤りやすかった。
summary: Grace Hopperが開発した、サブルーチンを数値コードで指定し引数を並べるだけで機械語プログラムを組み立てる仕組み。現代的な意味でのコンパイラの起点とされる。
problem_en: In the early 1950s, programming the UNIVAC I required programmers to manually translate every subroutine call into machine code, working out storage addresses and argument passing by hand each time. Reusing an existing library of subroutines was therefore tedious and error-prone, and there was no automated way to combine already-written subroutines into a new program.
summary_en: Grace Hopper and her team at Remington Rand built the A-0 system so that a program could be specified as a sequence of subroutines identified by numeric codes, with arguments listed after each code; the system then converted this specification into executable machine code for the UNIVAC I. Functionally A-0 behaved more like a loader/linker than a modern compiler, but it is widely cited as one of the earliest systems to automate the translation from a higher-level specification into machine code, and it began the lineage that Hopper's group extended through A-2, ARITH-MATIC, MATH-MATIC, and FLOW-MATIC, work that fed directly into the design of COBOL.

name: Action!
problem: Clinton ParkerはAtari 8-bit機を個人で購入した際、当時利用可能な開発ツールに満足できず、より高速に動作しコンパクトなプログラムを書ける言語を必要としていた。
summary: Atari 8-bit機向けのコンパイル型構造化言語兼統合開発環境。ALGOLに似た文法を持ち、6502プロセッサへ直接対応づけられる設計とされている。
problem_en: Clinton Parker bought an Atari 8-bit computer for personal use but was dissatisfied with the development tools available for it at the time. He wanted a language that could produce fast, compact programs while still being far more structured and maintainable than assembly language, and that came bundled with a productive, integrated editing environment.
summary_en: Action! is a procedural, compiled structured language and integrated development environment for Atari 8-bit computers, released in 1983 as a 16K bank-switched ROM cartridge. Wikipedia describes it as similar to ALGOL, and contemporary commentators likened it to a mix of C, Pascal, and Forth; it was essentially a port of the concepts behind Parker and Henry Baker's earlier Micro-SPL language to the 6502 processor, with the addition of a full-screen editor and integrated debugger.

name: Actor
problem: The Whitewater GroupのCharles Duffは、Microsoft Windows上でSmalltalkのような対話的な純粋オブジェクト指向開発環境を実現しつつ、Windows APIへ直接アクセスできる実用的な言語を必要としていた。
summary: Windows 2.1/3.0向けに開発された純粋オブジェクト指向言語。すべてがオブジェクトとして扱われ、Smalltalkをモデルとした対話的開発環境を備えていた。
problem_en: Charles Duff of The Whitewater Group wanted to bring a Smalltalk-like, purely object-oriented, interactive development experience to Microsoft Windows, while still giving programmers direct, low-level access to the Windows API — something that pure research Smalltalk environments of the time did not prioritize. The language grew directly out of object-oriented extensions to Forth that Duff had already been developing.
summary_en: Actor is a pure object-oriented language, released in 1988 exclusively for Microsoft Windows 2.1 and 3.0, in which even small integers are objects. It used a Baker semi-space garbage collector and a token-threaded interpreter written in 16-bit x86 assembly, paired with a Smalltalk-like interactive environment and a thin abstraction layer for native OS/Windows API access, plus a software virtual-memory system for the memory-constrained PCs of the era.

name: AIMMS
problem: 数理最適化モデル(線形・非線形・混合整数計画など)を構築・運用する際、汎用プログラミング言語で直接コーディングするのは煩雑で、モデルの数式的な構造をそのまま表現しにくいという課題があった。
summary: サプライチェーンやエネルギー市場などの意思決定支援のために、数理最適化モデルを代数的な記法で記述できるモデリング言語兼IDE。
problem_en: Building and operating mathematical optimization models — linear, quadratic, nonlinear, mixed-integer, and so on — directly in a general-purpose programming language is cumbersome, because the algebraic structure of the model does not map cleanly onto ordinary imperative code, making such models hard to write, read, and maintain.
summary_en: AIMMS (Advanced Interactive Multidimensional Modeling System) is prescriptive-analytics software created by mathematician Johannes Bisschop and co-designer Marcel Roelofs; the company behind it (originally Paragon Decision Technology, later AIMMS B.V.) was founded in 1989 and the system first appeared in 1993. It combines an algebraic modeling language supporting both declarative and imperative styles with an integrated development environment and graphical interfaces, and can hand models off to solvers such as CPLEX, MOSEK, Xpress, and CBC; it is used for decision support in areas such as supply chain management, retail, energy markets, and flood-protection planning.

name: Aldor
problem: 計算機代数システムAxiomを拡張するには、記号計算に特有の、型そのものを第一級の値として扱えるような高度な型システムを持つ言語が必要だったが、既存の汎用言語ではこれを自然に表現できなかった。
summary: 計算機代数システムAxiom(前身A#)を拡張するために設計された、型を第一級の値として扱える強い型付けの言語。Pascalに似た構文を持つ。
problem_en: Extending the Axiom computer algebra system required a language with an elaborate type system suited to symbolic mathematics — one in which types themselves could be treated as first-class values — but no existing general-purpose language expressed this naturally.
summary_en: Aldor, first appearing in 1990, is the successor to the A# language for extending the Axiom computer algebra system, designed by a team including Richard Jenks, Barry Trager, Stephen Watt, James Davenport, Robert Sutor, and Scott Morrison. It blends imperative, functional, and object-oriented features with an elaborate type system that lets types be used as first-class values and supports dependent typing; its syntax is heavily influenced by Pascal (with optional Python-like indentation sensitivity) and it also draws on ideas from Haskell. It compiles to machine code while still offering an interactive interface.

name: Alice ML
problem: Standard MLのような静的型付け関数型言語には、分散・並行・制約プログラミングといった当時の高度なアプリケーションが求める機能が組み込まれておらず、それらを自然に組み合わせて使える言語が求められていた。
summary: Standard MLの方言として、ザールランド大学で設計された多重パラダイム関数型言語。future/promiseによる並行実行や遅延評価、分散プログラミングのための機能を備える。
problem_en: Statically typed functional languages such as Standard ML did not come with built-in support for the distributed, concurrent, and constraint-based programming that more advanced applications of the time needed, and there was demand for a language that could combine these naturally with a familiar ML-style core.
summary_en: Alice ML, first appearing on June 16, 2000, was designed by the Programming Systems Lab at Saarland University in Saarbrücken as a general-purpose, high-level, multi-paradigm functional language and dialect of Standard ML, extended with imperative, distributed, concurrent, and constraint programming capabilities. Early versions ran on the virtual machine of the Mozart Programming System (Oz), allowing Alice and Oz code to interoperate; the language added future/promise types for concurrency, optional lazy evaluation (unlike Standard ML's default eager evaluation), and remote procedure calls, later running on its own SEAM virtual machine with just-in-time compilation.

name: AmbientTalk
problem: モバイル機器同士が不安定なネットワークを通じて、常時接続を前提とせずに通信するようなアプリケーションを開発するには、接続が途切れることを前提とした分散オブジェクトモデルが必要だったが、既存の分散オブジェクト言語は安定したネットワークを前提としていた。
summary: ブリュッセル自由大学で設計された、モバイル・アドホックネットワーク向けの実験的な分散オブジェクト指向言語。アクターモデルとfutureに基づく並行性を持つ。
problem_en: Building applications in which mobile devices communicate over volatile, ad hoc networks — without assuming an always-on connection — required a distributed object model designed around intermittent connectivity, whereas existing distributed object languages generally assumed a stable network.
summary_en: AmbientTalk, first appearing in 2006, is an experimental distributed object-oriented language designed by Tom Van Cutsem, Stijn Mostinckx, Jessie Dedecker, and Wolfgang De Meuter at the Software Languages Lab of the Vrije Universiteit Brussel, aimed at applications running on volatile mobile networks with intermittent connectivity and minimal infrastructure. It combines actor-model concurrency with futures, an event-loop architecture, and prototype-based object orientation with traits and delegation; it was implemented in Java (including for Android) with a 'symbiosis' interface allowing seamless interoperation between Java and AmbientTalk objects, and it drew on Smalltalk, Self, Scheme, and the E programming language. Wikipedia's infobox also lists AmbientTalk as having influenced the ECMAScript Harmony proposals, though the article does not elaborate on how.

name: Amiga E
problem: Amiga上でシステムアプリケーションを開発するには、C言語よりも高速にコンパイルでき、より読みやすく柔軟な型システムを持つ言語が求められていたが、当時のAmiga向け言語はコンパイル速度や表現力に課題を抱えていた。
summary: Wouter van Oortmerssenが開発した、Amiga(68000系/AmigaOS)向けの汎用言語。高速なコンパイル、モジュールシステム、多重パラダイム対応を特徴とし、Amigaで最も人気を集めた言語の一つとなった。
problem_en: Developing system-level applications on the Amiga in C worked, but developers wanted a language that compiled much faster (fast enough to use as a scripting-like tool), had more readable source code and a more flexible type system, and still produced efficient native code for the Motorola 68000-based AmigaOS.
summary_en: Amiga E, created by Wouter van Oortmerssen and first released on September 29, 1993, is a general-purpose language targeting system-level applications on AmigaOS/Motorola 68000 hardware. According to its creator, it 'became one of the most popular programming languages on the Amiga.' It offered very fast compilation (fast enough to double as a scripting alternative), readable syntax with a flexible type system, a powerful module system, exception handling, and multi-paradigm support spanning procedural, object-oriented, and functional styles, drawing influence from Ada, C++, and Lisp.

name: AngelScript
problem: ゲームエンジンにスクリプト機能を組み込む際、C++で書かれたエンジン本体とシームレスに連携でき、かつC++に慣れた開発者がすぐに書き始められる文法を持つ、軽量に組み込み可能なスクリプト言語が求められていた。
summary: AngelCodeのAndreas Jönssonが開発した、ゲーム向けの組み込み型コンパイルスクリプト言語。C++に近いクラス構文を持ち、静的型付けとガーベジコレクション付きハンドルを備える。
problem_en: Embedding scripting into a game engine required a lightweight, embeddable scripting language that could interoperate seamlessly with a C++ engine core and that C++-fluent developers could pick up immediately, without a steep syntactic learning curve.
summary_en: AngelScript is an open-source, game-oriented, compiled scripting language created by Andreas Jönsson at AngelCode, first appearing in 2003. It is statically typed and object-oriented, with garbage-collected handles resembling C++ pointers, support for single and multiple inheritance via interfaces, operator overloading, all-virtual methods, and direct integration with C/C++ functions; its class syntax closely follows C++ by design. It is used in games such as Amnesia: The Dark Descent, Overgrowth, SuperTuxKart, and It Takes Two, as well as via an Unreal Engine plugin, and is licensed under the zlib License.

name: Pig Latin
problem: Hadoop上でMapReduceジョブをその場限りの用途(アドホックな分析)のために書くには、Javaで直接MapReduceを記述する必要があり、データの変換パイプラインを素早く組み立てるには冗長すぎるという課題があった。
summary: Apache Pigのクエリ言語Pig Latin。MapReduceの複雑さを、SQLに似てはいるが手続き的なデータフロー記法として抽象化する。
problem_en: Writing MapReduce jobs directly in Java for ad hoc, exploratory data analysis on Hadoop was verbose and slow to iterate on, making it hard to quickly assemble and adjust data transformation pipelines over large datasets.
summary_en: Pig Latin is the language of Apache Pig, a high-level platform for running data-analysis programs on Apache Hadoop, originally developed at Yahoo Research around 2006 and donated to the Apache Software Foundation in 2007 (first official Apache release September 11, 2008). It abstracts MapReduce into a notation resembling SQL but, unlike SQL, is explicitly procedural and dataflow-oriented, giving programmers direct control over each step of the pipeline (expressed as a directed acyclic graph) with lazy evaluation, a nested relational data model, and support for user-defined functions in Java, Python, JavaScript, Ruby, or Groovy; jobs run via MapReduce, Apache Tez, or Apache Spark.

name: APT
problem: 航空機部品などの複雑な形状を数値制御(NC)工作機械で切削するには、切削経路のための座標計算を機械工やエンジニアが手作業で行う必要があり、非常に手間がかかり誤りも生じやすかった。
summary: MITのDouglas T. Rossが主導して開発した、数値制御工作機械向けの指示を生成する言語。航空宇宙産業14社や政府、大学を巻き込んだ世界初の大規模共同プログラミング事業として知られる。
problem_en: Machining complex shapes such as aerospace parts on numerically controlled (NC) machine tools required machinists and engineers to manually work out the coordinate geometry for cutter paths, a laborious and error-prone process for anything beyond simple shapes.
summary_en: APT (Automatically Programmed Tool), first appearing in 1956, was created under the leadership of Douglas T. Ross at MIT's Servomechanisms (Computer Applications) Laboratory to generate instructions for numerically controlled machine tools, letting programs specify tool geometry and motion in text rather than requiring hand calculation. Its development, drawing in the U.S. Air Force, multiple universities, and 14 aerospace companies, is described as the world's first major cooperative programming venture; it predated even FORTRAN, produced cutter-location (CL) files later converted to G-code, and spawned derivatives such as ADAPT, EXAPT, and UNIAPT, as well as early robotics languages like RAPT and ROBEX. It remains an international standard, with elements still used in modern CAM systems.

name: ArkTS
problem: HarmonyOS/OpenHarmony向けのアプリケーションを開発するには、TypeScriptの資産と開発者の知識を活かしつつ、宣言的UI記述やAOTコンパイル、並行処理といったモバイル/組み込み向けの要件を満たす言語が必要だった。
summary: HuaweiがHarmonyOS/OpenHarmony向けに開発した、TypeScriptを拡張したスーパーセット言語。ArkUIによる宣言的UI記述やAOTコンパイル、async/awaitとアクターによる並行処理をサポートする。
problem_en: Building applications for HarmonyOS/OpenHarmony required a language that could carry over existing TypeScript code and developer knowledge while also meeting mobile/embedded requirements such as declarative UI description, ahead-of-time compilation for performance, and concurrency — needs that plain TypeScript on a JavaScript engine did not fully address.
summary_en: ArkTS, first released on OpenHarmony on September 30, 2021 and formally introduced at Huawei's Developer Conference in November 2022, is a high-level, general-purpose, multi-paradigm, compiled, declarative, statically typed language and extension superset of TypeScript (which is itself a superset of JavaScript), replacing the earlier extended TypeScript (eTS) used in HarmonyOS 3.0. It compiles ahead-of-time to machine code, supports object-oriented programming with classes and method overriding, uses automatic garbage-collected memory management, handles nil values explicitly via optionals, supports concurrency through async/await and actors, and integrates with the ArkUI framework for declarative UI development; it draws on ideas from TypeScript, JavaScript, Swift, Rust, and other languages, and runs on HarmonyOS, OpenHarmony, and, via tooling, other platforms.

name: ARexx
problem: Amiga上の複数のアプリケーションを組み合わせて自動化するには、それぞれのアプリケーションと通信し機能を呼び出せる、汎用的なマクロ/スクリプト言語が必要だった。
summary: William S. Hawesが開発した、Amiga向けのRexx実装。ARexxポートを介して対応アプリケーションと通信し、機能を組み合わせて自動化できる。
problem_en: Automating and combining the functionality of multiple Amiga applications required a general-purpose macro/scripting language capable of communicating with each application and invoking its features, rather than relying on ad hoc, application-specific automation.
summary_en: ARexx, created by William S. Hawes in 1987, is a Rexx interpreter for the Amiga (from AmigaOS 2.0 onward) with Amiga-specific extensions, closely following the standard Rexx language described by Mike Cowlishaw; Hawes later took part in drafting the ANSI standard for Rexx. Scripts communicate with ARexx-compatible applications through 'ARexx ports,' letting a single script drive and combine features across different programs; the language treats all data as typeless text/strings and uses dynamic variable scoping. Development stalled after Hawes stopped working on Amiga software, and because its implementation is 68000 assembly, it cannot run at full speed on PowerPC systems and is absent from MorphOS, though legacy versions remain in limited use.

name: Axum
problem: 並行・並列処理を安全に書くことがC#などの既存の.NET言語では難しく、共有メモリに依存する従来のスレッドモデルに代わる仕組みが必要とされた。
summary: アクターモデルに基づく.NET向けの実験的並行言語で、2011年にプロジェクトが中止された。そのアイデアの一部は.NET 4.5のTPL Dataflowに引き継がれたとされる。
problem_en: Writing safe concurrent and parallel code was difficult in existing .NET languages such as C#, which relied on a traditional shared-memory threading model prone to data races and deadlocks. Microsoft sought a domain-specific language that would let developers isolate concurrent components from sequential ones, using message-passing instead of shared state.
summary_en: Axum was an experimental, actor-model-based concurrent language for the .NET Common Language Runtime, developed by Microsoft from 2009. It used C-like syntax and introduced isolated "agents" that communicated only through typed "channels" with protocol definitions. Microsoft decided not to ship Axum as a full product, and the project was discontinued around 2011; the English Wikipedia article notes that some of its ideas were carried into TPL Dataflow in .NET 4.5. Today it is referenced only as a historical experiment in language-level actor concurrency on .NET (status: historical).

name: bc
problem: Unix上で対話的にもスクリプトとしても使える、任意精度の数値計算を行える電卓言語が必要とされた。既存のdcは逆ポーランド記法で扱いにくく、より従来型のプログラミング言語に近い構文のフロントエンドが求められた。
summary: Version 6 Unixに登場した任意精度電卓言語。dcへのフロントエンドとして設計され、C言語風の構文を持つ。GNU bcなど複数の実装が現在も使われている。
problem_en: Unix needed a calculator language that could be used both interactively and as a script, supporting arbitrary-precision arithmetic. The existing dc used awkward reverse Polish notation, so a more conventional, C-like front-end syntax was wanted so that ordinary control structures such as if, while, and for could be used naturally.
summary_en: bc is an arbitrary-precision calculator language that first appeared in Version 6 Unix in 1975, designed by Robert Morris and Lorinda Cherry at Bell Labs as a compiler front-end that translates its C-like syntax into dc notation. It supports variables, arrays, functions, and familiar control-flow structures, with precision controlled by the global variable `scale`. Several independent implementations remain in active use today (status: active), including GNU bc, the OpenBSD reimplementation, and Gavin Howard's implementation shipped in Android, FreeBSD, and macOS.

name: BeanShell
problem: Javaコードをコンパイルせずにその場で試したり、テストやデバッグの際に動的にJavaのコードやオブジェクトを操作したりする手段が求められた。
summary: Javaソースコードをほぼそのまま解釈実行できる軽量スクリプト言語。緩い型付けやクロージャなどPerl・JavaScript的な機能をJava構文に加えた。Java 9のJShell導入以降は利用が縮小している。
problem_en: Java developers lacked a lightweight way to try out code interactively or to dynamically inspect and manipulate Java objects during testing and debugging, since Java itself required a full compile-run cycle. Patrick Niemeyer designed BeanShell as a small, embeddable Java source interpreter that could execute ordinary Java syntax on the fly, while also borrowing convenient dynamic features from scripting languages such as Perl and JavaScript, including loose typing, script-like commands, and closures.
summary_en: BeanShell is a small, embeddable Java source interpreter first released in 1999, designed so that code written for a Java compiler can usually run unchanged in BeanShell and vice versa. It became a popular testing and debugging tool on the JVM, and was formally proposed for standardization as JSR 274, which remains dormant. Since Java 9 introduced the built-in JShell REPL, BeanShell's role has diminished considerably (status: legacy), though the Apache-licensed project is still available.

name: BETA
problem: Simulaの共同開発者であるKristen Nygaardらは、クラス・プロシージャ・型といったオブジェクト指向言語に散在する複数の概念を、より少数の統一的な概念で説明し直したいと考えた。
summary: 「北欧学派」によるSimulaの後継的オブジェクト指向言語。クラスとプロシージャを「パターン」という単一概念に統合した点が特徴。2020年時点で開発は非アクティブ。
problem_en: Kristen Nygaard, co-creator of Simula, and colleagues at the University of Oslo and Aarhus University wanted to unify the many separate concepts scattered across object-oriented languages — classes, procedures, types, and more — into a smaller set of more fundamental, orthogonal concepts, refining and extending the object-oriented model that Simula had pioneered.
summary_en: BETA is a purely object-oriented language originating from the Scandinavian School, designed from 1976 by Kristen Nygaard, Bent Bruun Kristensen, Ole Lehrmann Madsen, and Birger Møller-Pedersen as an evolution of Simula, with implementations appearing from 1986. Its central innovation was unifying classes and procedures into a single concept called a "pattern," and it introduced nested classes and virtual class definitions as general abstraction mechanisms. Development on the project became inactive as of October 2020 (status: historical), but it remains an influential reference point in the theory of object-oriented language design.

name: BlooP/FlooP
problem: 計算可能性理論において、「有限回のループしか持たない手続き」と「無限に回りうるループを持つ手続き」の間にどのような表現力の違いが生まれるのかを、具体的なプログラミング言語の形で直感的に示したかった。
summary: 『ゲーデル、エッシャー、バッハ』でDouglas Hofstadterが示した対の教育的言語。BlooPは有界ループのみを持ち原始再帰関数しか表現できず、FlooPは非有界ループ(MUループ)を追加してチューリング完全になる。
problem_en: In the field of computability theory, Douglas Hofstadter wanted an intuitive, concrete way to illustrate the difference in expressive power between procedures restricted to bounded loops and procedures allowed unbounded loops, as part of his 1979 book Gödel, Escher, Bach.
summary_en: BlooP and FlooP are a pair of pedagogical languages introduced by Douglas Hofstadter in Gödel, Escher, Bach (1979) as models of computation. BlooP permits only bounded loops and no recursion, so it is not Turing-complete and can express exactly the primitive recursive functions, guaranteeing termination. FlooP adds unbounded "MU-loops," making it Turing-complete and able to express any computable function, including the Ackermann function, which BlooP cannot express. Never intended as practical languages, they continue to be used in university courses and discussions of computability theory (status: educational).

name: C--
problem: 関数型言語の実装者たちは、コンパイラの出力先としてC言語を使うことが多かったが、Cはテイルコール最適化を保証せず、ガベージコレクションや例外処理を直接サポートしないため、それらの機能を持つ言語の中間コードとしては不十分だった。
summary: コンパイラが生成する出力を想定した移植可能な中間言語。C言語風の構文を持つが、ガベージコレクションのサポートなど高水準言語のバックエンドとして必要な機能を備える。GHCの内部表現Cmmとして現在も使われている。
problem_en: Implementers of functional and other high-level languages commonly targeted C as a compiler back-end, but C did not guarantee tail-call optimization and had no direct support for garbage collection or exception handling, making it an awkward intermediate target for languages that relied on these features. Simon Peyton Jones and Norman Ramsey designed C-- as a portable, low-level intermediate language intended to be generated by compilers rather than written by hand, addressing these gaps.
summary_en: C-- is a portable intermediate language first released in April 1998, designed primarily as a compiler target rather than for direct human use. Its plain ASCII text representation resembles C syntax but removes or changes features such as variadic arguments and pointer syntax, while adding first-class support for garbage collection and exception handling that C lacks. Although the original C-- 2.0 (2005) and its main implementation, Quick C--, are no longer actively developed (Quick C-- was archived in 2019), a dialect called Cmm remains in active use as the internal intermediate representation of the Glasgow Haskell Compiler (status: niche).

name: C/AL
problem: Navision(後のMicrosoft Dynamics NAV)の業務アプリケーション開発において、データベースへのレコードの取得・挿入・更新を簡潔に記述できる、業務アプリケーション専用の言語が必要とされた。
summary: C/SIDE開発環境向けに設計された、Pascalの流れを汲む命令型言語。Microsoft Dynamics NAVのデータベース操作専用言語として使われたが、Business Centralへの移行にともない後継言語ALに置き換えられ廃止された。
problem_en: Business application development on Navision (later Microsoft Dynamics NAV) needed a dedicated language for concisely retrieving, inserting, and modifying records in the underlying Navision database, tightly integrated with the C/SIDE (Client/Server Integrated Development Environment) development tools rather than being a general-purpose language.
summary_en: C/AL is an imperative, Pascal-derived, database-specific programming language designed by Michael Nielsen for use within C/SIDE, the development environment for Microsoft Dynamics NAV (and its predecessor Navision) and, later, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. It has no console, so output during development is handled through dialog boxes. C/AL was used through Dynamics NAV version 14, after which Microsoft replaced it with the successor language AL when transitioning to Business Central, making C/AL obsolete (status: legacy).

name: Caché ObjectScript
problem: MUMPS言語は医療・金融分野のデータベースシステムで広く使われていたが、オブジェクト指向やマクロ、SQLの埋め込みといった現代的な機能を欠いていた。InterSystemsはANSI MUMPSとの後方互換性を保ちながら、これらの機能を追加した言語を必要としていた。
summary: ANSI標準MUMPSの機能上位互換言語として、InterSystemsのCaché(現IRIS)データベースのために設計された。オブジェクト指向、マクロ前処理、SQLの埋め込みなどをC言語風の中括弧構文でMUMPSに追加している。
problem_en: MUMPS was widely used for database systems in healthcare and finance, but it lacked modern language features such as object orientation, macro preprocessing, and embedded SQL. InterSystems needed a language that preserved backward compatibility with ANSI-standard MUMPS routines while adding these capabilities for commercial, large-scale application development.
summary_en: Caché ObjectScript is a functional superset of the ANSI-standard MUMPS programming language, first appearing in 1997 as part of InterSystems' Caché database system (now continued as InterSystems IRIS). It adds object-oriented programming, macro preprocessing, and embedded SQL to MUMPS, using C-like brace syntax for control blocks alongside private/public variables and multidimensional arrays. The English Wikipedia article flags the topic's notability as uncertain due to limited independent sourcing, but InterSystems continues to actively maintain and document the language (status: niche), which remains in specialized use in healthcare and enterprise database systems.

name: Caml
problem: 定理証明などの研究で使われていたML言語の考え方を引き継ぎつつ、フランスのINRIA/ENSでML系関数型言語の独自実装を作りたいという要求があった。
summary: MLファミリーの方言としてINRIA/ENSで開発された関数型言語。最初の実装はAscánder SuárezによりLispで書かれ、後にXavier LeroyによるCaml Light、Caml Special Lightを経て、オブジェクト指向機能を得てOCamlへと発展した。
problem_en: Researchers in France wanted their own implementation of a language in the ML family — whose Hindley-Milner type inference and pattern matching had proven powerful in theorem-proving contexts such as LCF — as a general-purpose functional language developed at INRIA and ENS Paris.
summary_en: Caml is a multi-paradigm functional and imperative language in the ML family, first appearing in 1985 and designed by Gérard Huet, Guy Cousineau, Ascánder Suárez, Pierre Weis, and Michel Mauny at INRIA and ENS Paris. The first implementation was written in Lisp by Ascánder Suárez in 1987. Xavier Leroy later rewrote it in C as the more efficient Caml Light, and a subsequent rewrite, Caml Special Light, added a powerful module system and eventually object-oriented features, becoming Objective Caml — renamed OCaml. The stable Caml release dates to version 0.75 (January 2002); OCaml is its actively maintained main descendant (status: historical for Caml itself).

name: CESIL
problem: コンピュータがほとんどの学校に無かった1960年代末の英国で、中学・高校の生徒に初歩的なプログラミングの概念を教えるための、単純で分かりやすい言語が必要とされた。
summary: 英国の教育プロジェクト「Computer Education in Schools」の一環として作られた教育用言語。単一のアキュムレータと14個の命令のみを持ち、整数のみを扱う。パンチカードや紙テープを介してメインフレームに提出する形式で使われた。
problem_en: In the late 1960s in Britain, when computers were unavailable in most schools, there was a need for a simple, accessible language to introduce secondary-school pupils to elementary computer programming concepts, deliverable through the era's batch-processing infrastructure.
summary_en: CESIL (Computer Education in Schools Instruction Language) was developed by the John Hoskyns Group as part of the Computer Education in Schools project (commenced 1968) and introduced in April 1969, with International Computers Limited (ICL) taking over the project in September 1969 to become ICL-CES. It is a simple accumulator-based language with only fourteen instructions, working exclusively with integers and lacking arrays, data structures, or string handling. Pupils wrote programs on coding sheets that were converted to punched cards or paper tape and submitted to mainframes for batch processing. No individual designer is named in the source; the language is credited to the Hoskyns organization. It is no longer used for its original purpose (status: historical), though modern emulators such as Visual CESIL and Wyrm CESIL keep it accessible today.

name: Céu
problem: 組込み・リアクティブなプログラムでは、CやC++で並行イベント処理を書くと安全性の保証が難しく、予測可能で決定的な動作を保ちながら安全にリアクティブなロジックを記述できる言語が求められた。
summary: 同期リアクティブなプログラミングモデルを持つ、CやC++の安全な代替を目指した言語。決定的な実行、少ないメモリ要求を特徴とし、リオデジャネイロ・カトリック大学(PUC-Rio)で開発された。
problem_en: Embedded and reactive programs that handle concurrent events are difficult to make safe when written in C or C++, which offer few guarantees against unpredictable interleavings or memory misuse. Francisco Sant'Anna, developing the language starting around 2011 at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio), sought a language that preserved deterministic, predictable execution while making reactive, event-driven logic safer to write than in C or C++.
summary_en: Céu is a synchronous reactive language intended for front-end and embedded applications, aiming to be a safer alternative to C and C++ through deterministic execution, synchronous concurrency over shared memory, and minimal memory requirements. Development began around 2011 by Francisco Sant'Anna at PUC-Rio, with the Wikipedia infobox listing April 3, 2014 as when the language first appeared. C was its primary influence. The most recent stable release documented is v0.30 (March 2018); the project maintains an active GitHub repository and website, but the Wikipedia article itself notes limited independent secondary coverage, indicating a specialized academic language without mainstream adoption (status: niche).

name: CFEngine
problem: 大規模なコンピュータシステム(サーバー群、デスクトップ、組込み機器など)の設定・保守を、機種やOSの差異を吸収しつつ自動化する必要があったが、それを手続き的なスクリプトで書くと保守が煩雑になりやすかった。
summary: 「最終的にどのような状態であるべきか」を記述する宣言型の構成管理言語兼システム。オスロ大学のMark Burgessが開発し、2008年にはPromise理論を組み込んだCFEngine 3がリリースされた。世界中で数百万台のコンピュータで使われている。
problem_en: Automating the configuration and maintenance of large-scale computer systems — servers, desktops, and embedded devices — while absorbing differences between platforms and operating systems was hard to do with traditional procedural scripts, which described the steps to reach a desired state rather than the state itself, making maintenance and reasoning about system state difficult at scale.
summary_en: CFEngine is a configuration management system centered on a declarative domain-specific language: rather than describing the steps needed to make a change, the CFEngine language describes the final desired state of a system. It was created by Mark Burgess, initially at the University of Oslo's Department of Theoretical Physics as a way to automate workstation management, with the project beginning in 1993. CFEngine 2 introduced a major redesign, and CFEngine 3, released in 2008, incorporated Promise Theory. CFEngine AS was founded in June 2008 (renamed Northern.tech in 2017). Released as free software under GPLv3 and implemented in C, CFEngine remains actively used today (status: active) on millions of computers across more than 100 countries, including at companies such as LinkedIn.

name: Ch
problem: 数学・数値計算・プログラミングを学ぶ初学者や、C/C++のコードを素早く試したいエンジニアに向けて、コンパイルなしにC/C++ライクなコードを対話的に実行できる環境が求められた。
summary: C90に準拠しC99の主要機能も取り込んだCのスーパーセットで、C++のクラスも扱えるインタプリタ言語。SoftIntegration社によって開発され、C-STEM StudioなどでのロボティクスやSTEM教育に使われている。
problem_en: Beginners learning mathematics, numerical computing, and programming, as well as engineers wanting to quickly try out C/C++-like code, needed an interactive environment that could interpret C/C++-style code without a full compile step, while still supporting numerical computing and plotting.
summary_en: Ch is a scripting language and cross-platform interpreter environment created by Harry H. Cheng, first released in October 2001 and now developed and marketed by SoftIntegration, Inc. It is a superset of C supporting C++ classes, implementing C90 and major C99 features such as complex numbers, variable-length arrays, and IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic, and it can call existing C/C++ library functions or be embedded within C/C++ applications. Combining shell and IDE functionality with numerical computing and graphical plotting, Ch integrates with the C-STEM Studio educational platform and supports robotics programming on Arduino and LEGO Mindstorms, among other platforms (status: niche); its latest stable release (8.0.0) was in November 2017.

name: Charm++
problem: スーパーコンピュータ上で大規模並列アプリケーションを書く際、プロセッサへの処理割り当てを実行中に動的に変更してロードバランシングや耐障害性を実現したいという要求があったが、従来のメッセージパッシングモデルではそれが難しかった。
summary: C++をベースにした、メッセージ駆動オブジェクト(chare)による並列オブジェクト指向言語。イリノイ大学アーバナ・シャンペーン校のParallel Programming Laboratoryで開発され、NAMDなど数十万コア規模のペタスケールアプリケーションで使われている。
problem_en: Writing large-scale parallel applications for supercomputers required the ability to dynamically reassign which processor a piece of work ran on during execution, in order to achieve load balancing, fault tolerance, and checkpointing — capabilities that traditional static message-passing models such as MPI did not easily provide.
summary_en: Charm++ is a parallel object-oriented programming paradigm and runtime system based on C++, designed by Laxmikant Kale and developed by the Parallel Programming Laboratory at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign since the late 1980s. It uses message-driven objects called "chares," which can be dynamically reassigned to different processors during execution to enable load balancing, fault tolerance, and checkpointing, while offering high-level abstraction over diverse hardware. Charm++ remains actively developed (latest stable release 7.0.0, October 2021) and underlies applications such as NAMD (molecular dynamics), OpenAtom, and ChaNGa, which have scaled to over a hundred thousand cores on petascale systems (status: active). Extensions include Adaptive MPI (AMPI) for MPI compatibility and Charm4py for Python development.

name: ChucK
problem: リアルタイムの音楽・音声合成において、演奏中にコードを追加・削除・変更できる「ライブコーディング」を、精密なタイミング制御と読みやすい構文で実現できる言語が求められた。
summary: 強く時間指向(strongly timed)の並行音楽プログラミング言語。プリンストン大学でGe WangがPerry R. Cookとともに開発し、ライブコーディングやPrinceton Laptop Orchestraでの演奏に使われた。
problem_en: Real-time music and audio synthesis needed a language that could support "live coding" — adding, removing, and modifying code on the fly while a program keeps running — combined with precise, sample-synchronous timing control and syntax that remained readable and flexible for composers and programmers alike.
summary_en: ChucK is a concurrent, strongly timed audio programming language for real-time synthesis, composition, and performance, created by Ge Wang as a graduate student working with Perry R. Cook at Princeton University, first appearing in 2003. It emphasizes live coding, direct support for real-time audio synthesis, a simple concurrent programming model, and precise, sample-synchronous timing, along with support for MIDI, Open Sound Control, unit generators, and file I/O, compiling to virtual-machine bytecode. ChucK remains actively maintained (latest stable release 1.5.2.4, April 2024) and freely distributed under GPL-2.0 across Linux, macOS, Windows, and iOS (status: active); it has been used in performances by the Princeton Laptop Orchestra and in the development of Smule's Ocarina app.

name: Cilk
problem: 共有メモリ環境での並列プログラミングにおいて、プログラマがタスクの分割(どこが並列化可能か)だけを宣言し、実際のスケジューリングやロードバランシングはランタイムに任せたいという要求から生まれた。MITの並列チェスプログラムStarTechなどの研究成果を統合し、Cとの高い互換性を保ったまま並列処理を書ける拡張言語として設計された。
summary: spawn/syncとワークスティーリングスケジューラによる並列プログラミングモデルは学術的に大きな影響を残した。商用版のIntel Cilk Plusは2017年に非推奨となったが、MITによる後継のOpenCilkとして現在も研究・実務で使われ続けているニッチな言語である。
problem_en: In shared-memory parallel programming, developers wanted a way to declare only where a computation could be split into parallel tasks, leaving the actual scheduling and load-balancing decisions to a runtime system rather than managing them by hand. Cilk grew out of research at MIT's Laboratory for Computer Science, led by Charles E. Leiserson, which combined work on scheduling theory with practical parallel systems such as the *StarTech parallel chess program and the PCM/Threaded-C runtime. It was designed as a minimal extension of C so that existing C code and programmer intuitions could be reused almost unchanged.
summary_en: Cilk's fork-join model (spawn/sync) together with its provably efficient work-stealing scheduler had significant academic impact and influenced later systems such as OpenMP 3.0's tasking model and Rust's Rayon library. The commercial line (Cilk++, then Intel Cilk Plus) was deprecated by Intel in 2017, but MIT's OpenCilk project revived and continues to maintain the language as of the 2020s, so it survives today as a niche but actively used parallel-programming tool rather than a purely historical curiosity.

name: CLIST
problem: IBMメインフレームのTSO(Time Sharing Option)環境において、繰り返し行うコマンド操作を自動化したいという要求から生まれた。当初は単純な逐次コマンドリストだったが、条件分岐やループ、変数などが追加され、MVSファイルの読み書きやISPFダイアログサービスの呼び出しにも対応する手続き型のコマンド言語(スクリプト言語)に発展した。
summary: REXXがTSO/E Version 2で利用可能になったことで補助的な位置づけとなったが、既存資産の保守目的で稼働システムに残っている歴史的言語である。
problem_en: On IBM mainframes running TSO (Time Sharing Option), users needed a way to automate repetitive sequences of commands. CLIST ("Command List", pronounced "C-List") originated around OS/360 Release 20 as, in its most basic form, simply a list of commands to be executed in strict sequence. Later versions added conditional logic, loops, parameter passing, and global variables, turning it into a full procedural scripting language capable of reading and writing MVS files, invoking external MVS applications, running in the background, and driving ISPF dialog services.
summary_en: CLIST has played a secondary role since Rexx became available under TSO/E Version 2, which offered a more powerful and more consistent syntax for the same environment. Today CLIST survives mainly as legacy code that continues to run and be maintained on IBM mainframe systems, making it effectively a historical language rather than one chosen for new development.

name: CMS-2
problem: 米海軍の戦術データシステム(艦載コンピュータなど)向けに、可搬性と再利用性の高い標準化された高水準言語が必要とされた。CMS-2はRAND Corporationが設計し、Computer Sciences Corporationが実装した、組み込み・リアルタイム環境向けの高信頼性言語であり、独立コンパイル可能なモジュール構造や複数のデータ型、ビット・文字列操作の直接サポートを備えた。
summary: 米軍の艦載システムなどで長期間使われてきたが、Adaなど後継言語への移行が進み、現在は歴史的言語として位置づけられている。
problem_en: For the U.S. Navy's shipboard tactical data systems, there was a need for a standardized high-level language that would improve code portability and reusability across different embedded computers. CMS-2 was designed by the RAND Corporation and implemented by Computer Sciences Corporation in 1968 as a high-reliability language for real-time embedded systems, featuring modular programs with independently compilable units, multiple data types (fixed-point, floating-point, boolean, character, status), and direct manipulation of bits and character strings.
summary_en: CMS-2 remained in long-term use in U.S. Navy shipboard systems, but as the military moved toward Ada and other successor languages, CMS-2 gradually receded into legacy status. It is treated today as a historical language documented mainly for its role in military embedded-systems history rather than for active new development.

name: Cobra
problem: スクリプト言語が持つ生産性・読みやすさと、静的型付けプラットフォームが持つ堅牢性を両立させたいという要求から生まれた。Pythonに似た簡潔な構文を採用しつつ、静的・動的型付けの併用、契約プログラミング(事前条件・事後条件・単体テスト)、コンパイル時のnil検査などを取り入れ、.NET/Mono上で動作する言語として設計された。
summary: 開発は2013年のバージョン0.9.6を最後に実質的に停止しており、現在は使われていない歴史的言語である。
problem_en: Cobra was designed by Charles Esterbrook to combine the productivity and readability of scripting languages with the robustness of statically-typed platforms. It adopted a clean, Python-like syntax while supporting both static and dynamic typing with type inference, contracts and assertions, unit testing built into the language, lambda expressions, closures, list comprehensions, generators, and compile-time nil-tracking for null safety, targeting the Microsoft .NET and Mono runtimes.
summary_en: Development effectively stopped after the final 0.9.6 release in December 2013, and Cobra is now a discontinued, historical language with no active user base, even though its source was open-sourced under the MIT License in 2008.

name: ColdFusion (CFML)
problem: Web開発において、HTMLファイルにデータベース操作や条件分岐、高度な書式設定機能などを直接組み込みたいという要求から生まれた。タグベースの構文(CFML)によって、HTMLに近い記法のままサーバーサイドの動的処理を記述できる、Web専用の高水準言語として設計された。
summary: Allaire、Macromedia、Adobeと開発元を変えながら商用製品として存続しており、現在もAdobe ColdFusionとして新バージョンが継続的にリリースされている。オープンソース実装のLuceeも登場し、レガシーなCFMLコードベースの保守を含め現役で使われ続けている。
problem_en: ColdFusion was created by Jeremy Allaire and Joseph J. Allaire to make it easy to augment plain HTML files with database commands, conditional operators, high-level formatting functions, and other elements needed to build dynamic web applications, at a time when writing such logic directly required lower-level CGI programming. Its tag-based markup language, CFML, let developers add server-side logic using a syntax that looked like an extension of HTML itself, alongside a JavaScript-like CFScript syntax and reusable ColdFusion Components (CFCs) for object-oriented programming.
summary_en: ColdFusion changed hands from Allaire Corporation (1995) to Macromedia (2001) and then Adobe Systems (2005), but has remained a commercially maintained product throughout, running on the JVM, .NET, and Google App Engine. An open-source CFML engine, Lucee, emerged in 2015 to modernize the platform, and Adobe continues to release new ColdFusion versions today, so the language remains actively used, particularly for maintaining and extending existing enterprise web applications.

name: COMTRAN
problem: FORTRANが科学技術計算向けの高水準言語として登場する中、商用(事務)処理分野にも同様の高水準言語が必要だと考えられ、IBMの「商用翻訳言語(COMmercial TRANslator)」として設計された。FLOW-MATICの影響を受けつつ、PICTURE句や段落(パラグラフ)構造など、後にCOBOLへ引き継がれる要素を多数導入した。
summary: 言語自体はCOBOL制定とともに姿を消したが、PICTURE句や段落構造、GO TOによる制御など多くの設計要素が直接COBOLに組み込まれ、事務処理言語の系譜における重要な先駆けとなった。
problem_en: As FORTRAN succeeded as a high-level language for scientific and technical computing, IBM's Bob Bemer designed COMTRAN ("COMmercial TRANslator") in 1957 to be the business-programming equivalent of FORTRAN. Influenced by FLOW-MATIC, COMTRAN introduced features such as the PICTURE clause (the first language to have one), a paragraph structure with non-significant line breaks, named paragraphs reachable via GO TO, an AT END clause for file operations, the figurative constant HIGH-VALUE, and a RETURN-CODE mechanism for communicating with the operating system.
summary_en: COMTRAN itself faded from use once COBOL was standardized, but it served as one of COBOL's direct forerunners: the picture clause, paragraph structure and naming conventions, and several other syntactic features were carried over almost directly into COBOL, making COMTRAN an important historical stepping stone in the lineage of business data-processing languages.

name: Control Language (CL)
problem: System/38、および後継のOS/400(現IBM i)において、コマンドのパラメータを名前付きで任意の順序で指定でき、Unix/DOSに見られる位置依存パラメータの問題を避けられるコマンド言語が必要とされた。IBM独自のコマンドオブジェクト(*CMD)機構により、パラメータの検証やF4キーによる入力補完・プロンプト機能を統一的に提供する言語として設計された。
summary: IBM iプラットフォームの中核をなす言語として現在も現役で使われており、Windows PowerShellの設計にも影響を与えたとされる。
problem_en: For the System/38 Control Program Facility and its successor OS/400 (now IBM i), IBM needed a command language in which parameters could be specified by name in any order, each mapped internally to a specific position when passed to a program — avoiding the positional-parameter dependency problems seen in Unix and DOS shells. CL commands are defined as command objects (*CMD) that can validate their own parameters and offer a built-in prompting interface (the F4 key) so users can be guided through valid values interactively.
summary_en: Control Language remains the core scripting and command language of the IBM i platform today, with well over two thousand built-in commands as of version 7R3, and it is credited as an influence on the design of Windows PowerShell, whose named, order-independent parameters echo CL's approach.

name: CORAL 66
problem: 英国国防省(Royal Radar Establishment)は、処理能力の限られた組み込み・リアルタイム計算機上でも使える高水準言語を必要としていた。CORAL 66は、動的メモリ割り当てを前提とせず固定小数点演算しかサポートしない機種でも動作するよう、ALGOL 60をベースにしつつ、強力な実行時チェックやインラインアセンブリの組み込みなどの機能を備えて1964年に設計され、1970年に正式に規格化された。
summary: 英国の軍事・産業システムで長く使われ、そのコンパイラ品質保証(コンパイラ認証)の手法が米国防省によるAdaの標準化にも参照されたとされる。1976年、エリザベス2世が英国君主として初めて送った電子メールがこのCORAL 66コンパイラの利用可能性を伝える内容だったという逸話でも知られる。
problem_en: The UK Ministry of Defence (via the Royal Radar Establishment) needed a high-level language usable on embedded and real-time computers with limited processing power, including machines restricted to fixed-point arithmetic with no support for dynamic memory allocation. CORAL 66, designed by Philip Woodward, I. F. Currie, and M. Griffiths starting in 1964 and formally defined in 1970, was based on ALGOL 60 but added structured record types similar to those later found in Pascal, data-packing facilities for constrained storage, inline assembly language support, and strong runtime checking and diagnostics, while also drawing on ideas from JOVIAL and Fortran.
summary_en: CORAL 66 was used for many years in UK military and industrial systems, and its approach to compiler quality control (compiler certification) is said to have been referenced when the U.S. Department of Defense defined Ada. It is also remembered for the anecdote that on 26 March 1976, Queen Elizabeth II became the first head of state to send an email, over ARPANET, announcing the availability of a CORAL 66 compiler.

name: Cryptol
problem: 暗号アルゴリズムの設計・実装・検証を専門に行うための言語が必要とされた。米国NSA向けに開発され、暗号仕様を数学的記述に近い形で表現し、ストリーム処理関数として暗号アルゴリズムの挙動を検証できるようにすることを目的としている。Haskellの影響を受けた構文を持つ。なお、英語版Wikipediaのインフォボックスは登場年を出典なしで「1980」としているが、開発元Galois, Inc.自体が1999年設立であることと整合せず、正確な登場年は一次資料上で確認できなかった。
summary: 現在もGalois社によって開発が継続され、Rockwell Collinsなど防衛関連企業でも採用されているニッチな暗号仕様記述・検証用DSLである。
problem_en: Cryptol is a domain-specific language developed by Galois, Inc. (Portland, Oregon) for all aspects of designing, implementing, and verifying cryptography, including the design of new ciphers. It lets cryptographers observe how stream-processing functions manipulate encryption algorithms, expressing cryptographic specifications in a form close to mathematical notation, with a syntax influenced by Haskell. It was originally developed for use by the U.S. National Security Agency and is used by defense contractors such as Rockwell Collins. Note: the English Wikipedia infobox lists an uncited "First appeared: 1980", which is inconsistent with Galois, Inc. itself having been founded in 1999; the precise year of Cryptol's first appearance could not be reliably confirmed from primary sources during this research.
summary_en: Cryptol continues to be actively developed by Galois, Inc. (latest stable release 3.2.0, August 2024) and is used by defense-related organizations such as Rockwell Collins for aerospace applications, making it a niche but actively maintained domain-specific language for cryptographic specification and verification.

name: Csound
problem: 音響信号処理・音楽合成を、テキストで記述する「オーケストラ(楽器定義)」と「スコア(演奏データ)」によって柔軟に行いたいという要求から生まれた。MITメディアラボのBarry Vercoeが、自身の先行システムMusic 11を発展させる形で1985年に開発し、MUSIC-N系譜のユニットジェネレータモデルを引き継ぎつつ、C言語で書かれた完全にモジュール化・拡張可能なシステムとして設計した。
summary: 現在も学術・実験音楽やサウンドデザインの分野で使われ続けているニッチなDSLであり、リアルタイムMIDI対応やライブコーディングなど機能拡張が続いている。MPEG-4のStructured Audio Orchestra Language(SAOL)にも影響を与えたとされる。
problem_en: Csound was created to let users describe sound synthesis and audio signal processing flexibly through a text-based "orchestra" (instrument definitions) and "score" (performance data). Barry Vercoe, at the MIT Media Lab, developed it in 1985 as an evolution of his earlier system Music 11, carrying forward the unit-generator model of the MUSIC-N lineage while making Csound, written in C, completely modular and extensible by the user. Later development was continued by John Fitch, Steven Yi, and Victor Lazzarini among others.
summary_en: Csound remains in active niche use today in academic and experimental music, and in sound design, with nearly 1,700 unit generators as of 2024, ongoing extensions such as real-time MIDI support, multi-dimensional arrays, user-defined types, live coding with orchestra recompilation during performance, and multi-core support. It is also cited as an influence on MPEG-4's Structured Audio Orchestra Language (SAOL).

name: Curl
problem: Webアプリケーションが、マークアップ・スクリプティング・コンパイル済みコードといった異なる言語やツール、フレームワークで書かれたコンポーネントの組み合わせになってしまうという、Web開発における長年の問題を解決したかった。MITのSteve Wardらが、マークアップ(HTML相当)、スクリプティング(JavaScript相当)、コンパイル可能なプログラミングの3層を単一の言語・処理系に統合する「Curl」を1998年に設計した。
summary: MIT発のCurl Corporationおよびその後継企業によって商用製品として継続的に開発されており、2025年時点でもWindows向けに新バージョンがリリースされているニッチな言語である。
problem_en: Curl was designed at MIT, led by Steve Ward, to address a long-standing problem in web development: a web application often ends up being made of components written in different languages, tools, and frameworks (markup for content, a scripting language for behavior, and a compiled language for performance-critical logic). Curl unified all three layers — HTML-like markup, JavaScript-like scripting, and compiled, object-oriented programming with multiple inheritance and reflection — into one language and runtime, which could be just-in-time compiled to native code and also supported offline, "occasionally connected computing."
summary_en: Curl has been developed continuously as a commercial product by Curl Corporation and its successor companies since 1998, with the latest stable release (8.0.15) shipping in October 2025, though it is now Windows-only after Linux and macOS support was dropped in 2019. It remains a niche language, and its "builder" style of layout syntax is noted as an influence on Groovy on the JVM.

name: Cyclone
problem: C言語がもたらすバッファオーバーフローなどのメモリ安全性の脆弱性を、Cのシステムプログラミングとしての強力さや利便性を損なわずに解消したいという研究目的で開発された。AT&T Labs ResearchのTrevor JimとコーネルのGreg Morrisettらの研究グループが、3種類のポインタ型やリージョンベースのメモリ管理、境界チェック付きのファットポインタなどを備えた「安全なC方言」として2001年から設計を開始し、2006年にバージョン1.0をリリースした。
summary: 開発自体は停止しており、64bit環境への対応もないまま歴史的な研究言語となっているが、そのアイデアの多くはRustの設計に取り入れられたとされ、後継の安全性重視言語の先駆けとして参照される存在である。
problem_en: Cyclone was a research project intended to be a safe dialect of the C language, designed to avoid buffer overflows and other memory-safety vulnerabilities that are possible in C programs, without losing the power and convenience of C as a tool for systems programming. Developed starting in 2001 by Trevor Jim at AT&T Labs Research together with Greg Morrisett's group at Cornell University, it introduced three pointer types with different safety guarantees, region-based memory management to prevent dangling pointers, bounds-checked "fat" pointers, optional garbage collection, and additional features such as pattern matching, type inference, exceptions, namespaces, and parameterized types. Version 1.0 was released on May 8, 2006.
summary_en: Cyclone is no longer actively developed and its reference tooling lacks 64-bit platform support, making it a historical research language today. However, many of its ideas are explicitly credited by Rust's original developers as having integrated much of what Cyclone pioneered, and it is also cited in connection with Microsoft's Project Verona, making it an important precursor in the lineage of memory-safe systems languages.

name: Cython
problem: 先行するPyrexが持っていた機能上の制約を解消しつつ、Pythonのコードにできるだけ近い書き方を保ったまま、C言語へと変換してネイティブに近い実行速度を得たいという要求から生まれた。SageMath開発者らがPyrexを2007年にフォークし、静的型宣言をオプションで付与できる仕組みや、CPython拡張モジュールを生成する仕組みを整備することで、Pythonの記述性とCの実行性能を両立させる言語として設計した。
summary: SciPy、pandas、scikit-learnなど科学計算エコシステムの基盤技術として広く使われている現役の言語である。
problem_en: Cython was forked from Pyrex by Sage developers, including Robert Bradshaw and Stefan Behnel, in 2007 to overcome limitations in Pyrex while keeping code as close to ordinary Python syntax as possible, and compiling it down to C to achieve performance approaching native C. It added more features and optimizations than Pyrex, allows optional static type declarations to speed up execution, provides a foreign function interface for integrating with C/C++, and generates CPython extension modules, supporting both Python 2 and Python 3 syntax.
summary_en: Cython is heavily used today as foundational technology in the scientific Python ecosystem, including projects such as SciPy, pandas, and scikit-learn, as well as SageMath and lxml, and remains under active development, making it a live, widely used language rather than a historical curiosity.

name: DataFlex
problem: 1980年代当時、多様なハードウェア・OSが混在する中で、アプリケーションコードをほぼどの環境でも動かせるようにしたいという移植性への要求から生まれた。Data Access Corporationは、独自の中間バイトコードにコンパイルする方式を採用し、データベース処理を中心とした第4世代言語(4GL)としてDataFlexを1982年に開発した。
summary: 開発元のData Access Worldwideにより現在も活発に開発が続けられ、Windows・Web・モバイルに対応する商用の4GL/IDE製品として現役で使われている。
problem_en: In the early 1980s, with a wide variety of incompatible hardware and operating systems in use, there was a strong demand for application code that could run on almost any system architecture regardless of the underlying hardware. Data Access Corporation (founded 1976, now Data Access Worldwide) developed DataFlex in 1982 as a fourth-generation, database-oriented language and IDE that compiled to an intermediate bytecode for portability, supporting multiple database backends over its history, including Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.
summary_en: DataFlex is described as a relatively early example of a fully-fledged, commercially used fourth-generation programming language, comparable in role to Visual Basic, Delphi, or C++ for building database applications. It remains under active development by Data Access Worldwide today, with version 25.0 released in June 2025, and an installed base of roughly three million users worldwide, running on Windows, web, and mobile platforms.

name: dc
problem: Unix上で、高水準言語の実装に先立って任意精度演算を伴う実用的な計算処理を行いたいという要求から生まれた。AT&T ベル研究所のLorinda CherryとRobert Morrisが、逆ポーランド記法(RPN)によるスタックベースの操作、レジスタ、マクロ、条件分岐やループを備えた「デスク計算機(desk calculator)」dcを設計し、C言語自体よりも早い時期からPDP-11上で使われていた。
summary: 現存する最古のUnix言語プログラムの一つとされ、bcの実装基盤としても使われてきた。今日でも標準的なUnix/Linuxシステムに搭載され続けている現役のツールである。
problem_en: On early Unix systems, there was a need for a practical way to perform arbitrary-precision arithmetic before higher-level languages were even available. Lorinda Cherry and Robert Morris at AT&T Bell Laboratories designed dc ("desk calculator") as a cross-platform, stack-based, reverse-Polish-notation calculator supporting registers, macros, conditionals, and loops, with multiple input/output radices; it ran on the PDP-11 even before the C programming language itself existed.
summary_en: dc is described as one of the oldest surviving Unix utilities and arguably the oldest surviving Unix language program. The bc calculator language was traditionally implemented on top of dc using infix notation as a more familiar alternative, and modern GNU bc is still built on GNU dc internally, making dc a foundational tool that continues to ship with standard Unix and Linux systems today.

name: DCL (DIGITAL Command Language)
problem: 1970年代、DECは複数の異なるオペレーティングシステム(IAS、RSTS/E、RSX-11、RT-11など)を並行して開発していたが、それぞれが独自のコマンド言語(CCLやRSX-11のMCRなど)を持ち、利用者はOSごとに異なる操作方法を覚え直す必要があった。DECはこれらを統一し、どのOS上でも共通の作法でファイル操作やプログラム実行、条件分岐を行えるコマンド言語を必要としていた。
summary: OpenVMS(旧VMS)の標準コマンド言語として設計され、現在もVSI(VMS Software Inc.)によって開発が継続されている。
problem_en:
Throughout the 1970s, Digital Equipment Corporation was developing several different operating systems in parallel — IAS, RSTS/E, RSX-11, RT-11, and later VAX/VMS — and each had grown its own command language (such as CCL, or MCR on RSX-11). Users who moved between DEC systems had to relearn a different set of commands and conventions each time, which was a burden both for end users and for DEC's own support and documentation efforts.

DCL was created to unify this experience: a single command language, with a consistent '$'-prefixed verb syntax, IF-THEN-ELSE conditionals, and lexical functions for querying system state, that could be layered onto multiple DEC operating systems and later become the standard shell of VAX/VMS (OpenVMS).
summary_en:
DCL became the standard interactive and scripting command language of OpenVMS, and is still maintained today by VSI (VMS Software Inc.), the company that continues OpenVMS development after DEC/Compaq/HP. Community ports such as PC-DCL and Open DCL also let DCL scripts run on Windows, Linux, and Unix.

It is now a legacy technology tied to the shrinking population of OpenVMS installations (status: legacy), but it remains historically notable as an early, unusually structured command-line shell — some retrospectives note stylistic parallels between DCL's qualifier syntax and lexical functions and later shells such as Windows PowerShell, though Wikipedia does not document a direct lineage claim beyond listing PowerShell under "Influenced".

name: DIBOL
problem: 1970年前後、中小企業向けの経理・在庫管理などの業務処理(MIS: Management Information Systems)ソフトウェアを、当時のミニコン上で効率よく開発したいという要求があった。COBOLは表現力があるが記述量が多く、DECの小型機で使うには重かった。DECは、COBOLのデータ部/手続き部という構造を保ちつつ、FORTRANやBASICに近い簡潔な文法とBCD(二進化十進)演算による正確な金額計算を備えた、業務処理向けの軽量言語を必要とした。
summary: DECのミニコン(PDPシリーズなど)上で長く使われた業務処理向け言語で、1993年に後継のDBLへ実質的に置き換えられた。
problem_en:
Around 1970, small and mid-sized businesses running on DEC minicomputers needed practical software for Management Information Systems (MIS) work such as accounting and inventory management. COBOL offered the expressive power for this kind of data processing, but its verbosity made it a heavy fit for DEC's smaller machines of the era.

DIBOL (Digital's Business Oriented Language) was DEC's answer: it kept COBOL's separation of a data division and a procedure division, but combined it with a syntax closer to FORTRAN and BASIC, plus BCD (binary-coded decimal) arithmetic for exact monetary calculations — giving business programmers a lighter-weight, COBOL-like tool tailored to DEC hardware.
summary_en:
DIBOL was used for many years as a business data-processing language on DEC minicomputers such as the PDP series, going through revisions like DIBOL-8, DIBOL-11, and DIBOL-32. Wikipedia does not name an individual designer; the language is credited to Digital Equipment Corporation as a whole.

Development of DIBOL itself effectively ended in 1993, when an agreement between DEC and DISC replaced it with the successor language DBL on OpenVMS, Digital UNIX, and SCO Unix. It is now a purely historical language (status: historical), remembered mainly as a COBOL-adjacent, DEC-specific business language of the minicomputer era.

name: DRAKON
problem: ソ連の再使用型宇宙往還機ブランに搭載する飛行制御ソフトウェアの開発では、PROL2、DIPOL、LAKSなど複数の異なる言語が並存し、開発者間での意思疎通やレビューが困難になっていた。ロケット工学者や運用担当者など、必ずしもプログラミングの専門家ではない人々にも読める、誤りの少ない統一的な記述手段が必要とされた。
summary: 旧ソ連の宇宙開発計画で生まれた、フローチャートを厳密に形式化したビジュアルなアルゴリズム記述言語で、現在も宇宙・産業分野の一部やソフトウェア教育で使われている。
problem_en:
In the development of flight-control software for the Soviet Buran reusable spacecraft, several different programming languages — PROL2, DIPOL, LAKS among them — were in simultaneous use, which made communication and review across teams difficult. The project needed a single, rigorously defined way of expressing algorithms that could be read not only by professional programmers but also by rocket engineers and mission operators who were not necessarily specialists in coding.

Vladimir Parondzhanov, together with participants from the Russian space agency's Pilyugin Center and the Keldysh Institute of Applied Mathematics, developed DRAKON as an answer: a strictly formalized flowchart notation (its Russian name is an acronym roughly meaning "a friendly Russian algorithmic language that ensures clarity") intended to make algorithms unambiguous and easy to follow regardless of the reader's programming background.
summary_en:
DRAKON is a visual algorithmic language built on a strict formalization of flowcharts, using a fixed set of icons and macro-icons (27 icons and 21 macro-icons per the Japanese Wikipedia article) to describe control flow in a way that stays legible however complex the logic becomes. Its accompanying CASE tool, Grafit-Floks, was completed in 1996, and DRAKON diagrams have been used on projects including Sea Launch, the Fregat upper stage, and the upgraded Proton-M launch vehicle, as well as at the German Aerospace Center (DLR).

Today it survives as a niche but living notation (status: niche): DRAKON-flavored hybrid languages such as DRAKON-C, DRAKON-Java, and DRAKON-ASM let a DRAKON diagram generate code in an existing target language, and free tools such as the DRAKON Editor keep it in occasional use for teaching algorithmic thinking and for business-process modeling outside the aerospace domain that produced it.

name: DYNAMO
problem: MITのJay Wright Forresterは、工場の在庫や生産計画がなぜ振動的に不安定になるのか(いわゆる「インダストリアル・ダイナミクス」)を数理モデルで説明しようとしていたが、モデルを解くたびに専門のプログラマーに依頼して個別に手でコーディングしてもらう必要があり、モデルの試行錯誤が非常に遅かった。専門のプログラマーでない研究者自身が、方程式を書くだけでシミュレーションを実行し結果を得られる仕組みが必要とされた。
summary: システムダイナミクスの創始者Forresterのもとで開発された、差分方程式によるシステムシミュレーション専用言語。『成長の限界』などの世界モデルの計算にも使われたが、現在は使われておらず歴史的言語として位置づけられている。
problem_en:
At MIT, Jay Wright Forrester was trying to explain, through mathematical modeling, why factory inventories and production schedules tended to oscillate unpredictably — the field he came to call "industrial dynamics." But every time he wanted to test a model, he had to hand it to a professional programmer to be coded by hand from scratch, which made iterating on a model painfully slow. What was needed was a way for the researchers themselves — not specialist programmers — to simply write down a system's equations and get simulation results back from a single run.

DYNAMO (DYNAmic MOdels), developed under Forrester's direction with Phyllis Fox, Alexander L. Pugh III, Grace Duren, and others at the MIT Computation Center from the late 1950s, grew out of an earlier proof-of-concept called SIMPLE and answered this need directly: a simulation language aimed at people who were not expert programmers, with immediate execution, graphical output, units checking, and clear error messages.
summary_en:
DYNAMO became the standard tool of the system dynamics field that Forrester founded, and its scope broadened over time from industrial dynamics to population studies, resource analysis, and urban planning. It was implemented on IBM 704/709/7090 assembly and later versions generated portable FORTRAN, and it was also realized on top of AED-0 and ALGOL 60. Its best-known use was as the computational engine behind the Club of Rome's 1972 world model published as *The Limits to Growth*.

According to Wikipedia, DYNAMO "has since fallen into disuse" and is now purely a historical language (status: historical); Wikipedia does not give a precise first-release year, only that development began in the late 1950s following a 1958 prototype and that a DYNAMO User's Manual was published by MIT Press in 1963. It remains significant chiefly for its historical role in the system dynamics movement rather than for any continuing practical use.

name: DAX (Data Analysis Expressions)
problem: Excelの数式は表計算のセル単位の計算には強いが、複数テーブルにまたがるリレーショナルなデータモデルに対して集計や比較(前年同月比など)を行う計算を表現するのは難しかった。一方、SQLやMDXは強力だが、Excelユーザーにとって馴染みのある数式的な書き方とは大きく異なっていた。MicrosoftはProject Geminiというセルフサービス型BIの取り組みの中で、Excelの数式に近い書き心地でありながら、リレーショナルなデータモデル上で動的な集計ができる言語を必要とした。
summary: PowerPivotやPower BI、SQL Server Analysis Servicesで使われる数式/クエリ言語で、Excel関数に似た書き心地でリレーショナルなデータモデルの集計・分析を行える。
problem_en:
Excel formulas are well suited to cell-by-cell spreadsheet calculation, but expressing aggregations and comparisons (such as year-over-year totals) across a relational model spanning multiple tables was difficult with formulas alone. SQL and MDX could do this kind of relational aggregation, but their syntax was far removed from the formula-style notation that Excel users were already comfortable with.

As part of "Project Gemini," Microsoft's push toward self-service business intelligence, the SQL Server Analysis Services team needed a language that felt like an Excel formula to the end user while being able to perform dynamic aggregation over a proper relational/tabular data model.
summary_en:
DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) was released in 2009 as part of Project Gemini and is now the native formula and query language of Microsoft PowerPivot, Power BI Desktop, and SQL Server Analysis Services (Tabular mode). It reuses many function names familiar from Excel formulas while adding functions designed for relational data and dynamic aggregation, and it supports Calculated Columns, Measures, and Calculated Tables.

DAX is under active development (status: active); by the time of Power BI's 2016 expansion and SQL Server 2016, it had grown to roughly 340 functions along with calculated tables, automatic date tables, and variables, and it remains the primary way analysts write business logic inside Power BI and other Microsoft BI tools today. Wikipedia's article does not name an individual designer, crediting the language instead to the SQL Server Analysis Services team at Microsoft.

name: Epigram
problem: 従来の関数型言語では、型は値とは別次元の静的な検査にすぎず、「長さnのベクトル」のように値に依存する性質をそのまま型として表現することができなかった。Conor McBrideとJames McKinnaは、型を第一級の存在として扱い、依存型と依存パターンマッチによって「型で仕様を表し、その仕様どおりにしか書けない」プログラムを実現できる言語を必要としていた。
summary: 依存型と依存パターンマッチを実用的なプログラミングスタイルとして提示した研究用言語で、後のIdrisやAgdaに直接影響を与えたが、現在は開発が停止している。
problem_en: In conventional functional languages, types live on a separate, static level from values, so a property that depends on a value — such as "a vector of exactly length n" — could not be expressed directly as a type. Conor McBride and James McKinna wanted a language that treated types as first-class entities and used dependent types together with dependent pattern matching, so that a specification written as a type could constrain a program to be provably correct with respect to that specification.
summary_en:
Epigram, first released in 2006 (version 1), demonstrated dependent types and dependent pattern matching as a practical programming style rather than purely a theoretical exercise, with the function's argument type able to appear inside the type of its result. According to Wikipedia, Epigram is listed as having influenced both Idris and Agda, making it an important stepping stone in the line of research that led to today's dependently typed languages.

Epigram itself is now unmaintained (status: historical); a planned version 2, intended to implement Observational Type Theory, was never officially released and exists only in incomplete form on GitHub. Its lasting significance lies in the ideas it popularized rather than in any continued practical use.

name: Euler
problem: ALGOL 60は当時の標準的な手続き型言語だったが、型の扱いが厳格で、手続きが呼び出しごとに異なる型の値を返すような柔軟な処理や、参照・記号・リストといった多様な値をひとまとめに扱うことができなかった。Niklaus WirthとHelmut Weberは、ALGOL 60をより単純かつ柔軟に拡張し、動的型付けやリスト構造を取り込んだ言語を必要としていた。
summary: Niklaus WirthがPascalを設計する以前に、Helmut Weberと共同でALGOL 60の拡張として設計した言語で、現在は歴史的言語として位置づけられている。
problem_en: ALGOL 60 was the standard procedural language of its time, but its strict, static typing made it awkward to write procedures whose return type could vary from call to call, or to work uniformly with a mix of value kinds — references, labels, symbols, lists — within a single flexible data structure. Niklaus Wirth and Helmut Weber wanted a language that extended ALGOL 60 into something simpler yet more flexible, incorporating dynamic typing and list structures.
summary_en:
Euler, first appearing in 1965, was conceived by Wirth and Weber explicitly as "an extension and generalization of ALGOL 60," aiming to be simpler yet more flexible than its parent. It introduced dynamic typing (variables were not fixed to one type), a small set of data types beyond ordinary constants — Reference, Label, Symbol, List (array), Procedure, and Undefined — and procedures whose return type could differ between invocations, with list elements able to mix types to build tree-like structures. It ran on the Burroughs B5500, among other machines.

Euler predates Wirth's later, far more influential work on Pascal, and is now purely of historical interest (status: historical): Wikipedia's article gives little information about any practical or contemporary use beyond its original implementation and a later Icon-based reimplementation from around 2000–2001.

name: Ezhil (எழில்)
problem: プログラミング教育の入門教材は英語のキーワードや構文を前提とすることが多く、英語を母語としないタミル語話者の児童・生徒にとっては、プログラミングの概念そのものよりも先に英単語や英文法を学ぶことが障壁になっていた。Muthiah Annamalaiは、タミル語の語彙と文法構造そのものでプログラムを記述できる言語を用意することで、K-12世代のタミル語話者がより自然にプログラミングの概念を学べるようにする必要があった。
summary: タミル語のキーワードと文法でプログラムを書ける教育用インタプリタ言語で、Pythonで実装されている。
problem_en: Introductory programming education is usually built around English keywords and syntax, which for Tamil-speaking children means having to learn English vocabulary and grammar before even reaching the underlying programming concepts. Muthiah Annamalai wanted a language whose keywords and grammatical structure were themselves Tamil, so that K-12 age native Tamil speakers could approach programming concepts more directly, closer to how they already think and speak.
summary_en:
Ezhil (Tamil: எழில், romanized Eḻil, meaning "beauty") first appeared around 2007 and was officially announced in 2009, created by Muthiah Annamalai as an interpreted, imperative language whose program text is written in Tamil script and follows Tamil grammatical constructs rather than an English-based syntax. It offers over 350 built-in functions, dynamic typing, and recursion, and runs cross-platform (Linux, Windows, macOS) as a Python-based implementation, distributed as open source under the GPLv3 license.

It remains a niche but living project (status: niche) focused on K-12 computer-science education for Tamil speakers, with a stable 0.99 release in August 2017 and a 10rc0 preview in March 2021.

name: FAUST (Functional AUdio STream)
problem: 音響信号処理(DSP)のアルゴリズムを、C++などの汎用言語で直接実装すると、サンプル単位の低レベルな最適化と、信号の流れを表す高レベルな構造記述とが混在し、コードが読みにくく再利用しにくくなりがちだった。GRAME(フランス国立音楽創造センター)のYann Orlarey、Dominique Fober、Stéphane Letzは、信号処理をブロック図的な合成演算子で純粋関数的に記述し、そこから確定的でメモリ使用量が一定な低レベルDSPコードを自動生成できる言語を必要としていた。
summary: 音響DSP処理を関数的な信号処理ブロックの合成として記述できるドメイン特化言語で、C++やRustなど多様な言語のコードを生成し、現在も活発に開発が続いている。
problem_en: Implementing digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms directly in a general-purpose language like C++ tends to mix low-level, sample-by-sample optimization with the high-level structure of how signals flow through a system, making the resulting code hard to read and hard to reuse. Yann Orlarey, Dominique Fober, and Stéphane Letz at GRAME (Centre National de Création Musicale) wanted a language that could express signal processing purely functionally, as the composition of block-diagram-style operators, and from that description automatically generate deterministic, constant-memory low-level DSP code.
summary_en:
FAUST (Functional AUdio STream), first appearing in 2002, is a purely functional, text-based language for describing DSP algorithms as libraries, audio plug-ins, or standalone applications, blending functional composition operators with a block-diagram way of thinking about signal flow. It compiles down to sample-level DSP code in C++, C, Java, Rust, WebAssembly, and other targets, and supports over 30 architecture files covering different platforms and plug-in formats.

Maintained by GRAME under the GPL as free and open-source software, FAUST is under active development (status: active) — its latest stable release was version 2.83.1 in December 2025 — and it won the 2022 Open Science Award for Open Source Research Software in the Documentation category.

name: Flavors
problem: MIT AIラボのLispマシン上では、Lisp Machine Lisp自体はオブジェクト指向の仕組みを持たず、複数の振る舞いの断片を組み合わせて1つのオブジェクトの型を作るような柔軟な拡張ができなかった。Howard Cannonは、複数の独立した「フレーバー」を合成してオブジェクトの振る舞いを組み立てられる、非階層的なオブジェクト指向の仕組みをLisp上に持ち込む必要があった。
summary: MIT AIラボのLispマシン向けに開発された、Lispへの初期のオブジェクト指向拡張で、mixin(混入)を初めて導入した言語として知られ、後のCLOS(Common Lisp Object System)に大きな影響を与えた。
problem_en: On MIT AI Lab's Lisp machines, the underlying Lisp Machine Lisp had no object-oriented facilities of its own, so there was no flexible way to compose several independent fragments of behavior into a single object's type. Howard Cannon set out to bring a non-hierarchical object-oriented mechanism to Lisp, in which independent "flavors" could be composed together to build up an object's behavior.
summary_en:
Flavors is an early object-oriented extension to Lisp, developed by Howard Cannon at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory for the Lisp machine and its Lisp Machine Lisp language. It is notable as the first programming language to include mixins, used a message-passing object model, and offered :before/:after "daemons" as part of its default method combination. Symbolics adopted it for its Lisp machines and later evolved it into New Flavors, which replaced message sending with generic function calls; both variants were hugely influential in the design of the Common Lisp Object System (CLOS).

Wikipedia's article does not state an exact year Flavors was first created; the earliest primary documentation it cites is the MIT AI Lab's 1980 "Flavors, Technical Report" and Daniel Weinreb and David Moon's A.I. Memo No. 602, "Flavors: Message Passing in the Lisp Machine" (November 1980), which is the value used here. Flavors is now a historical language (status: historical), though implementations still exist for Common Lisp.

name: Flix
designers: オープンソースコミュニティ
problem: 関数型言語は純粋性や型の表現力に優れるが、実務のプログラムには宣言的な関係(グラフの到達可能性のような再帰的なルール)を扱いたい場面もあり、そのたびにDatalogのような論理型言語との連携を別途用意する必要があった。またJVM上で純粋な関数型コードと副作用のあるコードを型システムで明確に区別する仕組みも十分ではなかった。デンマーク・オーフス大学の研究者たちは、関数型・命令型・論理型(Datalog)を1つの静的型システムの中で統合し、副作用を型と効果システムで区別できる言語を必要としていた。
summary: 関数型・命令型・論理型(Datalogによる第一級の制約)を統合したJVM上の研究言語で、オーフス大学を中心にオープンソースで開発が続けられている。
problem_en: Functional languages excel at purity and expressive type systems, but real programs sometimes need to state declarative relations — recursive rules like graph reachability — which traditionally meant reaching for a separate logic language such as Datalog. At the same time, JVM languages did not cleanly separate pure functional code from code with side effects at the type level. Researchers at Aarhus University in Denmark wanted a language that unified functional, imperative, and logic (Datalog) programming inside one static type system, with a type-and-effect system to keep pure and impure code visibly distinct.
summary_en:
Flix is a functional, imperative, and logic programming language that runs on the JVM, developed at Aarhus University with funding from the Independent Research Fund Denmark and a community of open-source contributors. It supports algebraic data types, pattern matching, parametric polymorphism, currying, higher-order functions, extensible records, and channel/process-based concurrency, and its type-and-effect system separates pure and impure code; distinctively, it also treats Datalog constraints as first-class, composable values, letting logic programs be embedded directly inside functional code. Wikipedia's infobox lists F#, Go, Haskell, OCaml, and Scala under "Influenced by."

Wikipedia does not state an exact "first appeared" year or name an individual designer (academic papers describing Flix's design, some co-authored by Magnus Madsen, are cited from 2016 and 2020, which is the basis for the year used here). It remains a niche, actively developed open-source research language (status: niche) with editor support in Visual Studio Code and roughly 2,700 GitHub stars as of the most recent check.

name: FOCAL
problem: DECのPDP-8のような小型で対話的な計算機では、専門知識がなくてもその場で数式を入力し即座に結果を得られる、JOSSのような対話型言語が有用だった。しかしJOSSはJohnniac機に特化しており、DECの小型機でも同様に手軽に使える対話型言語が必要とされていた。Richard Merrillは、限られたメモリしか持たないPDP-8上でも動作する、JOSSに似た対話的な計算用言語を実装する必要があった。
summary: DECのPDP-8など向けにJOSSをもとに開発された対話型言語で、BASICと競合したが普及に失敗し、後にソビエト連邦のPDP-11互換機で独自の復活を見せた。
problem_en: On small, interactive computers such as DEC's PDP-8, a JOSS-style interactive language — one where a non-specialist could type in a formula and get an answer immediately — was highly useful. But JOSS itself was tied to the Johnniac machine, so DEC needed an equally approachable interactive language for its own small systems. Richard Merrill set out to implement a JOSS-like interactive calculation language that could run within the tight memory constraints of the PDP-8.
summary_en:
