problem: 型システムの多相性(polymorphism)と、直交永続性(orthogonal persistence: 任意の型のデータをプログラムの実行終了後も透過的に保存できる仕組み)を組み合わせた、永続プログラミングの概念実証を行いたかった。
summary: 現在は開発が止まっている歴史的言語だが、多相型システムと直交永続性を頑健に組み合わせた最初の言語として位置づけられている。
problem_en: Napier88 was designed and implemented at the University of St Andrews, Scotland, primarily by Ron Morrison, with the implementation extended by Fred Brown, Richard Connor, and Al Dearle. It first appeared in 1988 as a proof-of-concept for an experiment in persistent programming, aiming to combine a polymorphic type system with orthogonal persistence - the property that data of any type can be transparently preserved beyond the end of a program's execution - in a single, robustly implemented language.
summary_en: Napier88 is now a historical language whose development ceased sometime after 1989 (the year its first implementation was actually released) once the research group's interests moved elsewhere; at its peak it had up to 1,000 registered users. It is historically significant as the first robustly implemented language to combine a polymorphic type system with orthogonal persistence.

name: Neko
problem: Haxe開発者Nicolas Cannasseが、ゲーム会社(フランス・ボルドー)でのR&D活動の一環として、組み込み可能な高水準動的型付けスクリプト言語と、それを実行する軽量な仮想マシンを必要としていた。
summary: Haxeのコンパイルターゲットの一つとしても使われる、ニッチなスクリプト言語兼VM。MITライセンスで開発が続けられている。
problem_en: Neko was designed by Nicolas Cannasse - also the creator of Haxe - as a high-level, dynamically typed programming language, together with NekoVM, the virtual machine that executes its bytecode. It was developed in 2005 as part of R&D work at video game companies in Bordeaux, France, to serve both as an embeddable scripting language and as a compilation target for other languages, most notably Haxe. Note: the English Wikipedia title 'Neko (programming language)' redirects to a combined article titled 'NekoVM' covering both the virtual machine and the language together; there is no separately titled language-only article.
summary_en: Neko remains a niche language today, maintained by the Haxe Foundation together with Shiro Games and Motion Twin under the MIT license, with its latest cited stable release being 2.3.0 (24 October 2019); it continues to serve chiefly as one of Haxe's compilation targets rather than as a widely used standalone language.

name: MDL
problem: MITのProject MAC内Dynamic Modeling Groupと人工知能研究所のために、反射的・メタプログラミング機能を備えた高水準のLisp系言語サポートが必要だった。
summary: 現在は使われていない歴史的言語だが、Scheme・Common Lisp・Prologなど多数の言語に影響を与え、アドベンチャーゲーム『Zork』の開発言語としても知られる。
problem_en: MDL was designed by Gerald Sussman, Carl Hewitt, Chris Reeve, and Bruce Daniels (with David Cressey also involved in the Dynamic Modeling Group) at MIT's Project MAC, first appearing in 1971. It was created to provide high-level, Lisp-based programming language support for the Artificial Intelligence Lab and the Dynamic Modeling Group at MIT, extending Lisp with reflective and meta-programming features.
summary_en: MDL is now an obsolete/historical language, but many of its features were carried forward into later Lisp dialects. Per its Wikipedia infobox, it influenced ZIL, Planner, Scheme, Common Lisp, Java, Prolog, and Smalltalk, as well as the actor model and interactive fiction as a genre; it is also known as the implementation language of the adventure game Zork.

name: Microsoft Power Fx
problem: Microsoft Power Platform(特にPower Apps)向けに、Excelの関数やマクロに慣れたユーザーがアクセスしやすい、表計算感覚のローコード言語が必要だった。
summary: Microsoft Power Platform向けのオープンソース・ローコード言語として現役。2021年11月にMITライセンスでソースコードが公開された。
problem_en: Microsoft Power Fx was designed by a team including Vijay Mital, Robin Abraham, Shon Katzenberger, Darryl Rubin, Greg Lindhorst, and Mike Stall at Microsoft, first appearing in 2021. It was created as a low-code, general-purpose language for the Microsoft Power Platform (notably Power Apps), using spreadsheet-like formulas so that users already familiar with Excel functions and macros could write logic accessibly; per its Wikipedia infobox it was also influenced by Pascal, Mathematica, and Miranda.
summary_en: Power Fx remains an actively developed language today; its source code was released under the MIT License on November 2, 2021, and a 2024 update added Copilot-based features such as 'Explaining a Formula' and 'Generating Power Fx from Natural Language.'

name: Mirah
problem: JRubyの開発者Charles Oliver Nutterが、Rubyのような構文を持ちながら、静的型付け(型推論)でJVMバイトコードに効率よくコンパイルできる言語を作りたかった。
summary: 2016年のリリース以降大きな更新が確認できず、ニッチな存在となっている。
problem_en: Mirah (originally called Duby) was designed by Charles Oliver Nutter (creator of JRuby) to provide a Ruby-like syntax that compiles to solid, fast, idiomatic JVM bytecode, using local type inference and a hybrid static/dynamic type system. Per its Wikipedia infobox it was influenced by Ruby, Java, and Boo. Its name is Javanese wordplay for 'ruby,' referencing Ruby running on the JVM ('Java'). Note: the article does not explicitly state a first-appearance year in prose; 2008 is inferred from the article's categorization.
summary_en: Mirah is a niche language today; its most recent cited stable release is 0.2.1 (September 26, 2016), and as of 2012 the Wikipedia article described it as still under development with only limited production use by some developers.

name: ML
problem: エディンバラ大学の定理証明支援系LCF(Logic for Computable Functions)のために、証明手続きを関数として記述するためのメタ言語(metalanguage)が必要だった。
summary: 現在は歴史的言語だが、Standard ML・OCaml・Haskell・Rust・Scala・Kotlin・F#・Erlangなど、現代の主要言語の多くに直接的な影響を与えたML系言語群の源流。
problem_en: ML was designed by Robin Milner (with Lockwood Morris and Malcolm Newey) at the University of Edinburgh, first appearing in 1973 as a metalanguage for the Edinburgh LCF (Logic for Computable Functions) theorem prover, used to express proof procedures as functions. Its Wikipedia infobox lists ISWIM, POP-2, PAL, and GEDANKEN as influences. Note: this entry is explicitly distinct from Standard ML (dataset id standard_ml) - the English Wikipedia article carries the hatnote 'Not to be confused with Standard ML,' and describes how design fragmentation among early ML dialects led to a later, separate standardization effort that produced Standard ML in 1983.
summary_en: ML is now a historical language, but per its Wikipedia infobox it directly influenced an extraordinary range of later languages, including Standard ML, OCaml, Haskell, Scala, Rust, Kotlin, F#, F*, Erlang, Clojure, Idris, Elm, Miranda, Nemerle, C++, and Coq (now Rocq) - making it one of the most influential root languages in the ML/functional lineage, distinct from (though the direct ancestor of) Standard ML.

name: Modelica
problem: 機械・電気・電子・油圧・熱・制御など複数の工学分野にまたがる複雑なシステムを、コンポーネント指向でモデリングできる統一的な言語が必要だった。
summary: 非営利団体Modelica Associationにより開発が続けられている、マルチドメインの物理システムモデリング言語として現役。
problem_en: Modelica was initiated by Hilding Elmqvist in September 1996, drawing on his PhD thesis and his experience with earlier modeling languages Allan, Dymola, NMF ObjectMath, Omola, SIDOPS+, and Smile; version 1.0 was released in September 1997. It was created as an object-oriented, declarative, multi-domain modeling language for component-oriented modeling of complex systems spanning mechanical, electrical, electronic, hydraulic, thermal, control, and other subsystems.
summary_en: Modelica remains an actively maintained language today, developed under the non-profit Modelica Association; the current stable release of the language specification is 3.6 (March 9, 2023), and its standard libraries are freely available so users can share and develop models without depending on any specific vendor's tool.

name: NELIAC
problem: 1950年代後半、米海軍電子研究所(NEL)は複数の異なる機種(CDC、IBM、UNIVACなど)上で共通に動作する高水準言語コンパイラを必要としていた。ALGOL 58をベースとしつつ、コンパイラ自身がNELIACで書かれ自分自身をコンパイルできる「自己ホスト型(セルフコンパイル)」の設計を採用することで、新しい機種への移植を容易にし、当時の多段パス方式の競合コンパイラに比べて60倍から120倍高速にコンパイルできたとされる。
summary: カナダ海軍の指揮管制システム280(1967-71年)や米海軍のHF方向探知網「Classic Bullseye」(1968年から1990年代初頭まで)などの軍用システムで実運用されたが、米海軍が商用サポート付きのコンパイラへ標準を移したことで使われなくなった歴史的言語である(status: historical)。
problem_en: In the late 1950s, the US Navy Electronics Laboratory (NEL) needed a high-level-language compiler that could run consistently across several different machines (CDC, IBM, UNIVAC, and others). Building on ALGOL 58, NELIAC adopted a self-hosting (bootstrapped) design in which the compiler itself was written in NELIAC and could compile itself, making it far easier to port to new machines. It is reported to have compiled roughly 60 to 120 times faster than the multi-pass competing compilers of its era.
summary_en: NELIAC saw real operational use in military systems such as the Royal Canadian Navy's Command and Control System 280 (1967-71) and the US Navy's HF direction-finding network "Classic Bullseye" (1968 to the early 1990s), but fell out of favor once the Navy standardized on commercially supported compilers, and it is now treated purely as a historical language (status: historical).

name: NESL
problem: 1990年代初頭、並列計算機向けのアルゴリズムを、機種に依存せず簡潔に記述する手段が求められていた。カーネギーメロン大学のSCandALプロジェクトは、関数型言語のスタイルと「入れ子になったデータ並列性(nested data parallelism)」の概念を組み合わせ、「フラット化変換(flattening transformation)」によって入れ子のデータ並列処理を実機上のフラットな並列処理へ変換する仕組みを持つNESLを開発した。プログラムの実行に必要な作業量(work)と深さ(depth)を形式的に見積もれる「言語ベースの性能モデル」を備え、移植性の高い簡潔な並列コードの記述を目指した。
summary: 最終リリースはバージョン3.1(1995年11月)で、それ以降の目立った開発は確認できず、現在は歴史的な言語として位置づけられている(status: historical)。Wikipedia本文では、NESLの入れ子データ並列性の考え方がData Parallel Haskellに大きな影響を与えたと述べられている(この記述はinfoboxではなく本文のみに見られる)。
problem_en: In the early 1990s there was a need for a concise, machine-independent way to express algorithms for parallel computers. The SCandAL project at Carnegie Mellon University combined a functional-language style with the concept of nested data parallelism, and built in a "flattening transformation" that converts nested data-parallel operations into flat parallel operations executable on real hardware. NESL also came with a language-based performance model that could formally estimate the work and depth required to run a program, aiming to make concise, portable parallel code possible.
summary_en: The final release was version 3.1 in November 1995, and no significant further development could be confirmed after that; the language is now treated as historical (status: historical). The Wikipedia article's body text (though not its infobox) states that NESL's approach to nested data parallelism was a major influence on Data Parallel Haskell.

name: NetRexx
problem: 1995年、IBMのMike Cowlishawは、登場して間もないJavaプラットフォーム上で、Rexxの平易な構文を活かしながらオブジェクト指向機能も利用できる言語を模索した。RexxやPL/Iの表現力を保ちつつ、Java仮想マシン(JVM)上で動作し、コンパイルと解釈のどちらの実行方式も選べる言語としてNetRexxが設計された。
summary: 現在もRexx Language Association(RexxLA)によって開発が継続されている(status: niche)。2025年5月にはバージョン5.01がリリースされ、2021年のバージョン4.01ではJava Platform Module Systemへの対応も追加された。利用は一部のRexx/JVM愛好家コミュニティに限られている。
problem_en: In 1995, IBM's Mike Cowlishaw sought a way to keep Rexx's plain, approachable syntax while also gaining access to object-oriented features on the then-new Java platform. NetRexx was designed to preserve the expressiveness of Rexx and PL/I while running on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), with a choice of either compiling or interpreting the source.
summary_en: NetRexx continues to be developed today by the Rexx Language Association (RexxLA) (status: niche). Version 5.01 was released in May 2025, and version 4.01 in 2021 added support for the Java Platform Module System. Its use is largely confined to a niche community of Rexx and JVM enthusiasts.

name: newLISP
problem: Lutz Muellerは、Common LispやSchemeのような本格的なLisp処理系が持つ複雑さや実行環境の重さを避けつつ、Lispらしい記号処理・関数型のスタイルを手軽なスクリプト言語として使いたいと考え、newLISPを設計した。ネットワーク処理や正規表現、XML処理などをあらかじめ言語に組み込み、単一の軽量な実行ファイルとして配布できることを重視した。
summary: 通称「newLISPクラシック」の最終安定版はバージョン10.7.5(2019年5月)である。開発者コミュニティの記録によれば、後方互換性を保ったまま高速化を図った後継実装「newLISP Neo」も存在し、開発は現在も一部で継続されている。日本語版Wikipediaには専用記事がなく、Lisp記事内の方言一覧でも赤リンクとして扱われている。ニッチな用途に限定的に使われる言語である(status: niche)。
problem_en: Lutz Mueller wanted the symbolic, functional style of Lisp available as a lightweight scripting language, without the complexity and heavy runtime of full Lisp systems such as Common Lisp or Scheme. newLISP was designed with networking, regular expressions, and XML processing built directly into the language, and with the ability to be distributed as a single lightweight executable.
summary_en: The final stable release of what is now called "newLISP classic" was version 10.7.5 in May 2019. According to community records, a successor implementation called "newLISP Neo," which preserves backward compatibility while improving performance, also exists and continues to see some ongoing development. Japanese Wikipedia has no dedicated article on newLISP; it appears only as a red (nonexistent-page) link in the dialect table of the Japanese "Lisp" article. It is a niche language with limited use today (status: niche).

name: Object REXX
problem: 1988年、IBMの「Oryx」プロジェクトはSimon C. Nashの技術指導のもとで、伝統的なRexxの構文とSmalltalkのオブジェクトモデルを融合させる実験を行った。手続き型のマクロ言語であったRexxの平易さを保ったまま、クラスベースの継承やポリモーフィズム、メッセージ送信といった本格的なオブジェクト指向機能を持たせることが目標だった。
summary: 1996年にOS/2 Warp 4の一部として製品版がリリースされたが、IBMは2004年10月にObject REXXの開発中止を発表し、権利をRexx Language Association(RexxLA)に譲渡した。RexxLAは2005年、オープンソース版の後継として「ooRexx(Open Object Rexx)」をリリースし、Object REXXの系譜は現在もそちらで継続している。単体の商用製品としてのObject REXXはstatus: legacyの位置づけである。
problem_en: In 1988, IBM's "Oryx" project, under the technical direction of Simon C. Nash, experimented with merging the syntax of classic Rexx with Smalltalk's object model. The goal was to preserve the plain, easy-to-learn style of Rexx (originally a procedural macro language) while adding full object-oriented features such as class-based inheritance, polymorphism, and message passing.
summary_en: A commercial product version shipped as part of OS/2 Warp 4 in 1996, but IBM announced the discontinuation of Object REXX in October 2004 and transferred the rights to the Rexx Language Association (RexxLA). In 2005, RexxLA released "ooRexx" (Open Object Rexx) as its open-source successor, and Object REXX's lineage continues today under that name. As a standalone commercial product, Object REXX itself is now positioned as legacy (status: legacy).

name: Obliq
problem: 1990年代前半、Luca Cardelliらディジタル・イクイップメント・コーポレーション(DEC)のチームは、分散システムやローカルなマルチスレッド計算をより簡単に記述できるオブジェクト指向スクリプト言語を求めていた。Modula-3が持つネットワークオブジェクト機能を活用しながら、Selfのようなプロトタイプベース(委譲による継承)の柔軟なオブジェクトモデルを組み合わせることで、オブジェクトを別のマシンへ安全に複製・移動できる分散計算の仕組みを実現した。
summary: インタプリタ自体がModula-3で実装されており、ディジタル・イクイップメント・コーポレーション(DEC)のModula-3配布物に無償で含まれる形で提供されていた。目立った現行の開発や利用は確認できず、歴史的な言語として位置づけられている(status: historical)。
problem_en: In the early 1990s, Luca Cardelli and colleagues at Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC) wanted an object-oriented scripting language that made distributed systems and local multithreaded computation easier to express. By combining Modula-3's network-objects facility with a flexible, Self-like prototype-based object model based on delegation, Obliq made it possible to clone objects and safely copy or move them across machines for distributed computing.
summary_en: Obliq's interpreter was itself written in Modula-3, and it was distributed free of charge as part of Digital Equipment Corporation's (DEC) Modula-3 distribution. No significant ongoing development or use could be confirmed, and it is now treated as a historical language (status: historical).

name: OmniMark
problem: 1980年代、SGML/XML文書のような構造化テキストを、内容全体をメモリに保持せずに大量かつ高速に変換・処理したいという出版業界のニーズがあった。カナダのExoterica社は「XTRAN」という名称のSGML処理プログラムを開発し、後にOmniMarkへと改称した。パターンと動作(action)を対にした「process」ブロックによるルールベースの記述と、コンテンツを逐次的に流し込みながら処理する「ストリーミング・アーキテクチャ」によって、大容量文書の変換を効率的に行うことを目指した。
summary: 現在はStilo International社の商用製品として提供されており(status: niche)、2022年7月時点での最新版はバージョン11.0である。組み込みのXMLパーサーやXQuery連携(Sednaネイティブ XMLデータベースとの統合)を備え、出版業界でのフォーマット変換用途を中心に使われ続けている。なお正確な初出年はWikipedia上では「1980年代」としか確認できず、しばしば言及される「1986年」という年自体は一次資料上で確認できなかった。
problem_en: In the 1980s, the publishing industry needed a way to transform and process large volumes of structured text such as SGML/XML documents quickly, without holding the entire content in memory. The Canadian company Exoterica developed an SGML-processing program called "XTRAN," later renamed OmniMark. It combined a rule-based style built from "process" blocks pairing patterns with actions, together with a streaming architecture that processes content sequentially as it flows in, aiming for efficient transformation of very large documents.
summary_en: OmniMark is today a proprietary commercial product of Stilo International (status: niche); as of July 2022 the most recent release was version 11.0. It includes a built-in XML parser and XQuery integration (via the Sedna native XML database) and continues to be used mainly for format-conversion tasks in the publishing industry. The exact founding year could only be confirmed on Wikipedia as "the 1980s"; the commonly cited year 1986 itself could not be verified against a primary source.

name: Opa
problem: Web開発では、クライアント側(JavaScript)、サーバー側、データベースをそれぞれ別の言語や技術で記述する必要があり、その境界を横断したバグや設計の不整合が生じやすいという課題があった。フランスのMLstate社は、単一の言語でクライアント・サーバー・データベース・分散実行を統合的に記述できるOpaを開発した。関数型言語をコアとしつつ静的型推論を持ち、クライアント側コードはJavaScriptへ、サーバー側コードはNode.jsへコンパイルされる仕組みを備えた。
summary: 2010年にOWASPカンファレンスで発表され、2011年6月にソースコードがGitHub上で公開された。最終安定版は2014年3月のバージョン1.1.1で、それ以降の活発な開発は確認できず、歴史的な言語として位置づけられている(status: historical)。
problem_en: In web development, the client side (JavaScript), the server side, and the database traditionally each require separate languages and technologies, which makes bugs and design inconsistencies across those boundaries easy to introduce. The French company MLstate developed Opa so that a single language could describe the client, server, database, and distributed execution in an integrated way. Its core is a functional language with static type inference, and it compiles client-side code to JavaScript and server-side code to Node.js.
summary_en: Opa was first presented at the OWASP conference in 2010, and its source code was released on GitHub in June 2011. Its final stable release was version 1.1.1 in March 2014, after which no significant further development could be confirmed; it is now treated as a historical language (status: historical).

name: OPAL
problem: 1980年代半ば、ベルリン工科大学(TU Berlin)のコンパイラ構成・プログラミング言語研究グループは、代数的仕様記述の考え方を反映した実用的な関数型言語を必要としていた。Peter Pepperを中心とするこの研究グループは、モジュールをシグネチャ(signature)と実装(implementation)に分離する設計や、パターンマッチングに似た分岐構文を備えた「最適化された適用型言語(OPtimized Applicative Language)」ことOPALを開発した。
summary: TU Berlinの当該研究グループにより1985年から2000年にかけて開発が行われたことが、プロジェクトの公式GitHubリポジトリ(TU-Berlin/opal)の記述で確認できる(この年代情報はWikipedia本文には記載がなく、公式リポジトリの記述による)。現在もソースコードはGitHub上で公開されているが、活発な開発は確認できず、歴史的な言語として位置づけられている(status: historical)。
problem_en: In the mid-1980s, the Compiler Construction and Programming Languages research group at the Technische Universität Berlin (TU Berlin) needed a practical functional language that reflected ideas from algebraic specification. Led by Peter Pepper, the group developed OPAL ("OPtimized Applicative Language"), whose modules separate a signature from an implementation and which offers a pattern-matching-like branching construct.
summary_en: According to the project's official GitHub repository (TU-Berlin/opal), OPAL was developed by that TU Berlin research group from 1985 to 2000 (this dating is not stated in the Wikipedia article itself, but comes from the official repository's own description). Its source code remains published on GitHub today, but no active ongoing development could be confirmed, and it is treated as a historical language (status: historical).

name: OpenQASM
problem: 量子コンピュータ上で実行する量子回路やアルゴリズムを、特定のハードウェアや実行環境に依存しない形で記述・交換するための共通の中間表現が必要とされていた。IBMの研究者Andrew W. Cross、Lev S. Bishop、John A. Smolin、Jay M. Gambettaは2017年、量子演算の記述に加えて、測定結果に基づく古典的なフィードフォワード制御フローや、タイミング指定・ゲートキャリブレーションの仕組みまで記述できる中間表現言語OpenQASMを発表した。
summary: IBMの量子コンピューティングフレームワークQiskitやIBM Quantum Platformで現在も使われている、現行の量子回路記述言語である(status: active)。仕様バージョン3.0がGitHub上で管理され、2024年5月にはリファレンス実装のバージョン3.1.0がリリースされた。Apache License 2.0のもとで公開されている。
problem_en: A common intermediate representation was needed to describe and exchange quantum circuits and algorithms for execution on quantum computers, independent of any particular hardware or runtime environment. In 2017, IBM researchers Andrew W. Cross, Lev S. Bishop, John A. Smolin, and Jay M. Gambetta introduced OpenQASM, an intermediate-representation language that describes not only quantum operations but also classical feed-forward control flow driven by measurement outcomes, along with explicit timing instructions and gate-calibration mechanisms.
summary_en: OpenQASM is the current quantum-circuit description language used in IBM's Qiskit framework and the IBM Quantum Platform (status: active). Specification version 3.0 is maintained on GitHub, and reference-implementation version 3.1.0 was released in May 2024. It is published under the Apache License 2.0.

name: Orc
problem: 分散環境上の複数サービス(Webサービス、センサー、人間へのメール送信など)を呼び出し、それらの応答を組み合わせて処理を進めたいが、並行処理・タイムアウト・キャンセル・障害処理を素朴に書くとコードがすぐ複雑になってしまう問題を解決したかった。
summary: テキサス大学オースティン校のJayadev Misraが考案した、サービス指向の並行処理オーケストレーションのための小さな言語。学術的な研究言語として使われている。
problem_en:
Modern computation often requires invoking many independent, possibly slow or unreliable services — web services, sensors, databases, or even sending an email to a human and waiting for a reply — and combining their results. Jayadev Misra at the University of Texas at Austin wanted a language in which such orchestration of concurrent, nondeterministic service calls (including handling timeouts, cancellation, and partial failure) could be expressed cleanly, instead of being buried in ad hoc concurrency control code.

Orc addresses this by providing uniform access to computational services (called "sites") and a handful of simple combinators for composing concurrent computations, letting programmers describe orchestration workflows declaratively.
summary_en:
Orc remains primarily a research and teaching vehicle (status: niche) developed and maintained by Misra's group along with collaborators such as William R. Cook and David Kitchin, released under the New BSD License.

It is notable in the literature on concurrent and orchestration languages for its minimal set of four core combinators, and it drew on ideas from Haskell, ML, Oz, and Smalltalk while remaining a fairly narrowly used academic language rather than an industrial tool.

name: Orwell
problem: Philip Wadlerらは、遅延評価とリスト内包表記・パターンマッチングを備えた純粋関数型言語を、オックスフォード大学の学生に教育目的で自由に使わせたいと考えたが、当時同種の機能を持つMirandaは商用ライセンスの制約を受けていた。
summary: オックスフォード大学で設計された遅延評価の関数型言語。Haskellの先駆けの一つとされる。
problem_en:
In the early-to-mid 1980s at Oxford University's Programming Research Group, Philip Wadler wanted a lazily-evaluated, pure functional language with list comprehensions and pattern matching that could be used freely for teaching and practical assignments, in a setting where comparable commercially-licensed languages such as Miranda placed restrictions on use and redistribution.

Orwell, designed by Wadler and implemented by Martin Raskovsky, offered such a free, lazy functional language, and became one of the earliest languages to combine list comprehensions with pattern matching in a teaching-friendly package.
summary_en:
Orwell is no longer in practical use today (status: historical); its final release dates to January 1990.

It is remembered chiefly for its historical role: it was widely used for coursework at Oxford's mathematics and computation degree program, and it is cited as one of the direct precursors to Haskell, whose design Wadler himself later helped lead.

name: Oxygene
problem: RemObjects Softwareは、Delphi系のObject Pascal構文に親しんだ開発者が、.NETやJavaなど新しい実行環境の機能(ジェネリクス、タスク並列ライブラリなど)を、Delphiとの完全な後方互換性にこだわらずフルに活用できる言語を提供したかった。
summary: RemObjects Software発、Object Pascal系の構文を持つ.NET/JVM/Cocoa向けマルチプラットフォーム言語。もとは「Chrome」という名称だった。
problem_en:
RemObjects Software wanted to give developers familiar with Delphi's Object Pascal syntax a way to fully exploit the capabilities of newer runtimes — the Common Language Infrastructure (.NET), the Java Virtual Machine, and later Cocoa and native/WebAssembly targets — such as generics and task-parallel libraries, without being constrained by the need for full backward compatibility with classic Delphi code.

Rather than porting Delphi as-is, the company (first under the name "Chrome", starting 2005) reinvented an Object Pascal-flavored language designed from the ground up to feel native on .NET and the JVM, later renaming it Oxygene.
summary_en:
Oxygene remains a niche but actively maintained commercial product (status: niche), now marketed as part of RemObjects' "Elements" toolchain alongside sibling languages that target the same set of runtimes.

It is used mainly by a relatively small community of Delphi-background developers who want Pascal-like syntax while targeting .NET, JVM, Cocoa, or WebAssembly, rather than being a mainstream general-purpose language.

name: P4
problem: 従来のネットワークスイッチは特定プロトコル(Ethernet、IP、TCPなど)の処理をハードウェアやファームウェアに固定的に組み込んでおり、新しいプロトコルやパケット処理方式に対応するにはハードウェア設計から見直す必要があった。SDN(ソフトウェア定義ネットワーキング)の考え方をさらに進め、パケット処理そのものをプログラム可能にしたいという要求があった。
summary: CPU・FPGA・ASICなど様々なパケット処理デバイスを対象に、プロトコルに依存しないデータプレーンの処理をプログラムとして記述できるドメイン特化言語。オープン・ネットワーキング財団が開発・保守する。
problem_en:
Traditional network switches hard-wire the handling of specific protocols (Ethernet, IP, TCP, and so on) into their hardware or firmware, so supporting a new protocol or a new way of processing packets has historically required redesigning the hardware itself. As software-defined networking (SDN) separated the control plane from the data plane, there remained a need to make the data plane — the actual packet-processing logic — programmable as well, independent of the specific target hardware.

P4 ("Programming Protocol-independent Packet Processors"), first appearing in 2013 and formally described in a 2014 SIGCOMM paper, addresses this by letting engineers describe how packets should be parsed and forwarded in a target-independent and protocol-independent way, with the same P4 program capable of being compiled for CPUs, FPGAs, or ASICs.
summary_en:
P4 is actively developed and standardized today (status: active) under the stewardship of the Open Networking Foundation (which absorbed the P4 Language Consortium), with the P4-16 specification in wide use.

It has become a standard tool in SDN and programmable-switch research and increasingly in production networks, used to define custom packet-processing behavior on programmable ASICs such as those from Barefoot/Intel (Tofino) as well as on FPGAs and software switches.

name: ParaSail
problem: マルチコア時代において、並行・並列プログラムに潜むデータ競合(レースコンディション)を実行時ではなくコンパイル時に検出したいが、従来の言語では共有変数やポインタのエイリアシングがあるために、それを静的に保証することが難しかった。
summary: S. Tucker Taftが設計した、ポインタを持たずリージョンベースのメモリ管理を採用することで並列安全性をコンパイル時に保証しようとするオブジェクト指向言語。AdaCoreが開発する。
problem_en:
In the multicore era, S. Tucker Taft wanted to catch data races in concurrent and parallel programs at compile time rather than at run time, but conventional languages make this hard to guarantee statically because they allow shared mutable variables and pointer aliasing that can be modified from multiple threads simultaneously.

ParaSail (Parallel Specification and Implementation Language), whose design Taft began in September 2009, tackles this by using a pointer-free, value-semantics programming model with region-based memory management instead of garbage collection, disallowing global variables and parameter aliasing so that every subexpression can safely be evaluated in parallel, with race conditions detected at compile time.
summary_en:
ParaSail remains a research and niche language (status: niche) developed under the stewardship of AdaCore and released under the GPLv3 license, with the latest stable version (9.3) dating to June 2021.

It is influential mainly as a proving ground for parallel-safety ideas — a pointer-free, race-free-by-construction programming model — that have informed later discussions of safe systems programming, and related dialects such as the Ada-like Sparkel, Java-like Javallel, and Python-like Parython were built on the same core language.

name: PARI/GP
problem: 数論(整数論)の研究者は、多倍長整数演算、因数分解、代数体や楕円曲線の計算など、数論特有の高精度・高機能な計算を高速に行うツールを必要としていたが、汎用の数式処理システムでは数論計算に特化した効率や機能が不足していた。
summary: ボルドー大学のHenri Cohenらが開発した数論計算のためのシステム。Cライブラリ(PARI)と対話型スクリプト言語・環境(GP)から成る。現在はKarim Belabasらが保守する。
problem_en:
Number theorists need tools that can perform number-theory-specific computations — arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic, factorization, and computations over algebraic number fields or elliptic curves — quickly and reliably, but general-purpose computer algebra systems did not necessarily offer the efficiency or specialized functionality that number theory demands.

PARI/GP, developed from 1985 onward by a team led by Henri Cohen at Université Bordeaux 1 (building on an earlier program called Isabelle by Cohen and François Dress from 1979), addresses this by providing a C library (PARI) for number-theoretic computation together with an interactive scripting environment and language (GP) built on top of it.
summary_en:
PARI/GP continues to be maintained today by Karim Belabas and volunteer developers (status: niche), with the latest release (2.17.2) dating to March 2025 and distribution under the GNU General Public License since version 2.1.0.

It remains a specialized but widely respected tool within the number theory research community — capable of arbitrary-precision arithmetic to millions of digits, factorization, and elliptic-curve computations — and its PARI library underlies parts of other computer algebra systems such as SageMath.

name: PEARL
designers: ドイツ規格協会(DIN)標準化委員会
problem: プロセス制御やリアルタイム制御のソフトウェアを、アセンブリ言語や汎用言語に手作業でマルチタスキング機構を組み込んで書くのは煩雑で誤りやすく、ドイツの産業界にはリアルタイム性とマルチタスキングを言語レベルで直接サポートする、学びやすい高水準言語が必要とされた。
summary: 「Process and Experiment Automation Realtime Language」の略。ドイツ規格協会(DIN)によって標準化されたマルチタスキング・リアルタイム制御向けの高水準言語。
problem_en:
Writing process-control and real-time control software by hand-rolling multitasking mechanisms on top of assembly language or general-purpose languages was cumbersome and error-prone. German industry needed an easy-to-learn, high-level language that supported real-time behavior and multitasking directly at the language level.

PEARL ("Process and Experiment Automation Realtime Language"), standardized from 1977 onward by the Deutsches Institut für Normung (DIN), addresses this by providing built-in support for multitasking and real-time programming, along with fixed- and floating-point numbers, character and string data, bit values, structures, and multi-dimensional arrays, and typed/untyped pointers with type casting.
summary_en:
PEARL survives today mainly in a narrow niche (status: niche): its current standardized form, PEARL-90, was codified as DIN 66253-2 in 1998, and the open-source OpenPEARL project keeps an implementation alive.

It is used chiefly in German industrial and process-control contexts with a long support horizon (such as certain plant-control systems), rather than being a widely taught or broadly adopted general-purpose language.

name: PeopleCode
problem: PeopleSoftのERP/HRMSアプリケーション(PeopleTools基盤)において、業務ロジックのカスタマイズや自動化をアプリケーション内部から行えるようにする、業務アプリケーション専用のスクリプト言語が必要とされた。
summary: PeopleSoft(現Oracle)のPeopleToolsフレームワークに組み込まれた、業務アプリケーションのカスタマイズ用スクリプト言語。
problem_en:
Within PeopleSoft's ERP and HRMS applications (built on the PeopleTools framework), there was a need for an application-specific scripting language that let customers and implementers customize and automate business logic directly from within the application itself, rather than modifying the underlying platform code.

PeopleCode, developed by PeopleSoft Corporation (later acquired by Oracle in 2005) as part of PeopleTools, addresses this by providing an object-oriented and imperative scripting language embedded in the PeopleTools runtime, with both loosely-typed and strongly-typed forms and interoperability with Java.

Note: the exact year PeopleCode was first introduced could not be confirmed from the Wikipedia article, which contains no date information; PeopleSoft's first product (version 1) shipped in late 1989, and PeopleCode/PeopleTools existed by at least PeopleTools 8 according to the article, which highlights that release as introducing important object syntax features.
summary_en:
PeopleCode is today classified as a legacy technology (status: legacy): it remains embedded in and essential to running and maintaining existing PeopleSoft/Oracle installations, but it is not a language adopted outside that ecosystem.

Oracle continues to support PeopleTools/PeopleCode for existing customers, and it is mainly encountered by developers and consultants maintaining or extending established PeopleSoft deployments rather than being used to build new, independent software.

name: PicoLisp
problem: Alexander Burgerは、内部データ構造を極限まで単純化し、単一の内部データ型だけで数値・シンボル・リストを表現できる、極小主義的なLisp処理系を作りたいと考えた。多くのLisp方言が機能追加によって複雑化していく中で、単純さそのものを言語の中心的な価値とする方向を目指した。
summary: 単一のセル型だけを内部データ構造とする極小主義的なLisp方言。データベース機能やPrologエンジンを組み込みで持つ。
problem_en:
Alexander Burger wanted to build a minimalist Lisp implementation whose internal data structures were reduced to the absolute minimum — a single internal data type (a cell) used to represent numbers, symbols, and lists alike — at a time when many Lisp dialects were growing steadily more complex through feature accretion. His design instead made simplicity itself the central value of the language.

First appearing in 1988 and completely rewritten in C in 1999, PicoLisp addresses this by keeping the core language extremely small while still providing practical facilities — such as built-in database (CRUD) operations on persistent symbols and an integrated Prolog engine — directly in the runtime rather than as external add-ons.
summary_en:
PicoLisp remains a niche language (status: niche) used mainly by a small but dedicated community, distributed under the MIT license after an earlier period under the GNU GPL.

Its design most closely resembles the early MacLisp, Interlisp, and especially Portable Standard Lisp, and its more recent developments include a 2021 LLVM-based reimplementation (pil21) and PilOS, a minimal experimental operating system built around the language.

name: Pict
problem: 並行計算の理論的基盤であるπ計算(pi-calculus)を、単なる数学的モデルとしてだけでなく、実際にプログラムを書いて実行できる静的型付き言語として実装し、π計算に基づく並行プログラミングのアイデアを実践的に検証したいと考えた。
summary: エディンバラ大学のBenjamin C. PierceとDavid N. Turnerが開発した、π計算に基づく数少ない静的型付き並行言語の一つ。実験的な段階に留まった。
problem_en:
The pi-calculus provided a theoretical foundation for concurrent computation, but Benjamin C. Pierce and David N. Turner wanted to move beyond it as a purely mathematical model and implement it as an actual, statically typed programming language that could be written and executed, so that ideas about pi-calculus-based concurrent programming could be tested in practice.

Pict, whose development began at the University of Edinburgh in 1992, addresses this by being one of the very small number of languages built directly on the pi-calculus, combining a concurrent computation model with a static type discipline.
summary_en:
Pict is today a historical, experimental language (status: historical); most development activity ceased around 1998 and the Wikipedia article describes it as remaining at an experimental stage.

It is remembered chiefly for demonstrating that a pi-calculus-based concurrency model could be given practical, statically-typed programming language form, and it influenced later languages including Orc and the related dialect Nomadic Pict.

name: PILOT
problem: 1960年代、カリフォルニア大学サンフランシスコ校(UCSF)医学部の心理学教授John Amsden Starkweatherは、専門的な計算機科学の知識を持たない教育者でも使える、コンピュータ支援教育(CAI)向けの簡便な言語を必要としていた。
summary: Programmed Inquiry, Learning, or Teachingの略。コンピュータ支援教育のために開発された、単一文字のキーワードを持つ簡易な対話型言語。姉妹言語のLogoと並び、教育用言語の初期の代表例。
problem_en:
In the 1960s, John Amsden Starkweather, a psychology professor at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) medical center, needed a simple language usable by educators without specialized computer science training, for the emerging field of computer-assisted instruction (CAI).

PILOT ("Programmed Inquiry, Learning, or Teaching"), whose development Starkweather began around 1960, addresses this with an imperative language structured similarly to BASIC and FORTRAN but built around single-character keyword commands — such as T for "type" (print text) and A for "accept" (read input) — making it easy to write simple interactive instructional dialogs. Early versions were demonstrated around 1966, with a near-complete version available by 1968 and public release following in 1969; the exact single "first appeared" year is not unambiguously stated in the Wikipedia article, which describes a gradual development process through the 1960s.
summary_en:
PILOT is today a historical language (status: historical) with no significant ongoing use; the IEEE Standard 1154-1991 that once codified it was withdrawn in 2000.

Alongside its contemporary Logo, it is remembered as an early and influential example of a language designed specifically for computer-assisted instruction, and it spawned numerous variants including PYLON, NYLON, Common PILOT, Atari PILOT (which added turtle graphics), and Apple PILOT.

name: PL/0
problem: Niklaus Wirthは、コンパイラ構築を学ぶ学生に、再帰下降パーサやEBNF、段階的洗練法(stepwise refinement)といった概念を、現実のPascalのような大きく複雑な言語ではなく、ごく小さな言語で手を動かして学ばせたいと考えた。
summary: Niklaus Wirthが著書『Algorithms + Data Structures = Programs』(1976年)で示した、コンパイラ構築教育用のPascalの極小サブセット。数十年にわたり世界中の大学のコンパイラ講義で使われてきた。
problem_en:
Niklaus Wirth wanted students learning compiler construction to practice concepts such as recursive descent parsing, EBNF grammars, and stepwise refinement hands-on, using a language small enough to fully implement in a course, rather than a large and complex real-world language like Pascal itself.

PL/0, introduced in Wirth's book Algorithms + Data Structures = Programs (the book's publication is cited as 1975 in some references and the language's introduction as 1976 in the article text), addresses this by stripping Pascal down to a minimal core: only integer types, only basic arithmetic and comparison operators (plus an odd function), only if-then and while-do control flow, and parameterless user-defined procedures.
summary_en:
PL/0 remains an actively used educational tool today (status: educational): compiler courses worldwide adopted it for decades to teach recursive descent parsing before many shifted toward tools like lex and yacc.

In the third edition of his compiler textbook, Wirth himself replaced PL/0 with the more elaborate Oberon-0, which adds arrays, records, and procedures with parameters, but PL/0 itself continues to be referenced and used as introductory teaching material.

name: PL/C
problem: 1960年代末のコーネル大学では、パンチカードによるバッチ処理が主流で、学生がプログラムを提出してから結果を受け取るまでに数時間かかることも珍しくなかった。構文エラーひとつでコンパイルが失敗して丸ごと待ち時間が無駄になるのを防ぎ、PL/Iのほぼ全機能を教育目的で使えるコンパイラが必要とされた。
summary: コーネル大学のRichard W. ConwayとThomas R. Wilcoxが開発した、教育用のPL/I方言。構文エラーを自動修正し、どんなプログラムでもコンパイルを完了させる特異な能力を持っていた。
problem_en:
At Cornell University in the late 1960s, batch processing on punch cards was the norm, and it was common for students to wait hours between submitting a program and receiving its output. A single syntax error that caused a compile to fail entirely would waste that whole turnaround cycle. Cornell needed a compiler that implemented nearly all of the large PL/I language for teaching purposes while avoiding that waste.

PL/C, developed in 1968-1969 by Professor Richard W. Conway and graduate student Thomas R. Wilcox at Cornell's Department of Computer Science (with partial funding from IBM), addresses this with the unusual capability of never failing to compile a program, through extensive automatic correction of syntax errors, so that even flawed submissions still produced usable output.
summary_en:
PL/C is today a historical language (status: historical) with no ongoing use; as of 2022 its source code appears to be lost.

It began regular use in September 1970, reached over 250 adopting universities and more than 200 installations worldwide by 1976, and spawned variants such as PL/CT (interactive terminals), PL/CS (assertions), and PL/CV (formal correctness proofs), but usage declined through the 1980s as Pascal became the preferred teaching language; Cornell itself switched to Pascal in 1984.

name: PL/M
problem: 1970年代前半、マイクロコンピュータ(Intel 8008/8080など)向けにソフトウェアを書く手段はアセンブリ言語に限られており、メモリやI/Oポートへの直接アクセスなど低レベルな制御を保ったまま、より高い抽象度でプログラムを記述できる言語が必要とされていた。
summary: Gary Kildallが開発した、Intelマイクロプロセッサ向けの高水準システム記述言語。CP/Mの初期バージョンの実装にも使われた。
problem_en:
In the early 1970s, writing software for microcomputers (such as the Intel 8008 and 8080) was largely limited to assembly language. There was a need for a language that offered a higher level of abstraction while preserving low-level control such as direct access to memory, I/O ports, and interrupts.

PL/M, designed by Gary Kildall at Microcomputer Applications Associates and first appearing in 1973, addresses this by synthesizing ideas from PL/I and XPL into a structured, high-level systems language purpose-built for microprocessors, deliberately omitting standard input/output facilities in favor of direct memory and I/O access, and including an integrated macro processor.
summary_en:
PL/M is today a historical language (status: historical), no longer supported by Intel, though aftermarket translation and compilation tools still exist for enthusiasts.

It is remembered as the first high-level language designed specifically for microprocessor-based systems, notably used to implement parts of the CP/M operating system, and versions such as PL/M-80 and PL/M-86 were widely used in embedded systems on Intel and Zilog Z80-based hardware throughout the 1970s and 1980s.

name: PL/S
problem: IBMは、自社のフラッグシップオペレーティングシステム群をアセンブリ言語で書き続けることの限界(保守性・移植性の低さ)を解消したいと考え、アセンブリ言語を置き換えられるだけの低レベル制御力(インラインアセンブリやレジスタの明示的制御)を保ちながら、より高水準に書ける機種指向(machine-oriented)言語を必要としていた。
summary: IBMが自社OS内部実装向けに開発した機種指向の高水準言語。もとはBasic Systems Language(BSL)という名称だった。
problem_en:
IBM wanted to overcome the limits of continuing to write its flagship operating systems entirely in assembly language (poor maintainability and portability), and needed a machine-oriented language that could replace assembly language while retaining enough low-level control — inline assembly support and explicit control over register usage — to be usable for systems programming.

PL/S, developed by IBM in the late 1960s under the name Basic Systems Language (BSL) and based on PL/I, addresses this by functioning as a replacement for assembly language; by the 1970s IBM had rewritten its flagship operating systems in it. The exact year the language was renamed from BSL to PL/S could not be confirmed from the Wikipedia article, which only states that it originated in the late 1960s under the BSL name.
summary_en:
PL/S is today a historical language (status: historical), effectively confined to IBM's own internal use; for competitive reasons IBM did not release the compiler externally for many years, distributing only source code.

It gave rise to successor languages including PL/S II, PL/S III, PL/AS, and PL/X, and is related to PL/DS, forming an internal family of IBM systems-implementation languages descended from PL/I.

name: PL360
problem: IBM System/360上でシステムプログラミングを行うには、その時点ではアセンブリ言語を使うほかなかったが、それでは高水準言語が持つ可読性や構造化された記述力を得られなかった。一方で純粋な高水準言語では、機械語命令やレジスタを直接指定するといった低レベルな制御ができなかった。
summary: Niklaus Wirthらがスタンフォード大学でIBM System/360向けに開発した、ALGOL風の構文を持つシステムプログラミング言語。高水準の構造とアセンブリ相当の低レベル制御を両立させた。
problem_en:
Systems programming on the IBM System/360 at the time meant using assembly language, which lacked the readability and structured expressiveness of a high-level language. Conversely, a pure high-level language of the era could not directly specify machine instructions and registers the way assembly could.

PL360, designed in 1966 by Niklaus Wirth together with Joseph W. Wells Jr. and Edwin Satterthwaite Jr. at Stanford University (described in a publication in early 1968), addresses this by being a one-pass compiler with ALGOL-like syntax that also lets programmers specify exact machine code instructions and registers similar to assembly language, while still providing high-level features such as structured control flow and five basic data types (byte/character, short integer, integer/logical, real, and long real).
summary_en:
PL360 is today a historical language (status: historical) with no practical use, but it occupies an important place in Niklaus Wirth's own trajectory as a language designer.

Wirth used the experience of PL360 directly in developing ALGOL W, and the language was later extended in the early 1970s and used to build Stanford's SPIRES (Stanford Physics Information Retrieval System) database management system.

name: PLEXIL
problem: NASAは火星探査ローバーや国際宇宙ステーション(ISS)など、人手による直接操作が難しい自律システムの行動計画を、階層的かつ検証可能な形で記述・実行する手段を必要としていた。従来は汎用プログラミング言語やミッション固有の実装に頼るしかなく、計画の階層構造や実行条件による状態遷移、外部システムとの連携を統一的に扱う仕組みが不足していた。NASAはPLEXIL(Plan Execution Interchange Language)を開発し、計画を「ノード」という共通単位で表現し、実行条件・終了条件・不変条件などの宣言的な条件によって状態遷移を制御することで、ローバーや衛星、居住施設など多様なハードウェアに同じ言語と実行エンジン(PLEXIL Executive)で対応できるようにした。
summary: NASAが開発した、自律システムの行動計画をノード単位の階層構造と宣言的な条件で記述するオープンソースの計画実行言語。
problem_en: NASA needed a way to describe and execute action plans for autonomous systems—such as planetary rovers, orbiting spacecraft, and space station procedures—operating where direct human control is difficult, in a form that is both hierarchical and verifiable. Previously, mission teams had to rely on general-purpose programming languages or mission-specific implementations, lacking a unified way to express a plan's hierarchical structure, condition-driven state transitions, and coordination with external systems. NASA developed PLEXIL (Plan Execution Interchange Language), representing automation plans as a common unit called a "node" whose state transitions are governed declaratively by conditions such as start, end, and invariant conditions, so that the same language and a single execution engine (the PLEXIL Executive) could be reused across diverse hardware including rovers, satellites, and habitat systems.
summary_en: PLEXIL is an open-source plan-execution language developed by NASA that represents the action plans of autonomous systems as a hierarchy of nodes governed by declarative conditions. It has been used in real missions and demonstrations, including the drill control system of the Mars Curiosity rover, the K10 rover, the Deep Space Habitat/Habitat Demonstration Unit, LADEE, and ISS procedure automation, executed via the PLEXIL Executive engine and distributed as BSD-licensed open source on GitHub. It remains a niche, domain-specific language used mainly in NASA-affiliated automation research and flight/ground demonstration projects rather than as a general-purpose language.

name: Promela
problem: 分散システムや並行プロトコルは、プロセス間の通信タイミングの組み合わせが爆発的に増えるため、デッドロックや競合状態、想定外の受信といった欠陥を人手のテストだけで見つけることが極めて難しい。Gerard J. Holzmannは、並行プロセスの振る舞いを簡潔にモデル化し、その正しさを検証できる形式手法を実現するため、検証用モデリング言語Promela(Process/Protocol Meta Language)を考案した。Promelaで書かれたモデルはSPINモデル検査器で解析され、シミュレーションや状態空間の網羅的探索、線形時相論理(LTL)による性質検証を通じて、デッドロックの不在やプロトコルの正しさを形式的に確認できる。
summary: Gerard J. Holzmannが考案した、SPINモデル検査器と組み合わせて並行・分散システムの正しさを形式検証するためのモデリング言語。
problem_en: Distributed systems and concurrent protocols suffer from a combinatorial explosion of possible interleavings and timings among processes, making it extremely difficult to find defects such as deadlocks, race conditions, or unspecified message receptions through manual testing alone. Gerard J. Holzmann devised Promela (Process/Protocol Meta Language), a verification modeling language, to concisely model the behavior of concurrent processes and to enable formal verification of their correctness. Models written in Promela are analyzed with the SPIN model checker, which can verify the absence of deadlocks and the correctness of a protocol through simulation, exhaustive state-space search, and checking of linear temporal logic (LTL) properties.
summary_en: Promela is a modeling language devised by Gerard J. Holzmann for formally verifying the correctness of concurrent and distributed systems in combination with the SPIN model checker. It supports dynamic creation of concurrent processes and communication via synchronous (rendezvous) or asynchronous (buffered) message channels, with guarded-choice control structures (if/fi, do/od) and an atomic construct for indivisible execution. Promela is not used as a general-purpose programming language today; it remains a specialized, niche language for formal verification of protocols and concurrent algorithms, used mainly in academic research and protocol/embedded-system verification alongside its companion tool SPIN.

name: Pure
problem: 科学計算やシンボリック計算の分野では、記号操作を柔軟に記述できる動的型付け言語と、実行速度に優れるネイティブコンパイルの両方が求められることが多いが、Albert Gräf自身が開発した従来の等式言語Qのインタプリタには実行速度や機能面の制約があった。Gräfはマインツ大学で、項書き換え(term rewriting)に基づく関数型プログラミングの表現力を保ちながら、LLVM経由でネイティブコードにジャストインタイムコンパイルされる後継言語Pureを開発し、ユーザー定義演算子やマクロ、任意精度演算、C言語ライブラリとの連携を備えることで、数学・科学計算からAI、シンボリック計算、リアルタイムマルチメディア処理まで幅広い用途に対応させることを目指した。
summary: 等式言語Qの後継として設計された、項書き換えに基づく動的型付けの関数型プログラミング言語。
problem_en: In scientific and symbolic computing, there is often a need for both a dynamically typed language flexible enough for symbolic manipulation and a language with the execution speed of native compilation, but Albert Gräf's own earlier interpreter for the equational language Q had limitations in speed and functionality. At the University of Mainz, Gräf built Pure as a successor to Q that would preserve the expressive power of term-rewriting-based functional programming while being just-in-time compiled to native code via LLVM for speed, adding user-defined operator syntax, macros, arbitrary-precision arithmetic, and a C library interface to support a wide range of applications from mathematics and scientific computing to AI, symbolic computation, and real-time multimedia processing.
summary_en: Pure is a dynamically typed, strongly typed functional programming language based on term rewriting, developed by Albert Gräf as the successor to his own equational language Q. Its syntax resembles Miranda and Haskell but, unlike them, it is a free-format language using explicit delimiters rather than the offside rule; it ships with an interpreter and debugger, supports user-defined operators, macros, and arbitrary-precision arithmetic, and is just-in-time compiled to native code via LLVM with a C library interface. Distributed as free software under the GNU LGPL and aimed primarily at mathematical and scientific applications (with additional use in AI, symbolic computation, and real-time multimedia processing), it remains a niche functional language today.

name: Qalb
problem: プログラミング言語の大多数は英語(ラテン文字)を前提としたキーワードや構文で設計されており、非英語圏、特にアラビア語のような右から左に書く言語の話者は、プログラミングを学ぶ最初の一歩から「自分の言語ではない記号体系」を受け入れることを強いられていた。レバノン系の計算機科学者Ramsey Nasserは、ニューヨークのEyebeam Art + Technology Centerでの活動の中で、プログラミング言語における英語圏中心主義(Anglophone bias)を可視化し問い直すことを目的として、完全にアラビア語で記述できる言語Qalbを考案した。
summary: Ramsey Nasserが2012年に発表した、完全にアラビア語で記述できる関数型プログラミング言語。Scheme風の括弧つき前置記法をベースに、キーワードをレバノン方言のアラビア語に置き換え、右から左に読み書きする。
problem_en: The vast majority of programming languages assume English (Latin-alphabet) keywords and syntax, which forces speakers of non-English languages -- especially right-to-left languages like Arabic -- to accept a foreign symbolic system before they can even begin to learn programming. Ramsey Nasser, a Lebanese-American computer scientist working at the Eyebeam Art + Technology Center in New York, created Qalb to make this Anglophone bias in programming-language design visible and to question it, by building a language that can be written entirely in Arabic.
summary_en: Qalb is a Turing-complete functional programming language released in 2012 by Ramsey Nasser that lets programmers write entire programs in Arabic, using a Scheme-like, parenthesized, right-to-left syntax with keywords drawn from Lebanese colloquial Arabic. It functions mainly as an art and awareness project about the English-centric design of most programming languages rather than as a language for production software development.

name: .QL(CodeQL)
problem: ソースコードの構造的な欠陥やセキュリティ上の脆弱性を発見するには、コードを単なるテキストではなく、クラスや関数、呼び出し関係、データフローなどを持つ「関係データ」としてモデル化し、それに対して柔軟な問い合わせ(クエリ)を実行できる仕組みが求められていた。従来のSQLは表形式データへの問い合わせには適していたが、プログラムが持つ階層構造やクラス階層のような再帰的・オブジェクト指向的な関係を自然に表現するのは難しかった。Oege de Moorらが2006年に英オックスフォードで創業したSemmle社は、Datalogという論理型クエリ言語をベースに、オブジェクト指向の型階層やメソッドを組み合わせた新しいクエリ言語「.QL」を開発した。
summary: Semmle社(創業者Oege de Moor)が開発した、Datalogをベースとするオブジェクト指向のクエリ言語。ソースコードを関係データとしてモデル化し、SQLにコンパイルして問い合わせる。現在は「CodeQL」としてGitHubのコードスキャン・脆弱性検出エンジンの中核を担う。
problem_en: Finding structural code smells and security vulnerabilities in source code requires modeling code not as plain text but as relational data with classes, functions, call relationships, and data flow, and then running flexible queries against that model. Traditional SQL suited tabular data well but struggled to naturally express the hierarchical, recursive, object-oriented relationships found in program structures such as class hierarchies. Semmle, founded by Oege de Moor in Oxford, England in 2006, addressed this by building .QL, a query language combining the logic-based query language Datalog with object-oriented concepts such as type hierarchies and methods.
summary_en: .QL, now widely known as CodeQL, is an object-oriented, Datalog-derived logic and query language created by Semmle (founded by Oege de Moor) around 2007 to model and query source code as relational data. Its queries compile into SQL, and following GitHub's 2019 acquisition of Semmle, it became the core engine behind GitHub's code scanning and vulnerability-detection features, remaining in active use today.

name: QCL
problem: 量子コンピュータが実機としてほとんど存在しなかった2000年前後、量子計算のアルゴリズムを検討するには、量子ビットの重ね合わせやユニタリ変換といった量子力学特有の操作を、既存の古典的プログラミング言語の枠組みでどう表現すべきかという課題があった。ウィーン工科大学理論物理学研究所のBernhard Ömerは、古典的な制御構造と量子演算を同じプログラム内で組み合わせて記述できる言語QCL(Quantum Computation Language)を設計し、古典的に量子コンピュータをシミュレートするインタープリタとして実装した。
summary: Bernhard Ömerが2000年に発表した、最初期に実装された量子プログラミング言語の一つ。C言語に似た構文で、古典データ型と量子データ型(qureg等)、ユーザー定義の量子演算子を同じプログラム内に混在させて記述できる。
problem_en: Around 2000, when almost no physical quantum computers existed, exploring quantum algorithms required deciding how to express quantum-mechanical operations such as qubit superposition and unitary transformations, since existing classical languages had no native way to do so. Bernhard Ömer, at the Institute for Theoretical Physics at the Vienna University of Technology, designed QCL (Quantum Computation Language) to let classical control structures and quantum operations be written together in a single program, implementing it as an interpreter with a built-in, classically simulated quantum computer.
summary_en: QCL is one of the earliest implemented quantum programming languages, created in 2000 by Bernhard Ömer at the Vienna University of Technology. It has C-like syntax and mixes classical and quantum data types and operations (such as qureg for qubit registers and built-in quantum gate libraries) within a single program, running on an interpreter with a classically simulated quantum computer. It is now primarily of historical interest, having been superseded by newer languages and SDKs such as Q# and Qiskit.

name: QuakeC
problem: 1996年にid Softwareが発売したFPSゲーム『Quake』では、ゲームのロジック(武器の挙動、モンスターのAI、ゲームルール、物理演算など)をエンジン本体のC/C++コードから分離し、MOD開発者やコミュニティが本体のソースコードを持たなくても内容を拡張・改造できるようにする必要があった。John Carmackはこの目的のために、C言語に似た構文を持つ専用の言語QuakeCを設計し、QuakeCで書かれたゲームロジックをコンパイルしてバイトコード(progs.dat)として出力し、Quakeエンジンがそのバイトコードをランタイムで解釈実行する、という仕組みを作った。
summary: John Carmack(id Software)が1996年に開発した、Quakeのゲームロジックを記述するためのCライクな言語。ソースはバイトコード(progs.dat)にコンパイルされ、Quakeエンジンがランタイムで解釈実行する。武器追加やAI改造など活発なMOD文化を支えた。
problem_en: When id Software released the first-person shooter Quake in 1996, its game logic (weapon behavior, monster AI, game rules, physics) needed to be separated from the engine's core C/C++ code so that mod developers and the community could extend and modify game behavior without access to the engine's source. John Carmack designed QuakeC, a C-like language, for this purpose: QuakeC source is compiled into bytecode (stored in a progs.dat file), which the Quake engine then interprets at runtime.
summary_en: QuakeC is a compiled, C-like, statically typed procedural language created in 1996 by John Carmack of id Software to script the game logic of Quake; its source compiles to bytecode that the Quake engine interprets at runtime. It deliberately lacked features such as custom structs, arrays, and pointer dereferencing, and its single-slot temporary string buffer caused well-known bugs when chaining string-returning calls. QuakeC was used only by the original Quake engine, and is now a historical language of interest mainly to retro-game and Quake mod-development communities.

name: RAPID
problem: ABBは産業用ロボットの制御言語として、以前はARLAという独自言語を使用していたが、複雑化する生産ラインの処理に対応できる、より表現力の高い専用言語が求められた。1994年、新しいロボットコントローラ「S4 Control System」の導入に合わせて、ABBはARLAを置き換える新しい専用言語RAPIDを発表した。RAPIDは、手続き(プロシージャ)・関数・トラップルーチンといった構造化されたルーチン単位、算術式・論理式の記述、自動エラー処理機構、複数タスクを同時に走らせるマルチタスキング機能を備えており、工場の生産ラインで動くロボットアームの動作を記述するための言語として設計された。
summary: ABB産業用ロボット向けの専用言語として現在も現役で使われている(status: active)。
problem_en: In the early 1990s, controlling ABB industrial robots relied on a dedicated in-house language called ARLA. Alongside the introduction of the S4 control system in 1994, ABB introduced RAPID as its new robot programming language, superseding ARLA. RAPID provides structured program units such as procedures, functions, and trap routines, along with arithmetic and logical expressions, automatic error handling, and support for running multiple tasks concurrently (multitasking).
summary_en: RAPID remains in active use today as ABB's dedicated programming language for its industrial robots (status: active), distributed together with development tools such as RobotStudio, whose reference manual documents the language. It continues to serve as ABB's standard robot programming language, though the Wikipedia article itself notes that it lacks sufficient inline citations and relies heavily on sources affiliated with ABB, so some details should be treated with appropriate caution.

name: Rapira
problem: ソビエト連邦では学校教育向けの情報処理教育を目的として、当時のPascal実装よりも扱いやすい教育用プログラミング言語が求められた。計算機科学者Andrey Ershovらは、POP-2やSETLといった言語の影響を受けた、タプルという柔軟なデータ構造を中核に持つ、動的型付けの対話的インタプリタ言語Rapiraを開発し、Agat(ソ連製Apple II互換機)やPDP-11互換機など当時ソ連の学校に導入されていた各種コンピュータ向けに実装した。
summary: 現在は実用言語としては使われておらず、ソ連の学校情報教育を伝える歴史的言語として位置づけられている(status: historical)。
problem_en: In the Soviet Union, computer scientist Andrey Ershov and colleagues developed Rapira as an educational programming language for school informatics education. According to Wikipedia, it was considered more elegant and easier to use than Pascal implementations of the time. Rapira was designed as an interactive, dynamically-typed interpreted language influenced by languages such as POP-2 and SETL, built around a flexible "tuple" data structure (a heterogeneous list supporting operations such as indexing, joining, and length counting). Its keywords were originally Russian-based (English and Romanian versions were added later), and implementations were provided for a range of computers deployed in Soviet schools, including the Agat, PDP-11 clones (Elektronika, DVK), and Intel 8080/Zilog Z80-based machines.
summary_en: Rapira is no longer used in any practical software context today and is regarded primarily as a historical artifact documenting the history of school computing education in the Soviet Union (status: historical). Its flexible tuple data structure and an integrated development environment (editor and debugger) were notable features for an educational language of its era. Today it survives mainly through emulators and volunteer revival projects such as "Rapira Reborn."

name: Ratfor
problem: 1960〜70年代のFortran 66はGOTO文中心の分岐と厳格な桁位置の書式しか持たず、構造化された制御構文を欠いていた。ベル研究所のBrian Kernighanは1974年にRatfor(Rational Fortranの略)を考案・実装し、if-else・while・forといった構造化制御構文、波括弧によるブロック化、自由な書式などをFortran 66用のプリプロセッサとして提供した。制御構造の多くはC言語から借用したもので、Ratforのコードは変換されて標準的なFortran 66としてコンパイルされる。
summary: 現在は歴史的な言語として位置づけられており(status: historical)、実務でゼロから採用されることはほとんどない。
problem_en: In the 1960s and 1970s, mainstream Fortran 66 relied primarily on GOTO statements and statement numbers for control flow and lacked structured constructs such as if-else, while, and for, remaining bound to a rigid column-based source format. Brian Kernighan at Bell Telephone Laboratories designed Ratfor (short for "Rational Fortran") in 1974 and described it in a 1975 paper in Software—Practice & Experience; the Wikipedia infobox lists 1976 as the year it first appeared. Ratfor is a preprocessor that adds control structures such as if-else, while, for, do, repeat-until, break, and next, brace-delimited blocks, free-form formatting, and comparison operators like < and > instead of Fortran's .LT./.GT. — features that, in Kernighan's own words, were "shamelessly stolen from the language C." Source code written in Ratfor was translated into standard Fortran 66 before compilation. The 1976 book Software Tools by Kernighan and P.J. Plauger, whose sample programs were themselves written in Ratfor, greatly raised the language's visibility.
summary_en: Ratfor is today regarded as a historical language (status: historical) and is rarely adopted from scratch for practical work. However, it is frequently cited in the history of programming languages as a preprocessor that bridged old GOTO-centric Fortran and structured programming, and as a notable case of a language that influenced software-engineering education through the book Software Tools. A successor, Ratfiv, extending the approach for Fortran 77, was later developed by Bill Wood in the early 1980s.

name: rc
problem: Plan 9開発にあたり、標準的だったBourne Shellの文法上の癖を解消した、より単純で一貫したシェルが求められた。Tom Duffは、変数を常に文字列のリストとして扱い展開時に再分割しない、制御構造をC言語に近い書き方にするなど、Bourne Shellに似た機能を保ちながらより単純で一貫した文法を持つシェルrc(run commandsの意)を設計し、1989年にVersion 10 UnixおよびPlan 9の標準シェルとして導入した。
summary: 現在はPlan 9系OSの標準シェルとして使われ続ける歴史的な言語として位置づけられている(status: historical)。
problem_en: In the late 1980s, Bell Labs was developing Plan 9 from Bell Labs as a successor to Unix. The Bourne shell, the standard command interpreter at the time, was widely used but had well-known syntactic quirks, such as word-splitting during variable expansion and the need for special notations (like "$@") to handle multiple values. Tom Duff designed rc ("run commands") to offer similar functionality to the Bourne shell with a simpler, more consistent grammar. In rc, all variables are treated as lists of strings and are not re-split upon expansion, removing the need for constructs like "$@". Its control structures were modeled on C rather than ALGOL-style syntax, and it was introduced in 1989 as the standard shell for Version 10 Unix and Plan 9.
summary_en: rc is not considered a mainstream shell today and is treated as a historical language (status: historical). However, it remains the standard shell on Plan 9-family systems (Plan 9 from Bell Labs and Plan 9 from User Space), and Byron Rakitzis's general-purpose Unix reimplementation, along with later designs such as the extended shell "es" and the Inferno operating system's shell, were influenced by it. It continues to be referenced as an example of a shell with simple, consistent syntax whenever shell language design is discussed.

name: Reason
problem: Facebookでは2010年代半ば、社内の一部プロジェクトでOCamlが採用されていたが、パターンマッチや関数適用の書き方などOCaml独自の構文は、JavaScript出身のWebエンジニアにとって学習コストが高く、社内での採用拡大の障壁になっていた。Jordan Walkeは、OCamlコンパイラが持つ強力な静的型システムと実行性能をそのまま生かしながら、波括弧やセミコロンを用いたJavaScript/C系言語に近い見た目の構文で書けるようにする「代替構文」としてReason(ReasonML)を設計した。Reasonの意味論はOCamlと完全に同一であり、あくまで表層の構文だけを置き換えるレイヤーという位置づけである。
summary: OCamlに対する構文拡張・ツールチェインとして2016年にFacebookで開発された言語で、OCamlと同じ意味論をJavaScript風の構文で提供する。Bloomberg社のBuckleScript(OCaml→JavaScriptコンパイラ)との統合により一時Webフロントエンド向け言語として注目されたが、2020年にBuckleScriptチームがReason構文から分岐して独自路線のReScriptに改名・独立し、Reason自身はMelangeコンパイラを介してJavaScriptへのコンパイルを継続する形で存続している。
problem_en: In the mid-2010s, Facebook used OCaml internally in several projects, but OCaml's distinctive syntax (pattern matching notation, function application style, etc.) presented a steep learning curve for engineers coming from a JavaScript background, which was a barrier to wider internal adoption. Jordan Walke designed Reason (ReasonML) as an alternate syntax layer that preserves OCaml's powerful static type system and runtime performance entirely, while offering a JavaScript/C-family-like surface syntax using curly braces and semicolons. Reason's semantics are identical to OCaml's; it only replaces the surface syntax.
summary_en: Reason is a syntax extension and toolchain for OCaml developed at Facebook in 2016, offering OCaml's exact semantics through JavaScript-style syntax. Its integration with Bloomberg's BuckleScript (an OCaml-to-JavaScript compiler) briefly made it a notable option for web frontend development, but in 2020 the BuckleScript team diverged from Reason's syntax and rebranded as the independent language ReScript. Reason itself continues to exist, now compiling to JavaScript via the Melange compiler.

name: RSL
problem: 1980年代、ヨーロッパの産業界ではソフトウェアの形式的検証によって仕様段階でバグを排除しようとする関心が高まっていたが、実務者にとってはVDMのような既存の形式仕様言語の表記や理論的背景が難解で、産業界への普及が進んでいなかった。Dines Bjørnerらは欧州の研究プロジェクトESPRIT II LaCoSのもとで、要求仕様から段階的詳細化を経て実装コードに至る「厳密な(rigorous)」開発プロセスを産業界に提供することを目指し、形式仕様記述言語RSL(RAISE Specification Language)と、それを取り巻く開発ツール群RAISE(Rigorous Approach to Industrial Software Engineering)を開発した。
summary: RAISE手法の中核となる形式仕様記述言語で、抽象データ型や関係、並行性などを記述できる。開発は1990年代の欧州研究プロジェクトESPRIT II LaCoSに遡り、国連大学国際ソフトウェア技術研究所(UNU-IIST、マカオ)などが教育・普及活動を続けてきたが、現在は主に形式手法の歴史的な事例として言及される。
problem_en: In the 1980s, European industry showed growing interest in formal verification of software to eliminate bugs at the specification stage, but existing formal specification languages such as VDM were seen as too notationally and theoretically demanding for practitioners, hindering industrial adoption. Under the European ESPRIT II LaCoS project, Dines Bjørner and colleagues developed the formal specification language RSL (RAISE Specification Language) together with the surrounding RAISE (Rigorous Approach to Industrial Software Engineering) toolset, aiming to provide industry with a rigorous development process leading from requirements specification through stepwise refinement to implementation code.
summary_en: RSL is the formal specification language at the core of the RAISE method, capable of describing abstract data types, relations, and concurrency. Its development traces back to the European ESPRIT II LaCoS project of the 1990s, and institutions such as UNU-IIST (Macau) have continued education and outreach efforts, but today it is mainly cited as a historical case study in formal methods.

name: RTL/2
problem: 1970年代初頭、化学メーカーのICI(インペリアル・ケミカル・インダストリーズ)では、プラントのプロセス制御など即応性が求められる組み込み用途のソフトウェアを主にアセンブリ言語で開発していた。アセンブリでの開発は保守性・可読性に乏しくバグの温床になりやすい一方、FORTRANのような当時の汎用高級言語はリアルタイム制御に必要な低レベルな資源管理・割り込み処理やコンパクトなコード生成に向いていなかった。J.G.P.バーンズは、ALGOL 68の概念を土台にしつつ規模を絞り込んだ、リアルタイム制御専用の高級言語RTL/2を設計した。プログラムを「ブリック(procedure brick, data brick, stack brick)」という単位に分割して個別コンパイルできるようにし、必要な箇所ではCODE文によってアセンブリ言語を直接埋め込めるようにすることで、高級言語の生産性とアセンブリ言語並みの実行効率・低レベル制御を両立させることを目指した。
summary: 英国の化学メーカーICI発のリアルタイム制御用高級言語で、ALGOL 68の考え方を組み込み・プロセス制御分野に適用したもの。1974年からSPL Internationalによって商用配布され、DEC PDP-11/VAX系のRSX-11MやVMS上で使われ、1980年には英国規格協会(BSI)によりBS 5904として標準化された。しかしCやAdaなど後続の言語の普及により置き換えられ、現在は歴史的な言語としてのみ言及される。
problem_en: In the early 1970s, the chemical manufacturer ICI (Imperial Chemical Industries) was developing embedded software requiring real-time responsiveness, such as process control for chemical plants, mostly in assembly language. Assembly development was hard to maintain and read, making it prone to bugs, while general-purpose high-level languages of the era such as FORTRAN were not suited to the low-level resource management, interrupt handling, and compact code generation demanded by real-time control. J.G.P. Barnes designed RTL/2, a high-level language dedicated to real-time control, based on concepts from ALGOL 68 but scaled down in scope. Programs were divided into separately compilable units called 'bricks' (procedure bricks, data bricks, and stack bricks), and assembly code could be embedded directly via CODE statements where needed, aiming to combine the productivity of a high-level language with the execution efficiency and low-level control of assembly language.
summary_en: RTL/2 is a high-level real-time control language originating at the British chemical manufacturer ICI, applying ALGOL 68-derived concepts to the embedded and process-control domain. It was commercially distributed by SPL International starting in 1974, used on DEC PDP-11/VAX systems running RSX-11M and VMS, and standardized by the British Standards Institution as BS 5904 in 1980. It was eventually superseded by later languages such as C and Ada, and today it is mentioned only as a historical language.

name: S-Lang
problem:
1992年、物理学者John E. Davisは、自身が開発していたテキストエディタ用に書いた関数群を他のプログラムでも再利用できるようにしたいと考え、S-Langライブラリの開発を開始した。当初のインタプリタの構文はPostScriptに似た構文だったが、後にC言語に近い構文へと進化し、オブジェクト指向的な構文要素も追加された。Davisの物理学・科学計算への関心を反映して、MATLABやIDLに似たベクトル化された配列演算がネイティブにサポートされている点も特徴である。

目的は、単体で動くインタプリタというより、テキストエディタ(JEDエディタが最初の採用例)のような既存アプリケーションに組み込んで拡張性を持たせるための、軽量で組込み可能なスクリプト言語ライブラリを提供することだった。
summary: S-Langは現在も開発が続けられており(2022年8月にバージョン2.3.3をリリース)、GPL 2.0以降でライセンスされている。JEDテキストエディタをはじめ、天文学分野のソフトウェア(slsh、ISISなど)に組み込まれる形でnicheに使われ続けている。
problem_en: In 1992, physicist John E. Davis started the S-Lang library, wanting to make functions he had written for a text editor reusable in other programs. The interpreter's original syntax resembled PostScript, but it later evolved to be much more C-like, with object-oriented constructs added as well. Reflecting Davis's background in physics and his interest in scientific computing, the language natively supports vectorized array operations similar to MATLAB and IDL. The goal was not to build a standalone interpreter but to provide a lightweight, embeddable scripting-language library that could be built into existing applications — such as the JED text editor, its first adopter — to make them extensible.
summary_en: S-Lang remains actively maintained today (version 2.3.3 was released in August 2022) and is distributed under the GPL 2.0-or-later license. It continues to see niche use, embedded in the JED text editor and in astronomy software such as slsh and ISIS, rather than as a general-purpose standalone language.

name: S-PLUS
problem:
1980年代、ベル研究所で開発された統計プログラミング言語Sは統計解析・グラフ作成のデファクトスタンダードとなっていたが、ベル研外での商用利用や継続的なサポート体制を備えた実装が求められていた。ベル研でSを学んだワシントン大学統計学教授のR. Douglas Martinは、シアトルに設立したStatistical Sciences社(後にInsightful社、さらにTIBCO Software社へと事業が引き継がれる)を通じて、1988年にSの商用実装であるS-PLUSを開発・発売した。

目的は、研究用言語であったSを、サポート・ドキュメント・GUIやExcel等外部アプリケーションとの連携を備えた、企業や官公庁でも安心して使える商用統計解析パッケージとして提供することだった。
summary: S-PLUSはオブジェクト指向的な統計解析機能や計量経済学向けのFinMetricsパッケージなどを備え、1990年代から2000年代にかけて商用統計ソフトウェアの代表格として使われた。しかし無料でオープンソースのSの後継言語Rの普及により徐々にシェアを失い、TIBCO社は2026年1月31日付でS-PLUSを正式に販売終了・引退させた。現在は歴史的な言語として位置づけられる。
problem_en: In the 1980s, the S statistical programming language, developed at Bell Labs, had become the de facto standard for statistical analysis and graphics, but there was demand for a commercially supported implementation outside Bell Labs. R. Douglas Martin, a professor of statistics at the University of Washington who had learned S while at Bell Labs, founded the Seattle startup Statistical Sciences, Inc. (later acquired by Insightful Corporation, and subsequently by TIBCO Software), through which S-PLUS — a commercial implementation of S — was developed and released in 1988. The goal was to turn S, originally a research language, into a commercial statistical-analysis package with support, documentation, and integration with external applications such as Excel, suitable for use in businesses and government agencies.
summary_en: S-PLUS offered object-oriented statistical-analysis features and packages such as FinMetrics for econometric time-series analysis, and it was a leading commercial statistical software package through the 1990s and 2000s. However, it gradually lost ground as the free, open-source S successor R grew in popularity, and TIBCO Software officially discontinued and retired S-PLUS on January 31, 2026. It is now regarded as a historical language.

name: SAIL
problem:
1960年代後半、スタンフォード大学人工知能研究所(Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)では、記号処理や連想的なデータ管理を必要とするAI研究のためのプログラミング環境が求められていた。Dan SwinehartとBob Sproullは、PDP-6/PDP-10用の整数専用ALGOL方言であったGOGOLコンパイラの資産と、連想記憶を扱う言語LEAPの機能を統合し、PDP-10・DECSYSTEM-20向けの大規模なALGOL 60風言語SAIL(Stanford Artificial Intelligence Language)を開発した。最初のリリースは1969年11月である。

目的は、従来のALGOL系言語が持つ手続き的な構造に加えて、三つ組(トリプル)による連想的なデータ格納、プロセス管理やコルーチン、バックトラッキング、文字列走査など、AI研究に必要な高度な機能を一つの言語に統合することだった。
summary: SAIL自体は現在使われていない歴史的な言語だが、1970年代後半には移植性を高めた派生言語MAINSAILが開発され、2005年時点でも限定的に使用されていたと報告されている。スタンフォード人工知能研究所における初期のAI研究基盤を支えた言語として記憶されている。
problem_en: In the late 1960s, the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory needed a programming environment for AI research that required symbolic processing and associative data management. Dan Swinehart and Bob Sproull combined the assets of the GOGOL compiler — an integer-only ALGOL dialect for the PDP-6/PDP-10 — with the associative-memory features of the LEAP language, to build SAIL (Stanford Artificial Intelligence Language), a large ALGOL 60-like language for the PDP-10 and DECSYSTEM-20. It was first released in November 1969. The goal was to integrate, into a single language, the procedural structure of ALGOL-family languages together with advanced facilities needed for AI research: associative data storage via triples, process management and coroutining, backtracking, and string scanning.
summary_en: SAIL itself is a historical language no longer in use, but a more portable derivative, MAINSAIL, was developed in the late 1970s and was reportedly still in limited use as of 2005. SAIL is remembered as a language that underpinned early AI research at the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.

name: SASL
problem:
1972年、セント・アンドルーズ大学のDavid Turnerは、Peter Landinが考案した関数型言語の理論的枠組みであるISWIMの適用的(値渡し)部分集合をもとに、SASL(St Andrews Static Language、後にSt Andrews Standard Languageとも呼ばれる)を設計した。当初は型を持たない厳密な(strict)評価の言語だったが、Turnerは1976年にこれを再設計・再実装し、非厳密(遅延)評価を行う言語へと変更した。

目的は、純粋関数型プログラミングの考え方を、実際に動く処理系として実験・検証できる、簡潔で数学的な言語を提供することだった。バロウズ社はSASLを用いてコンパイラやオペレーティングシステムを記述したと言われている。
summary: SASL自体は現在使われていない歴史的な言語だが、Turnerはこの遅延評価版SASLを土台として、その後KRC(Kent Recursive Calculator)、そして商用言語Miranda(1985年)を開発し、Mirandaはさらに後のHaskellの設計に直接影響を与えた。純粋関数型・遅延評価という現代の関数型言語の重要な系譜の出発点の一つとして位置づけられる。
problem_en: In 1972, David Turner at the University of St Andrews designed SASL (St Andrews Static Language, later also called St Andrews Standard Language), based on the applicative (call-by-value) subset of ISWIM, the theoretical functional-language framework devised by Peter Landin. It was initially an untyped, strictly-evaluated language, but Turner redesigned and reimplemented it in 1976 as a non-strict (lazy) language. The goal was to provide a concise, mathematically clean language in which the ideas of pure functional programming could be experimented with and validated as a working implementation. Burroughs Corporation is reported to have used SASL to write a compiler and an operating system.
summary_en: SASL itself is a historical language no longer in use, but Turner used this lazy-evaluation version of SASL as the foundation for his subsequent languages KRC (Kent Recursive Calculator) and then the commercial language Miranda (1985), which in turn directly influenced the design of Haskell. It stands as one of the starting points of an important lineage of modern functional languages built on purity and lazy evaluation.

name: Sawzall
problem:
2000年代初頭、Googleは検索ログなど莫大な量のログレコードを解析する必要に迫られていたが、こうした解析処理をMapReduceのフレームワーク上でC++やJavaによって直接記述すると、定型的なコードが多く冗長になりがちだった。Rob Pike、Sean Dorward、Robert Griesemer、Sean Quinlanらは、1件のログレコードを入力として受け取り、集計テーブルへの出力(emit)のみを行うという制約を課した手続き型のドメイン固有言語Sawzallを設計し、MapReduceのMapフェーズで実行されるスクリプトを簡潔に書けるようにした。

目的は、静的型付けでx86にコンパイルされる軽量な言語によって、ログ解析スクリプトの記述をC++やJavaで書くよりも大幅に速く、簡潔にすることだった。
summary: szlランタイムは2010年8月にApache License 2.0でオープンソース化されたが、MapReduce用の集計テーブル(テーブルアグリゲータ)部分は公開されなかった。Google社内では、Sawzallはその後Go言語をベースとしたLingo(logs in Go)にほとんどの用途で置き換えられており、現在は歴史的な言語として位置づけられる。
problem_en: In the early 2000s, Google needed to analyze enormous volumes of log records such as search logs, but writing such analysis directly in C++ or Java on top of the MapReduce framework tended to be verbose and boilerplate-heavy. Rob Pike, Sean Dorward, Robert Griesemer, and Sean Quinlan designed Sawzall, a procedural domain-specific language that takes a single log record as input and can only produce output by emitting values into aggregation tables, making it possible to write scripts run in the Map phase of MapReduce concisely. The goal was to make writing log-analysis scripts far faster and more concise than doing so in C++ or Java, using a lightweight, statically typed language that compiled to x86 machine code.
summary_en: The szl runtime was open-sourced under the Apache License 2.0 in August 2010, though the MapReduce aggregation-table component was not released. Within Google, Sawzall has since been replaced by Lingo (logs in Go), based on the Go language, for most purposes, and it is now regarded as a historical language.

name: SenseTalk
problem:
SenseTalkは1992年、NeXTSTEP向けのマルチメディア制作アプリケーションHyperSenseのスクリプト言語としてDouglas Simonsによって最初に作られた。HyperCardのHyperTalkから派生したxTalk系言語であり、2002年にEggplant Software社のテスト自動化製品Eggplant V1.0に組み込まれる際に大幅に再設計された。

目的は、プログラマではないテスターや業務担当者でも、英語の文章に近い自然な構文でGUIテスト自動化やマルチメディア制御のスクリプトを書けるようにすることだった。大文字小文字を区別しないキーワード、型を持たない(fluidな)変数、単位付き数値の直接サポート、正規表現を平易な英語風の構文で書ける「パターン言語」など、「人間中心のプログラミング(people-oriented programming)」を志向した設計が特徴である。
summary: SenseTalkは現在もKeysight Technologies社が保有するテスト自動化ツールEggplantの中核スクリプト言語として活発に開発が続けられており(2025年3月にバージョン2.23をリリース)、GUIテスト自動化の分野でnicheに実用されている。
problem_en: SenseTalk was first created in 1992 by Douglas Simons as the scripting language for HyperSense, a multimedia authoring application for NeXTSTEP. It is an xTalk-family language descended from HyperCard's HyperTalk, and it was substantially redesigned when it was built into Eggplant Software's test-automation product Eggplant V1.0 in 2002. The goal was to let testers and business users who are not programmers write GUI test-automation and multimedia-control scripts in a syntax that reads close to natural English sentences. Design features aimed at "people-oriented programming" include case-insensitive keywords, typeless ("fluid") variables, native support for numeric values with units, and a "Pattern Language" that lets regular expressions be written in plain, English-like syntax.
summary_en: SenseTalk remains under active development today as the core scripting language of Eggplant, a test-automation tool now owned by Keysight Technologies (version 2.23 was released in March 2025), and it is used in the niche field of GUI test automation.

name: SequenceL
problem:
SequenceLは1989年、テキサス工科大学でNASAの資金提供を受け、Daniel Cooke、Nelson Rushton、Brad Nemanichらによって開発が始められた。NASAが求めていたのは、要求仕様そのものが「自己検証可能」であるような仕様記述言語、つまり書かれた仕様をそのまま実行し、その結果を望ましい振る舞いと直接比較できるような言語だった。開発は20年以上にわたり継続され、後にTexas Multicore Technologies社によって商用のマルチコア対応コンパイラとして製品化された。

SequenceLの核となる「正規化-転置(normalize-transpose, NT)」という意味論は、スカラー値に対する演算をシーケンス(配列)の各要素に自動的に分配することで、プログラマが並列化を意識せずに書いたコードから、マルチコアCPUの処理能力を自動的に引き出すことを目指すものである。
summary: SequenceLは静的型付けかつ型推論を持つ純粋関数型・宣言型言語であり、マルチスレッドのC++やOpenCLコードへコンパイルされ、20以上の言語と連携可能である。バージョン3が2017年1月にリリースされ、コミュニティ版は無償で提供されているが、商用ライセンスの製品としてniche(専門分野向け)な用途で使われている。
